title: The top 100 retailers and Canada’s top 10 retailers
summary: This report from the Centre for the Study of Commercial Activity (CSCA) details the top 100 retail conglomerates in Canada for fiscal 2017, ranked by estimated annual retail sales. It highlights the significant concentration of retail buying power among a small number of large organizations, with the top three conglomerates accounting for 28% of total non-automotive retail sales. The article also discusses notable rank changes due to mergers, acquisitions, and performance shifts, and examines the market control dynamics between Canadian and U.S. retailers.

title: The Kroger Company: Report on Renewable Energy Goals
summary: Shareholders are requesting The Kroger Company to issue a report assessing the climate change risk reduction benefits of adopting quantitative, time-bound, enterprise-wide targets for increasing its renewable energy sourcing. The resolution highlights Kroger's lagging performance compared to competitors like Walmart, Target, and Costco in renewable energy adoption, despite the financial and reputational benefits. The report should discuss business risks from climate change, the potential of renewable energy to mitigate these risks, and options for increasing renewable energy adoption.

title: Dollar Tree planning $130M distribution center in Houston area
summary: Dollar Tree Inc. is planning to build a $130 million, 1.2 million-square-foot distribution center in Rosenberg, Texas, to serve both Dollar Tree and Family Dollar stores. This project is contingent on incentive agreements with local government. The article also lists several related recent distribution center developments in the Houston area.

title: Tilray to acquire hemp foodmaker Manitoba Harvest for up to $419M in U.S. expansion push
summary: Tilray is set to acquire Manitoba Harvest for up to $419 million in an effort to expand into the U.S. market, leveraging Manitoba Harvest's existing retail presence in stores like Walmart, Costco, and Whole Foods. This acquisition will allow Tilray to launch CBD-infused products where permissible, capitalizing on the increasing legalization and market growth of hemp-derived CBD products in the U.S. The deal aims to utilize Manitoba Harvest's manufacturing facilities and supply chain to reach approximately 16,000 stores across North America.

title: Target rips a page from Walmart, Amazon, welcoming outside sellers to website
summary: Target is launching Target+, an invite-only marketplace that will allow third-party sellers to offer a curated selection of products on its website, similar to Walmart and Amazon. This move aims to expand Target's online assortment while maintaining quality control by selectively inviting sellers. Shoppers using Target+ can still benefit from Red Card discounts, free shipping, and in-store returns for purchased items.

title: The Value Chain Constraint
summary: This article analyzes how companies like Amazon, Walmart, Google, and Microsoft succeed or struggle based on their integration within specific value chains, rather than solely on technological innovation. It argues that sustainable differentiation comes from effectively integrating different component pieces of a value chain, and that straying too far from this core integration can lead even large tech companies to struggle in new markets despite massive resources. The author uses examples like Amazon's grocery struggles, Google Cloud's challenges, and Microsoft's enterprise success to illustrate the concept, and Netflix's transformation as an exception that proves the rule.

title: Kona Coffee Farmers File Proposed Class Action Against Major Retailers Allegedly Passing Off Ordinary Coffee as Authentic
summary: Kona coffee farmers have filed a proposed class action lawsuit against major retailers and wholesalers, alleging they are deceptively labeling ordinary coffee as authentic Kona coffee. The lawsuit claims this practice artificially depresses prices for real Kona coffee and misleads consumers. Several settlements have already been reached with defendants, including Kroger, Safeway, Albertsons, Costco, and TJX, totaling millions of dollars and including agreements for clearer labeling of Kona coffee products.

title: The Buzz: Here's what Redding Costco project has to do with Grocery Outlet in Burney
summary: The same San Francisco attorney is representing residents who are challenging both the Costco relocation project in Redding and the development of a new Grocery Outlet in Burney, causing delays for both. The Burney Grocery Outlet project, approved by the Shasta County Planning Commission, faces an appeal based on concerns about environmental impact and traffic. Meanwhile, the Redding Costco project's environmental review is being recirculated due to an omitted health risk assessment, and Redding's second Grocery Outlet is set to open.

title: Costco builds 'fulfillment automation center' to expand e-commerce
summary: Costco has opened a "fulfillment automation center" to enhance its e-commerce capabilities, signaling increased investment in its online business. This move comes despite previous statements from its CFO expressing a preference for in-store shopping. The new center aims to support the company's expanding digital presence.

title: Costco Raises Minimum Wage to $15 an Hour
summary: Costco Wholesale is increasing its minimum wage for store workers to $15 an hour, marking the second such increase in less than a year. This announcement followed the company reporting higher than anticipated second-quarter financial earnings with significant increases in net sales and income. The move is part of a trend among retail giants like Target and Amazon to offer better wages and benefits to attract skilled workers.

title: Jury may hear claim that Costco managers ignored disability harassment
summary: A federal appeals court has ruled that a Costco employee's lawsuit alleging disability harassment can proceed to a jury trial, marking the first time the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals has allowed a hostile work environment claim under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). The employee, who has Tourette's syndrome and OCD, claims co-workers mocked him and managers were aware of or participated in the harassment. This ruling aligns the 2nd Circuit with other circuits in recognizing hostile work environment claims under the ADA.

title: Child Car Seats From Britax, Cosco, Graco, and Harmony Break in CR's Tests
summary: Consumer Reports found that five toddler-booster car seat models from Britax, Cosco, Graco, and Harmony had structural components break during crash testing with heavier child dummies, raising safety concerns. While all seats meet basic federal standards, CR's more rigorous tests revealed issues like harness support hardware breaking or top tether anchors failing. Consumer Reports advises parents not to stop using their current car seat if they don't have a replacement, as any car seat is better than none.

title: American Family Insurance to Acquire Ameriprise Auto & Home for $1 Billion
summary: American Family Insurance is acquiring Ameriprise Auto & Home (AAH) from Ameriprise Financial for $1.05 billion in cash, with net proceeds around $950 million. The acquisition will allow American Family to expand geographically, particularly in California where AAH has a significant presence, and will continue AAH's partnerships with Costco and Ameriprise Financial advisors. This sale aligns with Ameriprise Financial's strategy to focus on its core growth areas of advice and wealth management, and asset management.

title: Here's what Costco is doing with the old Sam's Club on Park Lane
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is opening its first Business Center in Texas, converting the former Sam's Club at 8282 Park Lane in Dallas. This new location, set to open in July, will primarily cater to business customers with specialized products and delivery options, though all Costco members can shop there. Costco is investing nearly $10 million to remodel and expand the 133,000-square-foot building.

title: Costco Increases Net Sales in April by 7.3%
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported a 7.3% year-over-year increase in net sales for April, reaching $11.60 billion, which caused shares to jump by 1.02% in after-hours trading. Comparable sales saw growth across various regions and e-commerce, indicating a positive trend and potential for third-quarter revenue to beat forecasts. The company also announced a 14% increase in its quarterly dividend payment to shareholders.

title: Snapshots of Optical’s 10 Largest U.S. Retail Players
summary: This article provides snapshots of the 10 largest U.S. optical retail players, detailing their performance, strategic initiatives, and key changes in 2018. It covers companies like Vision Source, Luxottica Retail, Walmart Inc., National Vision Holdings, and Costco Wholesale, highlighting their sales figures, store counts, and significant business developments. The report assesses their positions in the market and contributions to the optical industry.

title: How Costco uses $5 rotisserie chickens and free samples to turn customers into fanatics
summary: Costco cultivates immense customer loyalty through strategic design elements including exclusive memberships, extreme value (like $5 rotisserie chickens), and an engaging "treasure hunt" shopping experience. The company's low prices, unique store layout, free samples, and popular Kirkland Signature brand contribute to high customer retention and strong financial performance. Ultimately, Costco's business model focuses on providing high-quality products at low prices while making a fair return, leading to billions in revenue.

title: Treasure Hunt: Someone Bought a $400,000 Diamond Ring at Costco
summary: Costco's quarterly sales received a significant boost from an incredibly expensive purchase: a customer bought a diamond ring valued at around $400,000. This unusual transaction was announced by Costco's Chief Financial Officer Richard Galanti during a conference call with analysts.

title: Home Depot, Walmart Sued Over ‘Instant’ Tent Canopies
summary: Major retailers including Home Depot and Walmart are facing a patent infringement lawsuit over collasible "instant" tent canopies. Caravan Canopy Int’l Inc. filed the lawsuit, alleging infringement of U.S. Patent No. 5,944,040 by these companies for manufacturing, distributing, and selling such tents. The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.

title: Costco Sells $400,000 Diamond | JCK Magazine
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. recently sold a $400,000 diamond ring, which was highlighted by its CFO during a quarterly conference call. This high-value sale, alongside a $14,000 gold simulator, demonstrates the company's ability to cater to affluent shoppers despite being known for bulk purchases. Costco executives expressed amusement and surprise at the attention generated by the sale, recalling a similar event in 2012 when they listed a $2.3 million diamond.

title: Walmart CEO Calls for Raising the Federal Minimum Wage
summary: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon has called for Congress to raise the federal minimum wage, stating the current $7.25 is "too low" and that a thoughtful plan should be put in place. This marks the first time in over a decade a Walmart CEO has specifically demanded new legislation on the matter, despite the company having raised its own starting wage to $11 an hour. The announcement coincided with Senator Bernie Sanders campaigning at Walmart's annual meeting, advocating for a $15 an hour living wage for Walmart workers.

title: Costco to open long-awaited Cypress store in mid-July
summary: Costco is scheduled to open its new 148,000-square-foot store in Cypress, Texas, on July 20th, aiming to serve the fast-growing master-planned communities in northwest Harris County. This will be the ninth Costco in the Houston area and 33rd in Texas, offering about 4,000 brand-name and private-label products, along with various services. The company expects the store to employ 220 workers and contribute to its global operations, which reported $138.4 billion in revenue in fiscal 2018.

title: Target boosts worker benefits, including paid family leave
summary: Target Corp. announced a series of expanded benefits for its full- and part-time workers, including paid family leave and emergency child care, to attract and retain employees in a competitive labor market. The new policies include doubling paid leave to four weeks, extending subsidized backup care to all employees, and increasing adoption and surrogacy reimbursement to $10,000. These moves reflect a broader retail trend of enhancing wages and perks to address workforce challenges like turnover and absenteeism.

title: Watch Your Coins, Dollar Tree's Raising Prices
summary: Dollar Tree is testing higher prices with its "Dollar Tree Plus" collection due to increased tariffs on Chinese goods, which may impact its core demographic. Many retailers, including Dollar Tree, are expected to pass these increased costs onto consumers. Competitor Dollar General is expanding into health and beauty and food deserts to drive growth, a strategy Dollar Tree might consider as its shares are down 6.5% this year despite beating Q1 earnings expectations.

title: Costco will open outlet in Niagara Falls, Ontario
summary: Costco is set to open a new 150,000-square-foot store in Niagara Falls, Ontario, by fall 2020. This marks the retailing giant's expansion closer to the Buffalo Niagara region. The new store will anchor the renovated Niagara Square shopping center, located less than five miles from the Rainbow and Whirlpool bridges.

title: Walmart adds AI-powered cameras to more than 1,000 stores to reduce checkout theft
summary: Walmart is deploying AI-powered cameras in over 1,000 U.S. stores to combat checkout theft and shrinkage, which includes scanning errors and fraud. The "Missed Scan Detection" program has been in place for about two years and has reportedly led to a reduction in overall shrinkage, addressing issues like forgotten items or improperly scanned products. This initiative is part of Walmart's broader investment in security measures to improve customer experience and safety.

title: CubeSmart Self Storage Opens in Bayonne
summary: CubeSmart Self Storage has opened a 120,000-square-foot facility in Bayonne at 186 East 22nd Street, developed by Storage Deluxe. This opening contributes to Bayonne's growing commercial and retail development, following projects like Costco and QuickChek. The Bayonne location is Storage Deluxe's second self-storage facility in New Jersey, with Pure Properties brokering both deals.

title: Costco-anchored center in South Florida sells for $97M
summary: InvenTrust Properties Corp. has acquired Southern Palm Crossing, a Costco-anchored shopping center in Royal Palm Beach, for $97 million. The center includes many restaurant tenants. The transaction was reported in July 2019 by the South Florida Business Journal.

title: Costco’s Craig Wilson Becomes President of The Center for Food Integrity Board
summary: Craig Wilson, VP of quality assurance and food safety at Costco Wholesale Corp., has been elected president of The Center for Food Integrity (CFI) board of directors. This election took place at the board's July meeting in Kansas City, Mo., alongside other new officers and board members from various food and agriculture industries. The CFI board also approved a multiyear Strategic Direction plan to help the food industry build trust and address critical issues.

title: Weis Markets Adds Weis 2 Go Curbside Pickup and Home Delivery in More than 61 New Locations
summary: Weis Markets announced the expansion of its Weis 2 Go online ordering service, now offering pick-up and home delivery in 61 additional locations, bringing the total to 150 stores. This service provides a seamless shopping experience through mobile ordering, same-day pickup, and various payment options, including the use of Weis Preferred Shopper cards and acceptance of coupons. The company highlights the convenience of the service, including one-hour home delivery at participating stores and the option to waive the curbside pick-up fee for a limited time.

title: Everything Canadians need to know about the Capital One data breach
summary: The Capital One data breach affected about 100 million people in the United States and 6 million in Canada, with approximately one million Canadian Social Insurance Numbers compromised. The compromised data includes names, addresses, income, and some credit card customer data. Capital One will notify affected customers and offer free credit monitoring and identity theft insurance, advising them to monitor accounts for suspicious activity.

title: Another Costco may be set to open in Marin County
summary: Costco is considering opening a second location in Marin County, specifically in San Rafael. Pre-application documents have been submitted for a store, tire center, and gas station at the Northgate Mall, an initiative that aims to revitalize the mall into a "vibrant town center" and create local jobs. The new store would occupy the space previously held by Sears and Restoration Hardware, featuring a modern architectural design.

title: Kroger cuts food waste 9%, installs solar panels at Ralphs
summary: Kroger significantly reduced food waste by 9% last year through its Zero Hunger Zero Waste initiative and increased its landfill diversion rate by 13%. The company also surpassed its electric savings goal and reduced plastic resin in its private label line. Concurrently, Kroger subsidiary Ralphs installed a large solar panel system at its distribution center in Paramount, California, set to provide half of the facility's energy needs.

title: Costco Children's Golf Classic brings in record sum, country star brings down the house
summary: The Friends of Costco Guild's 20th annual Children’s Golf Classic achieved a record sum. The three-day event, starting August 17, included a VIP party, dinner with entertainment, and a golf tournament across nine local courses. The article highlights the success of this long-standing charity event.

title: Target launches new Good & Gather food brand Sunday
summary: Target is launching a new flagship food and beverage brand called Good & Gather, starting September 15th, across all its stores. The brand will feature over 2,000 products by the end of 2020, replacing Archer Farms and Simply Balanced, and reducing Market Pantry offerings. This initiative is part of Target's strategy to boost sales and enhance its store-owned brands to compete in the growing private label market.

title: Target, Like Walmart, Proves Main Engine of Economy Is Humming
summary: Despite recession fears, major discount retailers like Walmart and Target significantly beat Q2 sales expectations and raised full-year profit guidance, indicating a robust U.S. consumer economy. This performance, coupled with strong results from home improvement retailers, suggests a positive outlook for the upcoming holiday season. The retailers' success is attributed to strong fundamentals like price, assortment, and convenience, alongside strategic investments in online options and store remodels.

title: Lovesac plans to open showroom at St. Johns Town Center
summary: Lovesac, a direct-to-consumer specialty furniture brand, plans to open a 1,575-square-foot showroom at St. Johns Town Center in Jacksonville, Florida. The city is reviewing a permit application for a $175,000 tenant build-out. This new showroom will support Lovesac's e-commerce business model, complementing its existing presence at Costco in Jacksonville.

title: Costco spinoff concept could bring new life to Country Club Centre
summary: A Costco Business Center concept is being considered for the Country Club Centre in Arden-Arcade, potentially revitalizing the retail center after three anchor stores departed in 2018. This move signifies Costco Wholesale Corp.'s interest in expanding its spinoff concept for business customers in the Sacramento area.

title: Crowds force Costco to shut 1st China store early on opening day
summary: Costco's first store in China, located in Shanghai, was forced to close early on its opening day due to overwhelming crowds and resulting traffic jams. Videos showed thousands of people in the aisles, and local authorities advised residents to shop during off-peak hours for safety. This event occurred as other Western retailers have struggled to gain market share in China against strong local competition.

title: Amid Hour-Long Lines, Customers Fight Over Products as Costco Opens First Store in China
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp.'s first store in China experienced overwhelming demand on its opening day in Shanghai, leading to customer fights over products and hours-long waits. The frenzy caused the retailer to suspend operations temporarily due to heavy traffic, highlighting both the market's potential and the challenges faced by foreign retailers in China. This opening occurred amidst a U.S.-China tariff war and a history of global rivals struggling in the Chinese market.

title: Costco limits shoppers in first China store after opening-day fiasco
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp will limit the number of shoppers at its first China store in Shanghai after overcrowding forced an early closure on its opening day. No more than 2,000 shoppers will be allowed in at any given time, with local police assisting traffic flow. The move comes after viral images showed chaotic scenes of shoppers vying for products and enduring long queues.

title: Here’s how the stocks held by Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway have performed in 2019
summary: This article examines the performance of stocks held by Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway in 2019, highlighting top performers like Mastercard and Costco, and significant underperformers like Kraft Heinz. It delves into the challenges faced by Kraft Heinz, including changing consumer tastes, accounting issues, debt, and an SEC investigation, and mentions Buffett's regrets regarding his investment in the company.

title: Target's loyalty program is expanding nationwide in October with perks for all shoppers
summary: Target is expanding its free loyalty program, Target Circle, nationwide in October, offering personalized deals and opportunities to support local non-profits. Shoppers will earn 1% on purchases to redeem later, receive a birthday discount, and can vote to direct Target's charitable giving. Existing RedCard holders will continue to receive 5% off purchases and can utilize other Target Circle perks, while the Cartwheel savings tool will be integrated and rebranded as "Target Circle offers."

title: Lovesac's stock surges as it moves manufacturing out of China
summary: Lovesac's stock surged 23 percent after reporting a second-quarter loss that was less severe than anticipated, with sales increasing by 44.8 percent. The company is actively shifting its manufacturing out of China to mitigate tariffs, aiming to complete the move by the end of next year, primarily relocating to Vietnam. This strategic shift and strong revenue growth highlight Lovesac's efforts to expand its brand and multi-channel model.

title: Netflix vs Apple: Here's which stock would have made you richer if you invested $1,000 10 years ago
summary: This article compares the returns of a $1,000 investment made 10 years ago in Netflix versus Apple. Netflix significantly outperformed Apple, turning $1,000 into nearly $47,400 compared to Apple's $10,400. The article also discusses Apple TV+'s launch and its potential impact on Netflix, noting that while Netflix's past returns are impressive, its future growth depends on subscriber retention amidst new competition.

title: Costco buys Owatonna land for first Minnesota distribution center
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has purchased 150 acres in Owatonna, Minnesota, for $13 million. The big-box retailer plans to construct a 354,000-square-foot distribution center on the site, marking its first such facility in the state. This move indicates Costco's expansion of its logistics infrastructure in the region.

title: Tinder all set to release television series
summary: Dating app Tinder has wrapped filming on its first television series, as owner Match Group Inc seeks to dive deeper into creating original content. The multi-episode series centers on an "apocalyptic" storyline with a relationship subplot. This move is part of a larger strategy by Match Group to engage users on a deeper level, following similar content initiatives by other major tech and retail companies.

title: Owatonna picks up three big projects, including a Costco distribution center
summary: Owatonna, Minnesota, is experiencing significant industrial growth with three major projects underway on the west side of I-35. Costco Wholesale Corp. is building its first distribution center in Minnesota, while Daikin and Minimizer are also constructing new facilities. These developments are expected to create approximately 400 new jobs, capitalizing on Owatonna's strategic location near major highways.

title: 200-acre Synergy Tech Park development in Saratoga County attracting interest from Amazon, UPS and Costco
summary: A 200-acre Synergy Tech Park development in Saratoga County, New York, is drawing interest from major companies like Amazon, UPS, and Costco. The park, located in Clifton Park, is anchored by a new U-Haul regional storage center and is being developed by Mark Rekucki of M.J. Properties Inc. The project aims to create a significant warehouse park in the region.

title: U-Haul breaks ground on Synergy Tech Park site
summary: U-Haul has broken ground on its first facility within the new Synergy Tech Park in Clifton Park, N.Y., a project by MJ Properties. This 155,000-square-foot facility is a significant step for the 200-acre tech park, which represents an $18.2 million investment by MJ Properties to attract corporate, commercial, and light industrial users. The site will offer a full-line moving and storage center with 900 climate-controlled storage rooms.

title: Costco’s first China warehouse has 200,000 members, blowing past the 68,000 average
summary: Costco's first warehouse in China, located in Shanghai, has garnered over 200,000 members, significantly exceeding the average membership numbers. This strong performance was highlighted by Costco's Chief Financial Officer Richard Galanti during the company's fourth-quarter earnings call. The article also notes that Costco sold a $220,000 diamond in the fourth quarter, indicating strong sales in other areas.

title: Walmart will subsidize vendors, in first shots of holiday price war with Amazon
summary: Walmart is launching a "Competitive Price Adjustment program" to subsidize third-party sellers on its marketplace, lowering prices for consumers while ensuring vendors receive their original listed amount. This move is a direct response to Amazon's similar programs and intensifying competition for online shoppers, particularly ahead of the holiday season. The strategy aims to attract shoppers with deep discounts, mirroring Amazon's past tactics and current practices under FTC scrutiny.

title: Investing in Smart Water Technology with Xylem
summary: This article discusses the growing importance of smart water technology, driven by increasing water scarcity. It highlights Xylem (XYL), a publicly traded company that is aggressively expanding its footprint in smart water solutions through acquisitions, positioning itself as a leader in digitizing the water economy. The piece also touches on investment strategies like Dividend Growth Investing and showcases smart water technology startups.

title: Adaptable couch & chair furniture store comes to Boise mall
summary: Lovesac, the national furniture company specializing in reconfigurable couches and foam-filled chairs, is opening a new store at Boise Towne Square next to the Apple Store. This marks Lovesac's second attempt at a Boise Towne Square location, having previously operated on the upper level. The company, known for its Sactionals and Lovesacs, plans to open approximately 20 new stores annually following a successful IPO.

title: How a Houston-area county landed a national retailer's 2M-square-foot, 1,300-job distribution center
summary: Ross Stores Inc. has selected Waller County in the Houston area for a new 2 million-square-foot distribution facility. This development is projected to create 1,300 full-time jobs, marking a significant economic boost for the region. The article details the successful move to attract this national retailer.

title: Target unveils Black Friday 2019 ad with deals on televisions, toys, gift cards and more
summary: Target has released its Black Friday 2019 ad, featuring deals on electronics, toys, and gift cards, and will kick off its "HoliDeals" season with a two-day Black Friday preview sale starting November 8th. The retailer plans to offer four times more early deals this year, including discounts on Target digital gift cards, and will reintroduce its Black Friday shopping incentive of a 20% off coupon for future purchases. Target is also investing nearly $50 million more in payroll for guest services during the holiday season.

title: Kroger launches auto buying program with TrueCar
summary: Kroger has partnered with TrueCar to launch the Kroger Auto Buying Program, offering customers access to pricing information, guaranteed savings on new cars, and discounts on used cars. This initiative is part of Kroger's strategy to provide more services and perks to its customers, mirroring efforts by competitors like Costco and Amazon, and contributes to its alternative profit portfolio which is projected to generate significant operating profit. The program is available to customers of several Kroger-owned grocery chains and aims to provide a more transparent car-buying experience.

title: Target shoppers can tap the app and get groceries dropped on their porch the same day
summary: Target now offers same-day delivery through its app, allowing customers to order groceries and other items for a $9.99 fee, waived for purchases over $75 from Nov. 17-26. Shipt members receive free delivery, and new users can try a four-week free trial. This move positions Target competitively alongside other retailers like Walmart and Amazon, which also offer various same-day delivery options.

title: Why Costco Is Thriving Even as the U.S.-China Trade War Drags On
summary: Costco is successfully navigating the U.S.-China trade war despite tariffs that are impacting other retailers. The company benefits from its high sales volumes, fast inventory turnover, and a business model that relies on membership fees for a significant portion of its operating earnings, providing stability in a volatile retail sector. Costco's scale grants leverage with vendors, and its strategic expansion and focused inventory management allow it to maintain low prices and strong sales growth, outpacing competitors and the broader retail market.

title: Top Women in Health, Wellness and Beauty — Retailers
summary: This article recognizes leading women in the health, wellness, and beauty retail sectors. The women are honored across three categories: Business Excellence, Commitment to Care, and Rising Stars, acknowledging their significant contributions to their respective companies and the industry. Their roles span merchandising, pharmacy operations, marketing, strategy, and clinical services at major retailers.

title: Delta Gift Cards 10% Off
summary: Delta Air Lines gift cards are available at a 10% discount at Costco, both online and in-store. These gift cards can be used for air transportation on Delta marketed flights, with up to three usable per transaction, but cannot be used for upgrades, baggage fees, or in-flight purchases. This sale presents a good opportunity for frequent Delta flyers to save on tickets.

title: It’s hard for shoppers to avoid Amazon — even in their investments
summary: This article discusses the pervasive presence of Amazon, not just in consumer shopping habits but also increasingly within investment portfolios. It raises the question of whether to invest in the consumer discretionary sector, linking the decision to beliefs about a potential economic downturn. The core message emphasizes the importance of understanding what one is investing in.

title: Georgetown approves incentives for Costco store
summary: Georgetown leaders have approved incentives for a new Costco store, hoping it will attract shoppers from surrounding cities like Temple, Killeen, Fort Hood, and Waco. The arrival of the big box store is expected to boost the local economy, but also raises concerns about its potential impact on small businesses in the area.

title: Costco receives final approval to build in Midland
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has received final city approval to build a new 157,000-square-foot store in Midland, Michigan. The Midland City Council approved the site plans, which include an attached tire facility and an eight-pump fuel station at 4816 Bay City Road. This marks the completion of the city's site plan review process, although Costco's construction timeline remains unknown.

title: Your complete guide to investing with a conscience, a $30 trillion market just getting started
summary: ESG investing, which considers environmental, social, and governance factors, grew to over $30 trillion in 2018 and is projected to reach $50 trillion in the next two decades. Once considered niche and potentially detrimental to returns, ESG strategies have proven to be market-beating and are gaining significant momentum as investors demand greater transparency and companies face consequences for not adapting. The article explores various ESG strategies, highlighting their growing popularity, market performance, and the factors driving this surge, particularly among younger generations and institutions.

title: Costco Enters New Market in Georgia
summary: Costco is expanding its domestic growth by opening its first location in Dallas, Georgia. The new 135,000-square-foot store will include a massive parking lot and potentially a gas station. Paulding County officials have issued a $17.6 million building permit, and the land purchase was finalized in December 2019.

title: Target was strong where it needed strength, and that bodes well for the rest of the year
summary: Target's 2019 holiday sales missed expectations, causing a stock selloff, primarily due to weakness in electronics, toys, and home goods. Despite the overall miss, the company showed strength in key investment areas like apparel, beauty, and food, which analysts believe bodes well for its long-term strategy and profitability. CEO Brian Cornell expressed confidence, maintaining the retailer's earnings outlook due to strong gross margin mix and effective digital fulfillment.

title: Hot dogs, chickens, pumpkin pies and other revelations from the Costco shareholders meeting
summary: During their annual shareholder meeting, Costco CEO Craig Jelinek discussed the state of the company, highlighting popular items such as hot dogs, chickens, and pumpkin pies. The meeting provided insights into the company's operations and key consumer products.

title: The Daily Deal Sales Tax Trap
summary: This article highlights the complexities and potential liabilities merchants and their accountants face in collecting sales tax on daily deal vouchers, especially when additional, undisclosed discounts are offered by the daily deal business. It discusses varying state regulations, the nuances of voucher classification, and potential penalties for non-compliance, emphasizing the need for greater transparency among all parties involved.

title: How to redeem Costco credit card rewards
summary: This article explains the unique rewards program for the Costco Anywhere Visa Card by Citi, detailing how cardholders earn and redeem rewards. Unlike typical rewards cards, redemption for Costco credit card rewards occurs annually in February via a certificate, which can only be used for merchandise or cash at a U.S. Costco warehouse. The article covers the tiered cash back structure for various purchases and provides a comprehensive FAQ about the reward certificates.

title: JFE Franchising Partners with Weis Markets as Their Fresh Sushi Program Provider
summary: JFE Franchising has partnered with Weis Markets to become their fresh sushi program provider, converting 114 Weis Markets locations in the Northeast. This partnership expands Snowfox retail sushi kiosks to over 900 total locations in the US, marking a significant milestone for Snowfox's presence in the Northeast. Retail fresh sushi is a rapidly growing category capable of representing a substantial portion of store sales.

title: Costco to close store at Phoenix mall
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. will be closing its store at Christown mall in Phoenix later in 2020. The company did not renew its lease for the Phoenix mall location.

title: If you invested $1,000 in American Express 10 years ago, here's how much you'd have now
summary: If you invested $1,000 in American Express a decade ago, it would have grown to over $4,000, representing a 301% total return, outperforming the S&P 500. The article details American Express's history, its stock performance including challenges like the 2008 recession and the Costco contract loss, and its recent successes driven by fee-based products and millennial engagement.

title: Hoarding Toilet Paper Over Coronavirus? Officials Say Be Prepared, Don't Hoard
summary: Amid reports of consumers buying large quantities of emergency supplies due to coronavirus concerns, Los Angeles health officials advise residents to be prepared for a few days, but not to hoard. They emphasized that while an emergency preparedness kit with a few days' worth of supplies is prudent, long-term hoarding is unnecessary and is contributing to supply chain issues. The article also mentions the potential for price gouging prosecution during the declared state of emergency.

title: Costco sales surge 11% as coronavirus fear prompts stockpiling
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported an 11% surge in sales due to customer stockpiling of essentials amid coronavirus fears, forcing frequent replenishment of items. The company also exceeded holiday-quarter expectations with a 28% increase in e-commerce sales and strong membership revenue, while acknowledging the continued rise in traffic into March. Analyst Garrett Nelson of CFRA Research considers Costco a primary beneficiary of coronavirus-related consumer stockpiling.

title: Target joins Kroger in limiting purchases of virus-related items
summary: Target Corp. has joined Kroger Co. in limiting purchases of high-demand virus-related items like hand sanitizer and disinfecting wipes to six per person due to widespread stockpiling caused by the novel coronavirus outbreak. This move follows similar restrictions by Kroger and other grocers to manage a buying frenzy that has disrupted retail supply chains. Target's CEO noted "aggressive shopping" but stated the virus hasn't yet altered their full-year outlook, though analysts remain concerned about its potential impact on U.S. consumer spending.

title: Costco supply chain struggles to keep up with demand amid COVID-19 preparations
summary: Costco's supply chain faced significant challenges keeping up with surging demand as members stocked up on supplies in preparation for COVID-19. Empty shelves were observed in stores, including bread sections, as customers rushed to purchase goods. This article highlights the immediate impact of coronavirus fears on consumer buying habits and retailer operations.

title: Costco tells office workers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is requiring its head office employees in Issaquah to report to work, despite public health requests to allow remote work. CEO W. Craig Jelinek stated that this decision is based on equity and fairness, as the majority of Costco employees work in stores and warehouses and do not have the option to work from home. This contrasts with companies like Amazon and Microsoft, which have allowed many office workers to work remotely amid coronavirus concerns.

title: Weis Markets stores announce modified hours due to coronavirus
summary: Weis Markets announced modified store hours due to the coronavirus pandemic, effective Tuesday, March 17, 2020. Stores will now be open daily from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. This change allows time for staff to restock shelves and sanitize stores, ensuring customer and associate safety during the COVID-19 outbreak.

title: Costco buys logistics firm Innovel for $1 billion
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp announced the acquisition of Innovel Solutions for $1 billion to enhance its final-mile delivery of bulky products across the U.S. and Puerto Rico. Innovel, previously owned by Sears-operator Transform Holdco LLC, will continue serving Sears and its existing third-party customers. This move is part of Costco's strategy to boost online sales of large items like appliances and furniture, with Costco's shares rising 3.5% after the news.

title: Costco buys final-mile delivery firm for $1 billion
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has acquired Innovel Solutions, a third-party logistics provider specializing in "final mile" delivery for big and bulky products, for $1 billion. This acquisition will enhance Costco's e-commerce last-mile delivery capabilities and allow for faster growth in sales of large items. Innovel will continue to serve its existing customers, including Sears and other third parties.

title: Kroger hiring 10,000 new employees, offering paid time off for workers with COVID-19
summary: Kroger is hiring an additional 10,000 employees for its stores, manufacturing plants, and distribution centers due to increased demand during the coronavirus outbreak. The company will also provide 14 days of paid time off for any full-time or part-time employees who are forced to quarantine or are diagnosed with COVID-19. Kroger emphasizes its competitive hourly wage and benefits package.

title: Coconut water is the pandemic’s newest shortage
summary: Amid coronavirus concerns, sales of coconut water, particularly from Vita Coco, have surged significantly across the U.S., depleting typical stockpiles and straining supply chains. While other bottled waters are also in high demand, this trend raises concerns about potential supply disruptions if borders close, especially since coconuts are not grown in the US.

title: Spend $250, get an ounce of caviar: Restaurant suppliers get creative to survive
summary: Restaurant suppliers are pivoting their business models due to the coronavirus pandemic, with major distributors like Sysco and US Foods redirecting efforts to supply grocery stores. Smaller, niche suppliers are turning to e-commerce and direct-to-consumer sales to offload inventory and stay afloat. These changes reflect a significant shift in the food supply chain as restaurants grapple with closures and reduced business.

title: Costco, Home Depot limiting number of customers in store
summary: Costco and Home Depot are implementing new policies to limit the number of customers in their stores to help prevent the spread of the coronavirus. Costco will allow only two people per membership card, adjust closing times, and change gas station operating hours. Home Depot will also limit customer numbers, eliminate major spring promotions, adjust closing times for cleaning, and provide thermometers to associates for health checks.

title: DoorDash Starts Delivering Toilet Paper and Other Groceries
summary: DoorDash, the largest food delivery app in the U.S., is expanding its services to include deliveries from convenience stores like 7-Eleven and Wawa. This accelerated rollout, prompted by the coronavirus pandemic, allows customers to order essential goods such as toilet paper and other packaged items. The company currently has over 1,800 convenience stores listed on its app across the U.S.

title: Costco, Home Depot to limit number of shoppers in stores
summary: Major retailers Costco Wholesale Corp. and Home Depot are implementing new policies to limit the number of shoppers in their stores to promote social distancing. Costco will allow no more than two people per membership card and has special hours for seniors, while Home Depot will close earlier for cleaning and restocking, and is eliminating major spring promotions to reduce store traffic. Both companies are also prioritizing essential supply shipments and donating personal protective equipment.

title: Infographic: Retailers’ cage-free egg pledges
summary: U.S. egg producers are converting to cage-free systems as North American retailers commit to sourcing only cage-free eggs. While some retailers already exclusively sell cage-free eggs, many others, including major grocery chains, are still in transition, with most aiming for completion by 2025 or 2026. This shift is also driven by new laws in several U.S. states requiring cage-free egg production and sales.

title: Costco sales jumped by more than $1.5 billion as coronavirus spread in March
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported a significant increase in sales for March, with net sales rising by nearly 12% to $15.49 billion, compared to $13.87 billion in March 2019. This surge, including a 48% jump in online sales, reflects consumer stockpiling as the coronavirus pandemic led to widespread lockdowns. The report covers the five-week period from March 2nd to March 6th.

title: PriceSmart Sees Sales Surge Almost 20% In March, Postpones New Bogotá & Bucaramanga Stores, To Launch Online Shopping & Delivery Option
summary: PriceSmart (NASDAQ: PSMT) announced a 17.1% increase in net merchandise sales for March 2020, reaching $306.1 million, driven by members stocking up on essentials. However, sales moderated in the latter half of March due to government mandates and consumer concerns regarding the pandemic. In response, PriceSmart is launching online ordering and delivery options, postponing new store openings in Costa Rica, Bogotá, Bucaramanga, and Jamaica, and implementing cost-saving measures to address the expected adverse impact on traffic and sales.

title: Costco set to open new store in China's Suzhou city
summary: U.S. retail giant Costco will open a new store in Suzhou, China, marking its third store in the country and the first outside Shanghai. The company's subsidiary purchased land for over 142.5 million yuan ($20.2 million) to build a warehouse store of more than 50,000 square meters. This expansion highlights Costco's strategy to strengthen its presence in China, capitalizing on the growing middle class's demand for quality and value.

title: Ebay Names Jamie Iannone Chief Executive Officer
summary: Ebay Inc. announced the appointment of Jamie Iannone as its new chief executive officer, effective April 27, 2020. Iannone, previously COO of Walmart eCommerce, brings over 20 years of experience in digital and omnichannel platforms and has been elected to Ebay's Board of Directors. The Board expressed confidence in Iannone's proven track record of innovation and leadership to guide Ebay's future growth.

title: Spinner P’15 Offers Insight on Food Supply Chain Amid Coronavirus Pandemic
summary: Steven Spinner P’15, chairman/CEO of United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI), discusses the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on the food supply chain. He reassures consumers about food availability despite chaotic purchasing habits and logistical challenges, highlighting adaptations made by producers and a predicted long-term shift towards e-commerce and touchless procurement in grocery shopping.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights: Sprouts Farmers Market, Best Buy, Kroger, Walmart and Costco Wholesale
summary: This article from Zacks Analyst Blog highlights five retailers—Sprouts Farmers Market, Best Buy, Kroger, Walmart, and Costco Wholesale—that are offering curbside pickup services to mitigate risks during the COVID-19 lockdown. The blog details how curbside pickup works, its benefits in reducing infection risks, and provides individual company analyses including expected earnings growth rates and Zacks Ranks. It emphasizes the convenience and safety of this option for consumers amidst social distancing measures.

title: Smithfield Foods Is Blaming “Living Circumstances In Certain Cultures” For One Of America’s Largest COVID-19 Clusters
summary: Smithfield Foods faced one of America's largest COVID-19 outbreaks at its South Dakota pork plant, with a spokesperson attributing the spread to "living circumstances in certain cultures" among its largely immigrant workforce. However, a BuzzFeed News investigation revealed that the company made significant missteps in informing and protecting employees in the crucial weeks after the first case emerged, including uneven safety protocols and delayed closures. The outbreak led to the indefinite closure of the plant, impacting 5% of the national pork supply and causing severe repercussions for workers and the supply chain.

title: Del Monte Fresh Produce Details Brick-and-Mortar Retail Strategies
summary: Del Monte Fresh Produce is offering tips to consumers on how to store and maximize the shelf life of fresh produce during stay-at-home orders, aiming to ensure continued access and reduce food waste. The company highlights specific storage advice for various fruits and vegetables, along with suggestions for meal prep and "root to stem" cooking. These strategies are designed to help families make fresh items last longer between supermarket trips.

title: Former Costco Employee Says She Was Forced Out Over Workplace Claim
summary: A former Costco Wholesale Corp. employee is suing the company, alleging she was forced to resign in 2019 after being wrongfully denied available jobs following an on-the-job injury. Monica Barnett's lawsuit accuses Costco of wrongful termination, retaliation, and discrimination, claiming the company failed to accommodate her work restrictions and tried to force her out after she filed a workers' compensation claim. She seeks unspecified damages in the Los Angeles Superior Court lawsuit.

title: Costco Files Application to Put Store in West Little Rock
summary: Costco (Nasdaq: COST) has filed an application with the city of Little Rock to open a 165,000-SF warehouse store on Chenal Parkway, which would be its first location in Arkansas. The proposed development includes a tire center, optical exam center, liquor sales, and a detached gas station, creating 200-250 jobs. This move is seen as a significant validation of the Little Rock market's growth potential.

title: Kroger, Albertsons Limiting Some Meat Purchases
summary: Kroger and Albertsons have begun placing limits on some meat purchases in select stores, a move also adopted by Stop & Shop, to prevent panic buying and ensure availability amid increased demand. This follows warnings from Smithfield Foods CEO Kenneth M Sullivan about potential meat supply shortages due to COVID-19 related plant shutdowns and increased consumer demand for at-home meal preparation. Sales of meat spiked significantly in March, with ground beef, chicken breasts, and pork loin seeing the largest dollar increases.

title: Costco limits meat purchases as supply shortages loom
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp has announced limits on the purchase of beef, pork, and poultry products. This decision comes as grocery stores anticipate significant meat supply shortages due to disruptions caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market Reports Pandemic Revenue Gains
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market Inc. reported a 16% year-over-year gain in net sales and a 10.6% boost in comparable-store sales for Q1 2020, largely driven by increased consumer demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's net income rose to $92 million, a 64% increase, despite higher expenses due to increased worker pay, bonuses, and e-commerce fees. Sprouts' CFO noted uncertainty regarding future consumer behavior and market visibility for the remainder of 2020.

title: Are You Paying Extra for Eggs? Lawsuits Accuse Producers of Price Gouging (Published 2020)
summary: Amid the coronavirus pandemic, the price of eggs surged, leading to separate lawsuits in California and Texas. These lawsuits accuse the largest U.S. egg producer, along with supermarkets and wholesalers, of price gouging and making excessive, illegal profits. The sudden increase in demand for eggs due to more home cooking is cited as the reason for the price hike.

title: Costco says stay-at-home orders, lower gas prices hurt monthly results
summary: Despite images of long lines, Costco reported a 1.8% decline in April sales to $11.39 billion and a 3.3% drop in U.S. same-store sales. The company attributed these negative results to stay-at-home orders, lower gas prices, and declines in categories like hearing aids and travel, though e-commerce saw a boost.

title: Grocery Dive: Kroger and Wegmans Expand Mobile Self-Checkout Apps
summary: During the Covid-19 pandemic, grocery stores like Kroger and Wegmans are expanding their mobile self-checkout apps to meet increased demand for contactless shopping, contributing to significant sales surges. This trend is driven by both convenience and the necessity of social distancing practices, with companies like Sam's Club also seeing a massive increase in app usage. The article suggests that mobile self-checkout will remain popular even after the pandemic due to its efficiency.

title: Kroger announces new bonuses after cutting hazard pay
summary: Kroger announced new "thank you" bonuses for its workers just days after ending hazard "hero" pay, following an outcry from the United Food and Commercial Workers International union. Full-time workers will receive $400 and part-time workers $200, paid in two installments, totaling an estimated $130 million from Kroger. The union, however, pledged to continue pressuring the company for ongoing bonus pay as the pandemic continues.

title: Kroger employees scared that company isn't doing enough to keep them safe
summary: Kroger employees express fear about returning to work due to the company's policy on masks for shoppers, exposing front-line workers to COVID-19. Despite the risks, Kroger ended "hero pay" and stated its employee infection rates are lower than the general public. Other retailers like Costco have mandated masks for all, highlighting differing approaches to worker safety during the pandemic.

title: Apollo Global invests $1.75 billion in U.S. supermarket operator Albertsons
summary: Apollo Global Management has invested $1.75 billion in Albertsons Companies Inc., a move that signals confidence in the debt-laden U.S. supermarket operator whose performance has improved due to the coronavirus pandemic. The investment, representing a 17.5% stake through convertible preferred shares, values Albertsons at around $10 billion (excluding debt) and provides the company with more time and a valuation floor for its planned IPO.

title: Fact Check: Are empty meat shelves at Walmart an anti-Trump conspiracy?
summary: This article fact-checks a viral social media claim that empty meat shelves at Walmart are part of an anti-Trump conspiracy orchestrated by the Walton family. It investigates the ownership of Walmart, the political donations of Walton family members and executives, and the genuine reasons for meat shortages. The article concludes that the claim is false, attributing the shortages to COVID-19 related disruptions in meat processing plants, not political motives.

title: Costco reopening food courts, reviving samples to lure back shoppers
summary: Costco is reopening nearly all of its food courts by mid-June and plans to reintroduce a "slow rollout" of free food samples to attract shoppers back to its warehouses. This move comes as the company seeks to boost in-store traffic, which was down 2% in the last quarter, and as its profits were negatively impacted by COVID-19 related costs despite a rise in revenue.

title: Costco plans to bring back free samples next month
summary: Costco is planning to bring back free samples in mid-June after stopping them in March due to coronavirus concerns. While the samples will return, the method of distribution will change from the old way where members could pluck them from a tray, and it's unclear how shoppers will eat them given the mask requirement.

title: Should You Buy or Sell Costco Stock?
summary: This article analyzes whether Costco stock (COST) is a good investment, weighing its strong performance during the pandemic and formidable business model against its high valuation and low dividend yield. It discusses Costco's growth in sales and membership, its "economic moats," and challenges such as rising costs and the need to scale up e-commerce operations. The article concludes that Costco is a wonderful company, despite its high price.

title: Costco Is Reopening All of Its Food Courts and Bringing Back Beloved Samples
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is reopening its food courts and bringing back customer-favorite food samples after altering operations due to the coronavirus pandemic. CFO Richard Galanti announced that almost all food courts are expected to be operational by mid-June, though menus will remain limited. Food sample availability will also resume in mid-June with a slow roll-out and altered experience.

title: Inside Costco’s new, $450 million chicken operation
summary: Lincoln Premium Poultry's $450 million poultry processing operation, established to exclusively supply Costco, is now sending products to market and aims to supply all Costco locations in the western U.S. The facility represents a new model for the poultry supply chain, giving Costco influence over bird raising, processing, and employment practices, while also boosting the local economy. It utilizes advanced technology for bird welfare and efficiency, including air chilling and automated deboning, and works with approximately 80 independent growers.

title: Costco should be Warren Buffett's next bulk purchase
summary: The article suggests Costco Wholesale Corp. as a prime acquisition target for Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc., citing Costco's strong brand, predictable cash flow from memberships, and consistent sales growth. Despite the current high valuation, Costco aligns with Buffett's investment philosophy, and its market capitalization matches Berkshire's cash reserves, making it a feasible "bulk purchase" given Buffett's past interest in large deals.

title: Top 5 Reasons A Win-Win Relationship With China Benefits The US Economy
summary: This article highlights five reasons why a cooperative relationship between the US and China is beneficial for the US economy, especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and trade tensions. It emphasizes mutual support during the pandemic, the importance of China's consumer market for US companies, the support for US jobs through trade, the negative impact of trade wars on US stocks, and the opportunity for US investors in China's economic recovery. The piece advocates for strengthening the win-win aspects of the relationship.

title: The Billowing Business of Sadler’s Smokehouse
summary: This article details the journey of Sadler's Smokehouse, from a small East Texas drive-in in 1948 to a major processing facility acquired by Hormel Foods Corp. for $270 million in 2020. It highlights Sadler's commitment to traditional slow-smoking techniques and its success in bringing authentic barbecue to both foodservice and retail markets. The acquisition by Hormel Foods is presented as an opportunity to expand Sandler's reach while preserving its legacy.

title: The billowing business of Sadler's Smokehouse
summary: Sadler's Smokehouse, which started as a drive-in in 1948, grew into a major producer of slow-smoked meats, serving both foodservice and retail giants. Hormel Foods Corp. acquired Sadler's for $270 million in February, recognizing its highly differentiated brand and potential for expansion into retail and deli channels. The company attributes its success to a commitment to traditional slow-smoking techniques, selecting quality hardwoods, and dedicated pitmasters.

title: Target CEO Discusses How Protests and the COVID-19 Pandemic Are Changing Retail
summary: Target CEO Brian Cornell discusses how the COVID-19 pandemic and Black Lives Matter protests have fundamentally altered the retail landscape. He highlights Target's initiatives to address racial injustice, including a $10 million donation and an internal task force. The article also notes Target's success due to prior digital investments, which led to significant online sales growth and a shift towards permanent changes in shopping behavior.

title: Costco to reduce coronavirus senior shopping hours
summary: Costco announced it will reduce its special shopping hours for seniors and vulnerable customers starting July 13. The temporary measure, initially expanded to Monday through Friday from 9 to 10 a.m., will be scaled back to just Tuesdays and Thursdays during the same time slot. This change comes as the country moves towards reopening, with Costco maintaining face cover requirements for shoppers during these dedicated hours.

title: Here Are the Top 100 U.S. Retailers Ranked by Sales
summary: The National Retail Federation released its annual Top 100 Retailers report, ranking companies by sales from their most recent fiscal year. Walmart, Amazon, Kroger, Costco, and Walgreens lead the list, all operating with omnichannel strategies. Notably, only one pure-play jewelry retailer, Signet Jewelry, made the cut at number 98, though several others on the list also sell fine jewelry.

title: Costco to keep coronavirus senior hours indefinitely after planning to reduce them
summary: Costco has reversed its decision to reduce special operating hours for seniors and immunocompromised shoppers, opting to keep them at five days a week due to a surge in coronavirus cases. Eligible members aged 60 or older, disabled individuals, or those with underlying health conditions can shop from 9 to 10 a.m., Monday through Friday. Face coverings are required for all members, with exceptions for medical conditions or children under two.

title: Costco reports another surge in sales for June
summary: Costco experienced an 11% increase in June sales, mirroring a similar surge in March, driven by the Covid-19 pandemic. This comes as the company has seen "off the charts" sales due to the coronavirus outbreak and recently made a $1 billion acquisition to improve "last mile" delivery.

title: Kroger will require all shoppers to wear masks beginning July 22
summary: Kroger announced that it will require all shoppers to wear face masks in its stores starting July 22, joining other major retailers like Walmart in implementing such policies. This decision aims to protect employees and customers and follows CDC recommendations to reduce the spread of COVID-19. While Kroger did not detail enforcement, it recommended e-commerce services for those unable or unwilling to wear masks.

title: BJ's Wholesale Club opening 2 stores
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club announced plans to open two new locations in Long Island City and Newburgh, New York, in early 2021. This expansion is expected to create 300 jobs and offer members significant savings on groceries and other household essentials. The new clubs will feature an expanded fresh food section and one will include a BJ's Gas station.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club Could Come to Wayne’s Willowbrook Mall
summary: A BJ’s Wholesale Club store, including a gas station, is proposed for the Willowbrook Mall in Wayne, New Jersey, specifically in a vacant part of the old Sears site. The 105,031-square-foot store plan, submitted by Seritage SRC Finance, LLC, is on the agenda for the Passaic County Planning Board's virtual meeting on July 30. This potential new location would introduce significant competition to the existing Costco across the street.

title: Walmart Business Model
summary: This article details Walmart's business model, highlighting its strategy of leading on price, differentiating on access, competing on assortment, and delivering a great customer experience. It covers Walmart's operations, history, ownership, mission statement, revenue streams (products and services), and competitive landscape. The article also provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of the company.

title: Combine the Corsair Void RGB Elite headset and the ST100 RGB stand together for $140
summary: Costco is offering a bundle deal on the Corsair Void RGB Elite wireless headset and the Corsair ST100 RGB Premium stand for $139.99, saving buyers about $30 compared to purchasing them separately. The headset features high-quality audio with 7.1 surround sound and comfortable memory foam earpads, while the stand provides RGB lighting, a 3.5mm audio input, and two USB 3.1 inputs. Both devices can be customized using Corsair's iCue software.

title: Polar Beverages goes nationwide in blockbuster deal with Keurig Dr Pepper
summary: Polar Beverages has entered a long-term franchise agreement with Keurig Dr Pepper to expand its seltzer distribution nationwide, leveraging Keurig's direct-to-stores delivery and manufacturing networks. This deal allows Polar to maintain ownership while gaining national reach for its quirky-flavored seltzers, aiming to elevate its market position from third nationally in the nearly $2 billion sparkling water category. The partnership builds on an existing 30-year relationship where Polar distributed KDP brands, and now KDP will manufacture and distribute Polar seltzers in new territories, sharing marketing costs.

title: How is Tractor Supply acing the pandemic?
summary: Tractor Supply Company reported strong second-quarter sales and plans to open new stores, attributing its success during the pandemic to long-term innovation, an understanding of physical stores as assets, and a customer-centric "customer as the channel" approach. The retailer emphasized key initiatives like an improved e-commerce platform, enhanced mobile shopping, and expanded delivery options, which allowed it to swiftly implement curbside pickup and ship-from-store services. Tractor Supply's success is presented as a case study for other retailers, highlighting the importance of customer segment clarity, integrated customer journeys beyond distinct channels, and a culture of agile experimentation.

title: Loomis Costco project could get final approvals next week
summary: The Loomis Costco project, including a new store and gas station, is nearing final approval. The town of Loomis took a step closer to approving the project on Tuesday night, with the proposal set to go before the Town Council next week.

title: Dick’s Sporting Goods to open outlet store in Tempe
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods is set to open a new outlet store, "Overtime," at the Arizona Mills Mall in Tempe. This development was reported by Brandon Brown of the Phoenix Business Journal on August 7, 2020. The article also briefly mentions other related news like Covid-19's impact on Sprouts and gym openings, and updates on Costco and J.C. Penney.

title: Dollar Tree, Family Dollar reverse mask policy again. Now requiring customers wear masks amid COVID-19.
summary: Dollar Tree and Family Dollar have reinstated a mandatory mask policy for all associates, customers, and vendors in their stores, aligning with most other major retailers and CDC guidelines. This marks another reversal for the company, which initially required masks in early July before shifting to a "request" in areas without local ordinances. The change follows similar moves by other large retailers in response to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

title: American Express Said to Be in Talks to Buy Kabbage for $850 Million
summary: American Express is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire online lender Kabbage for an all-cash deal worth up to $850 million. This potential acquisition would further solidify American Express's presence in the small-business market, a sector from which 30% of its revenue is derived. The move follows similar high-value fintech acquisitions by Mastercard and Visa, indicating a broader trend among traditional card networks to integrate fintech innovation.

title: Belinda Carlisle 'Go-Go's' After Kroger: Reconsider Ties With Monkey-Abusing Coconut Company
summary: PETA supporter and Go-Go's singer Belinda Carlisle urged Kroger to stop sourcing coconut milk from Chaokoh due to its alleged use of forced monkey labor in Thailand. Carlisle, who resides in Thailand, highlighted the cruel conditions under which monkeys are reportedly trained and exploited to pick coconuts. PETA's exposé led over 25,000 stores to drop Chaokoh products, and Carlisle is campaigning for other major retailers like Costco and Albertsons to follow suit.

title: Appeals Court Sides with Costco in $21 Million Fight Over "Counterfeit" Tiffany Rings
summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit has sided with Costco in its long-standing legal battle with Tiffany & Co., overturning a lower court's decision that found Costco liable for trademark infringement and counterfeiting. The appeals court ruled that the district court erred by granting summary judgment and preventing a jury from deciding key issues, remanding the case for a new trial. This decision suggests that a jury could reasonably conclude that customers would not be confused by Costco's use of "Tiffany" to describe a ring setting style, rather than implying a genuine Tiffany product.

title: US Appeals Court Voids Tiffany's Judgment Against Costco Over Fake 'Tiffany' Rings
summary: A federal appeals court has overturned a $21 million judgment granted to Tiffany & Co. against Costco Wholesale Corp. regarding the sale of diamond engagement rings bearing the "Tiffany" name. The court ruled that a lower court erred by not allowing jurors to decide if Costco's use of the name was likely to confuse customers or if Costco acted in good faith, sending the case back for a new trial. Costco argued that "Tiffany" had become a generic term for a pronged diamond setting.

title: U.S. appeals court voids Tiffany's judgment against Costco over fake 'Tiffany' rings
summary: A federal appeals court has overturned a $21 million judgment Tiffany & Co had won against Costco Wholesale Corp. The court ruled that a lower court judge erred in finding Costco liable for selling diamond rings labeled "Tiffany," stating that reasonable jurors could find customers were not confused and that Costco acted in good faith. The case has been sent back for a new trial.

title: Second Circuit Vacates Tiffany's $21 Million Win Over Costco
summary: The Second Circuit Court of Appeals vacated Tiffany's $21 million summary judgment win over Costco in a trademark infringement and counterfeiting case. The court ruled that Costco raised triable issues of fact regarding likelihood of confusion, Costco's intent, and consumer sophistication, remanding the case for trial. This decision provides guidance on evidence treatment at the summary judgment stage and clarifies the distinction between trademark infringement and counterfeiting.

title: Revisited: Media Consumption during the Coronavirus Pandemic
summary: This article revisits media consumption trends during the COVID-19 pandemic, analyzing changes in digital visits across various categories like news, retail, government, and travel from mid-March to early August 2020. It highlights how digital engagement remained significantly higher than pre-pandemic levels in many sectors, despite some declines from peak lockdown periods, while travel showed a gradual recovery after an initial sharp drop. Comscore's data reveals sustained shifts in consumer behavior and the varying impacts on different industries.

title: Grocery boosts BJ’s Wholesale Club to 24% Q2 comp-sales growth
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club reported significant financial growth in Q2 fiscal 2020, with net sales climbing 18.4% to $3.87 billion and comparable-club sales surging 17.2%. Grocery sales were a major catalyst, increasing by 25%. E-commerce sales skyrocketed 300%, largely driven by buy-online-pickup-in-club (BOPIC) and same-day delivery services, propelling the company years ahead of its digital transformation goals.

title: BJ’s Wholesale makes pickup contactless, adds grocery items
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club has introduced new contactless curbside pickup services at all its stores and is expanding its buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPIS) service to include fresh and frozen grocery items. These initiatives aim to provide members with more convenient shopping options, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. Other retailers like Sam’s Club, Costco, and Target are also implementing similar services.

title: Second Circuit Vacates Trademark Infringement Holding Against Costco For Use of the Term ‘Tiffany’
summary: The Second Circuit Court of Appeals has vacated and remanded a lower court's decision that Costco was liable for trademark infringement and counterfeiting for using the term "Tiffany" in relation to diamond rings. The appeals court determined that the district court erred by granting summary judgment to Tiffany & Co., finding that Costco had presented sufficient evidence to raise genuine questions about the likelihood of customer confusion, its good faith, and the sophistication of consumers. This means a jury could reasonably conclude that "Tiffany" describes a type of ring setting, not exclusively a Tiffany & Co. product, and that Costco used the term descriptively.

title: Beyond Meat Launches DTC Platform With 2 Day Home Delivery, is #1 Refrigerated Plant Meat Brand
summary: Beyond Meat has launched a direct-to-consumer (DTC) platform offering two-day home delivery across 48 contiguous U.S. states. This announcement coincides with SPINS data confirming Beyond Meat as the #1 brand in refrigerated plant-based meat for July, holding the top four selling items overall. The company is promoting the launch with a $5 discount on all orders and highlights its carbon-neutral shipping.

title: Target adding 600 more products to Good & Gather food and beverage brand, including signature line
summary: Target is expanding its Good & Gather food and beverage brand with 600 new products, bringing the total to nearly 2,000 items and making it Target's largest store-owned brand. The brand, which launched a year ago, has already generated over $1 billion in sales and is expected to become a multi-billion dollar brand. This expansion is part of Target's strategy to enhance its food and beverage offerings and increase profitability through store-owned brands.

title: AquaBounty salmon is what’s for dinner if you can find it
summary: AquaBounty's genetically engineered (GE) salmon is facing opposition from environmental groups, which are pressuring retailers not to sell it, despite regulatory approvals and positive reviews. The company plans its first U.S. harvest and commercial sales soon, having developed the faster-growing salmon through genetic modification. Retailers like Costco express caution, while environmental groups highlight potential risks to wild salmon populations and widespread market rejection.

title: Supercharged Sales Growth at Kroger
summary: Kroger reported significant earnings growth in Q2, driven by a 127% increase in e-commerce sales and strong identical same-store sales growth of 14.6% excluding fuel. This performance comes as consumers increased at-home cooking during the pandemic, leading Kroger to update its full-year 2020 guidance for identical sales to exceed 13% and adjusted EPS growth of 45% to 50%. The company's investments in digital operations and customer experience have been key to its success and growing market share.

title: New US Foods Chef'Store set to open in Charleston
summary: US Foods Chef'Store is set to open its sixth big-box location in Charleston at 1510 Meeting St. in mid-September. The 59,000-square-foot store will offer wholesale food, equipment, and supplies to both the restaurant industry and the public, operating without a membership requirement. This opening is part of a larger trend of new large retail stores in the Charleston area, following Costco and preceding a new Whole Foods Market.

title: Walmart launches Amazon Prime subscription competitor, 'Walmart+'
summary: Walmart has launched its new subscription program, "Walmart+", to compete with Amazon Prime. For $12.95 a month or $98 a year, subscribers receive benefits like unlimited free same-day delivery, fuel discounts, and a touch-free in-store shopping experience. This initiative aims to cater to consumer demand for faster online purchase delivery and integrates previous services like "Delivery Unlimited."

title: Zoup! Restaurant-Quality Broth Hits 9,000+ Stores Nationwide
summary: Zoup! Good, Really Good® Broth has significantly expanded its distribution, now available in over 9,000 stores nationwide, including major retailers like Kroger banners and Walmart. The brand, founded by Zoup! Eatery's Eric Ersher, offers premium, natural, and organic broths and bone broths, focusing on high-quality ingredients and restaurant-level taste. Zoup! was also recognized on the Inc. 5000 list for its rapid growth, achieving 420% revenue growth in three years.

title: Epic is not EXACTly the Microsoft of Madison
summary: This article argues that while Epic Systems Corp. is often compared to Microsoft in terms of its regional economic impact, the comparison is flawed. The author, through Erik Iverson of WARF, suggests that Exact Sciences, due to its publicly traded nature and broad employee stock options, is more akin to Madison's Microsoft, creating localized wealth. The article also details Epic's private stock plan for employees, noting its differences from Microsoft's early model.

title: Costco co-founder told CEO 'I will kill you' following hot dog combo price hike suggestion
summary: Costco co-founder Jim Sinegal famously threatened current CEO W. Craig Jelinek with death if he ever raised the price of the $1.50 hot dog and soda combo. This exchange, which occurred after Jelinek noted the company was losing money on the item, went viral. Costco has not increased the price of the popular combo since 1984, selling an impressive 151 million units in 2019.

title: Costco’s Sales Get Another Boost From Pandemic Buying
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. continues to see increased sales as consumers stock up on groceries, cleaning supplies, and home furnishings during the pandemic. The company's total revenue reached $53.38 billion, a 12% increase from the previous year. This surge in sales is attributed to people redirecting spending from travel and dining to bulk purchases.

title: Why Costco says it won't offer curbside grocery pickup
summary: Costco's CFO, Richard Galanti, stated the company has no immediate plans to offer curbside grocery pickup despite rivals doing so. The company is focusing on its strong in-store sales, which saw a 14.1% increase in total comp-store sales and a 91.3% jump in e-commerce sales, driven by customers buying more per trip during the pandemic.

title: Infographic: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) reports Q4 2020 earnings
summary: Costco Wholesale Corporation reported strong Q4 2020 earnings, with net profit increasing to $1.39 billion or $3.13 per share and net sales growing by 13% to $52.28 billion.
