The company's results surpassed analysts' expectations, driven by an 11.4% increase in comparable-store sales. Costco's stock closed higher on Thursday but saw a decline in after-hours trading.

title: Worried about more shortages, grocery stores are stockpiling goods
summary: Grocery stores across the U.S. are stockpiling products like paper towels, Clorox wipes, and even holiday turkeys and cold remedies to avoid shortages during a potential second wave of coronavirus. This strategy shifts from stocking weeks to months worth of supplies, driven by consumer hoarding and ongoing demand, which has also led to higher prices. Manufacturers like Clorox anticipate shortages well into 2021 despite increased production efforts.

title: Walmart brings online shopping experience in stores with app-driven redesign
summary: Walmart is redesigning its Supercenters to integrate the online shopping experience into its physical stores, aiming to encourage app usage and streamline customer navigation. The redesign, inspired by airport wayfinding systems, will include updated signage, self-checkout kiosks, and contactless payment options. This initiative follows a trend among other retailers like Amazon and Whole Foods to merge in-store and online shopping experiences.

title: Costco to open in Midland Nov. 12
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is scheduled to open its new Midland location on November 12, 2020, at 4816 Bay City Road. General Manager Mark Zuerner discussed the store's offerings, including its unique pallet-driven inventory, food court with the famous $1.50 hot dog, a fuel station, optical and hearing aid centers, and pharmacy services. The store will open with over 200 employees, many hired locally, and will implement safety measures for the coronavirus pandemic, including an hour early senior shopping and social distancing.

title: Walmart’s U.K. Retreat Leaves Asda With New Owners, Old Problems
summary: Walmart Inc. has sold a controlling stake in its U.K. supermarket chain Asda to TDR Capital and the Issa brothers, marking its retreat from the U.K. retail market. This move leaves Asda with new owners, who are expected to bring entrepreneurial flair, but also faces long-standing challenges in the competitive U.K. supermarket business against established players like Tesco and J Sainsbury. The 1999 acquisition of Asda by Walmart was initially seen as a major disruptor to the market.

title: Office Stationery And Supplies B2B Market to Reach $29.14 bn by 2024, 3M Co., Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Amazon.com Inc., and WHSmith Plc., Emerge as Key Contributors to Growth | Technavio
summary: The office stationery and supplies B2B market is projected to grow by USD 29.14 billion from 2020-2024, with a CAGR of almost 3%. Key market drivers include the increasing demand for recyclable stationery products and the growing online sale of office stationery and supplies. Major contributors to this growth include 3M Co., Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Amazon.com Inc., and WHSmith Plc., with APAC expected to contribute 36% of the market share.

title: Humana Welcomes Additional Retail Pharmacies to Preferred Medicare Part D Network
summary: Humana has announced the addition of Kroger Health, Costco, Publix, and HEB to its preferred stand-alone Medicare Part D pharmacy network, effective January 1, 2021. This expansion significantly increases the number of locations where Humana Medicare prescription drug plan members can access lower out-of-pocket costs on medications, growing from 5,200 to nearly 9,500 pharmacy locations. The move aims to provide Humana members with more convenient and affordable options for their prescription drug needs.

title: Kroger, Costco, Publix and H-E-B Join Humana’s Medicare Part D Pharmacy Network
summary: Kroger Health, Costco, Publix Super Markets, and H-E-B have joined Humana's preferred stand-alone Medicare Part D pharmacy network for 2021. This expansion significantly increases the number of locations where Humana Medicare prescription drug plan members can find lower-cost prescription medications, adding almost 9,500 pharmacy locations. The new agreements are set to take effect on January 1st of next year.

title: Poway Unified parents rally against proposed Costco development at vacant school site
summary: Parents and students in the Poway Unified School District rallied against a proposal to lease a vacant school site to Costco Wholesale Corp. The district's board had voted to explore the long-term lease for the 27.2-acre "surplus property," citing Costco's offer of $2.1 million annually for the first 10 years. Protesters gathered over 2,000 signatures, accusing the board of using the pandemic to advance the deal without proper community engagement.

title: Sam's Club expands autonomous floor-sweeping robots to all U.S. stores
summary: Sam's Club is expanding its partnership with Brain Corp to deploy autonomous floor-scrubbing robots to all its U.S. stores, totaling around 600 locations. This initiative builds on Walmart's earlier collaboration with Brain Corp and also includes an expanded shelf analytics pilot with cleaning company Tennant to improve pricing accuracy and product availability. The move highlights a growing trend of robotics in big box retail to enhance efficiency and promote contactless environments.

title: BJ's Wholesale Club could be next anchor at Willowbrook Mall in Wayne
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club is proposing to open a 105,031-square-foot members-only store and a six-pump gas station at Willowbrook Mall in Wayne, New Jersey. The new store would occupy the former Sears department store space. This would mark BJ's Wholesale's first location in Passaic County, pending approval from the Planning Board.

title: Carter’s to close at least 200 stores
summary: Carter's plans to close approximately 200 stores, representing 25% of its fleet, as leases expire, focusing on more profitable e-commerce and wholesale partnerships. The closures target older, lower-margin stores in declining areas while the company also plans to open some new locations in densely populated areas. Despite the pandemic's challenges, increased e-commerce sales and essential children's apparel demand helped the company exceed third-quarter expectations.

title: Dollar General pays employees the least among 25 retailers, according to UBS report
summary: A new UBS report indicates that Dollar General pays its employees the least among 25 major U.S. retailers, with an average hourly wage of $9.68. This figure is significantly lower than competitors like Costco ($17.60), Walmart ($13.08), and Target ($13.21), despite Dollar General's substantial sales growth during the COVID-19 pandemic. The report highlights the disparity in COMPENSATION WITHIN the retail sector, particularly for discount chains.

title: Capital One ending Costco and Hudson’s Bay contracts, closing offices in Montreal and Toronto
summary: Capital One is reducing its Canadian operations by ending its credit card partnership contracts with Costco Canada and Hudson's Bay in 2021, shifting focus to its own branded credit card business. This strategic change will lead to the closure of its Montreal and Toronto call centers, although most employees will retain their jobs within Capital One, with some layoffs expected. The company assures customers that their card operations will not be immediately affected and they will be supported through the transition.

title: Pushing for US & Middle East to eat organic, Saudi prince joins Back To The Roots round
summary: Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed bin Talal Al Saud's investment firm, KBW Ventures, has joined a funding round for organic gardening company Back to the Roots. The company, co-led by agrifoodtech specialists S2G Ventures and Acre Venture Partners, sells home organic growkits and seeds, with a focus on US-grown retail seed packets. Prince Khaled, a prominent vegan investor, sees significant market potential for organic produce in the Gulf countries and actively supports companies that positively impact the food chain and offer healthy options.

title: Grocers look to online subscriptions to lock in digital demand
summary: Grocery retailers like Kroger, Ahold Delhaize, and Albertsons are increasingly offering online subscription programs for delivery or pickup to capitalize on the shift to digital shopping and build customer loyalty. These programs serve as a defensive measure against competitors like Amazon Prime and Walmart+, aiming to retain existing customers and attract new ones. Experts suggest that grocers need to offer additional perks beyond just delivery fee waivers to make these subscriptions truly valuable and differentiate themselves from third-party services like Instacart.

title: Here are the businesses closing their doors on Thanksgiving
summary: Many major retailers and businesses are opting to close their doors on Thanksgiving this year, a shift from previous years. This decision allows their employees and customers to spend time with family, with some companies also citing safety concerns due to the coronavirus pandemic. As a result, Black Friday sales are largely expected to begin online or in stores on Friday morning, bringing back a more traditional start to the holiday shopping season.

title: Trump administration partners with chain and independent community pharmacies to increase access to future COVID-19 vaccines
summary: The Trump administration announced partnerships with large chain pharmacies and networks representing independent pharmacies to ensure widespread access to future COVID-19 vaccines. This initiative aims to cover about 60% of pharmacies across the U.S. and its territories, leveraging existing infrastructure to deliver vaccines at no cost to patients. The program was established in anticipation of FDA-authorized and CDC-recommended COVID-19 vaccines becoming available before the end of 2020.

title: How Walmart, Kroger Plan to Become Advertising Giants
summary: Walmart and Kroger are looking to become major players in online advertising, capitalizing on the pandemic-driven surge in e-commerce. These retail titans aim to leverage increased online traffic and consumer data to boost long-term profits through their advertising platforms. The accelerated shift to e-commerce has provided a significant opportunity for these well-positioned retailers.

title: Amazon opens online pharmacy, disrupting another industry
summary: Amazon has launched an online pharmacy service, allowing customers to order prescriptions for home delivery. This move significantly impacted the pharmaceutical sector, causing stock drops for CVS Health Corp., Walgreens, and Rite Aid, as analysts predict a shift in prescription fulfillment from traditional retail channels to Amazon. The company's entry into health care, following its 2018 acquisition of PillPack, is seen as a major disruption, potentially leading to its evolution into a pharmacy benefit manager.

title: Costco Executive Membership Class Action Settlement
summary: Costco agreed to a $525,000 class action settlement to resolve claims that it failed to refund consumers for cancelled executive memberships, despite advertising a "Risk-Free 100% Satisfaction Guarantee." Eligible Class Members who cancelled their memberships and were not fully refunded could claim a free year of Costco membership or a cash payment of up to $15. The settlement received final approval in December 2020, and payouts of $15 were reported by February 2021.

title: Target-owned Shipt Seeking Another 50K Seasonal Shoppers
summary: Target-owned Shipt announced plans to hire an additional 50,000 seasonal shoppers nationwide, on top of the 100,000 announced in October, to meet increased demand for online delivery services during the holiday season. The company is particularly focusing on adding 6,000 shoppers in the Twin Cities, alongside other key markets, aiming to support customers with care during an "unprecedented holiday season." Shipt shoppers are gig workers and for now, the company remains an independently operated subsidiary of Target.

title: Here is a list of Black Friday store hours in the Houston area
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of Black Friday store and mall hours for the Houston area in 2020. It advises shoppers on special opening and closing times for various retailers and emphasizes the requirement for masks due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The piece helps residents plan their shopping trips efficiently and safely.

title: Walmart+ drops free shipping minimum
summary: Walmart+ is eliminating its $35 shipping minimum for members, directly enhancing its competition with Amazon Prime. This change, effective Friday, means members will receive free next-day and two-day shipping on items shipped by Walmart regardless of order total, though grocery delivery from stores still has a minimum. Additionally, Walmart is expanding fuel discount opportunities for members, offering Sam's Club pricing at various gas stations.

title: Pitney Bowes offers same-day delivery as fast as 2 hours with gig economy last-mile partners
summary: Pitney Bowes has launched a new door-to-door same-day delivery service through its SendPro platform, leveraging third-party gig economy logistics providers. This service offers delivery windows as short as two hours for parcels up to 50 pounds, traveling distances of 50 miles or less. The initiative aims to enable smaller shippers to compete with larger retailers, with interest primarily coming from small to medium businesses, B2B, and offline fulfillment companies.

title: Sonos Arc SL spotted at Costco: Mic-free soundbar costs less than Sonos Arc
summary: Sonos has reportedly launched a microphone-free version of its Dolby Atmos soundbar, the Sonos Arc SL, available exclusively at Costco in the US and Canada. This "SL" model is $50 cheaper than the regular Sonos Arc, costing $749, and comes in a "shadow edition" color. While it lacks built-in microphones for voice assistants, its audio and hardware are otherwise identical to the standard Sonos Arc.

title: Kroger, other retailers see 'eye-popping profits' as workers reap little benefit
summary: A new report by the Brookings Institution reveals that supermarket chains and other food retailers saw their profits soar by an average of 39% in the first half of the year due to the pandemic, with Kroger's profits jumping 90%. Despite these "eye-popping profits," front-line workers largely reaped little benefit, as many retailers quickly ended "hero pay" and replaced it with less generous bonuses. The report highlights inequalities between worker compensation and company financial performance, prompting unions to press for the reinstatement of hazard pay amidst rising COVID-19 cases.

title: Coca-Cola sells its Centre County production facility for $5.6 million
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has sold its Centre County water bottling plant to Milesburg Properties, LLC, which is affiliated with Niagara Bottling, for $5.593 million. The sale's impact on the estimated 100 employees at the facility is unclear, as neither company responded to requests for comment. Local commissioners hope Niagara Bottling will continue to be a good community resource and employer.

title: Coca-Cola sells bottling plant to Niagara Bottling
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has sold its water bottling facility in Centre County, Pennsylvania, to Niagara Bottling. The facility was sold to Milesburg Properties LLC, which shares a corporate office address with Niagara Bottling. A local commissioner expressed hope that Niagara Bottling will continue to be a positive community resource and employer.

title: Costco Isn't Owned by China, Has Solid U.S. Roots
summary: This article clarifies that Costco is an American company, not owned by China, despite its successful ventures in the Chinese market. It details Costco's origins in the U.S., its merger with Price Club, and its global expansion. The article also touches on the enthusiasm surrounding Costco's first store opening in China and differences in its Chinese online presence.

title: Why Costco Has Won 2020
summary: Costco experienced significant sales acceleration in 2020, driven by its reputation as a pandemic "safe space" for shoppers and robust growth in fresh food and online grocery sales. The retailer's Q1 results showed a 17% increase in same-store sales and 86% jump in online sales, with net sales reaching $42.35 billion. Costco also reported increased membership fee income and a unique offering of a private jet service, while continuing to pay employees higher wages during the pandemic.

title: Costco Keeps Drawing Homebound Shoppers
summary: Costco reported strong quarterly sales driven by homebound Americans spending more on food, home goods, and fitness products during the pandemic. The warehouse chain saw a 17.1% increase in comparable sales and an 86% jump in e-commerce sales for the quarter ending November 22, catering heavily to its high-income shopper base. This growth comes as the retail landscape continues to evolve in response to pandemic-related consumer behavior.

title: Costco beats estimates as grocery demand booms during pandemic
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST.O) exceeded market estimates for its first-quarter profit and revenue due to increased demand for groceries, liquor, and electronics from consumers staying home during the pandemic. The company saw an 86% jump in online sales and a 7% rise in membership revenue. Despite incurring $212 million in COVID-19-related charges, its net income soared 38% to $1.17 billion, with total revenue reaching $43.21 billion.

title: Amazing Comparable Sales Aren’t Enough to Move the Needle for Costco
summary: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) reported strong fiscal first-quarter results, beating EPS and revenue estimates and showing significant increases in net and comparable sales. Despite these positive financial figures, including a substantial jump in e-commerce, the stock remained relatively flat in early trading, suggesting that the impressive sales weren't sufficient to significantly move the market. The report also detailed expenses related to COVID-19 premium wages and noted that the company did not issue forward guidance.

title: Costco’s revenue beats on strong food demand during pandemic
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp reported first-quarter revenue that surpassed market estimates due to increased purchases of frozen foods, liquor, and home furnishings by consumers staying home during the pandemic. Online sales saw a significant jump of 86%, supported by investments in faster delivery. The company's net income and total revenue also saw substantial increases compared to the previous year.

title: Costco Is Selling Boxes Of More Than 50 Cheesecake Bites From The Cheesecake Factory
summary: Costco is now selling boxes of The Cheesecake Factory's cheesecake bites, offering an easy alternative to buying a whole cheesecake. Each box contains 54 pre-sliced bites of original cheesecake with vanilla crumb, featuring caramel, raspberry, and chocolate swirl flavors. These frozen treats can be thawed in the fridge for 8-12 hours or even enjoyed frozen, and were spotted at Costco for about $13.

title: Here is what the redevelopment of Paradise Valley Mall could look like
summary: Macerich, owner of Paradise Valley Mall, has submitted initial concept renderings to the City of Phoenix for a major redevelopment of the 77-acre property. The proposed transformation includes a mix of housing, retail, a specialty grocery store, and office space, aiming to revitalize the failing mall into a vibrant, mixed-use development similar to Kierland Commons or Desert Ridge Marketplace. The first phase focuses on the southeast side of the property, with existing anchors like JCPenney and Macy's not part of the immediate redevelopment plans.

title: Grocery Retail Market in UK to Grow by $ 43.22 Billion During 2020-2024 | Featuring Aldi Stores Ltd., Co-operative Group Ltd., and Costco Wholesale Corp. among others | Technavio
summary: The grocery retail market in the UK is projected to grow by USD 43.22 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of almost 4%. This growth is attributed to rapid urbanization and increasing consumer spending, though the demand for convenient food products could pose a challenge. Key contributors to this growth include the foods and beverage segment and the hypermarkets and supermarkets retail format, with major players like Aldi Stores Ltd., Co-operative Group Ltd., and Costco Wholesale Corp. driving the market.

title: FedEx, UPS are managing surge in packages with strict limits on shippers
summary: FedEx and UPS are implementing strict package limits on shippers to manage the record surge in holiday package volumes, leading to backlogs for retailers like Costco. This strategy helps the carriers maintain strong on-time delivery scores despite the high demand and pandemic-related challenges, though it frustrates businesses unable to ship all their inventory. Small and medium-sized businesses have been particularly affected, with some experiencing sudden cutoffs and significant delays.

title: Kroger Makes PETA’s Corporate ‘Naughty’ List for Monkey Labor Scandal
summary: PETA has included Kroger on its corporate "naughty" list for continuing to sell coconut products from suppliers that use forced monkey labor in Thailand. Despite efforts from PETA and a growing number of retailers banning such products, Kroger has refused to sever ties with brands like Chaokoh. PETA's list also highlights other companies for animal welfare concerns, including Starbucks, Petco, and Urban Outfitters.

title: Kroger lays out its top food trends for 2021
summary: Kroger has released its top food trend predictions for 2021, focusing on "futureproof foods" that boost immunity and gut health, alongside easy-to-prepare comfort foods, vegetarian keto options, and international flavors. The grocer also reflected on 2020 trends, which highlighted typical pandemic shopping habits like snack foods and ingredients for home-cooked restaurant-style meals. These predictions align with broader industry trends concentrating on wellness and promoting Kroger's own growing private labels, particularly the "Simple Truth" brand with its plant-based offerings.

title: Private-label Food and Beverage Market in US 2020-2024 - Featuring Albertsons Companies Inc., Amazon.Com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., Among Others to Contribute to the Market Growth
summary: The private-label food and beverage market in the US is projected to grow by USD 30.68 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of almost 4%. This growth is primarily driven by product line extensions from private-label vendors and the premiumization of these products. Key companies contributing to this market include Albertsons Companies Inc., Amazon.com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., and Walmart Inc.

title: Costco Is Selling a Babe Ruth Autographed Ball for $64,000
summary: Costco is offering a Babe Ruth autographed baseball for $63,999.99 on its website, surprising customers looking for everyday essentials. Additionally, the retail giant also lists a Ty Cobb autographed bat for $159,999.99, featuring a surprisingly cordial inscription. These high-value sports memorabilia items are unexpected offerings from the bulk retailer.

title: A Babe Ruth-Signed Baseball Is Now on Sale at Costco (Yes, Costco) for $64,000
summary: Costco is selling a rare baseball autographed by Babe Ruth for $64,000 through its website, positioning it as a significant sports memorabilia item. The "Home Run Special" baseball comes with a full letter of authenticity, and Costco claims it's one of the finest examples in existence. This move by Costco into high-end memorabilia reflects the booming market for such collectibles, with baseball items often being the strongest segment.

title: Best Buy Mission Statement | Vision | Values & Culture (2025 Analysis)
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Best Buy's mission statement, vision statement, values, and culture. It examines how Best Buy's commitment to technological innovation, enhancing customer lives, and positive global impact drives its operations. The article also highlights the company's core values, including fostering a rewarding work environment and ethical conduct, and its guiding cultural behaviors of being human, making it real, and thinking about tomorrow.

title: Fresno big-box stores like Target, Walmart to be shut down under proposed emergency order
summary: Fresno City Councilman Luis Chavez is proposing a five-day closure of all retail businesses, including big-box stores like Target and Walmart, within city limits to provide relief for struggling hospitals and help curb coronavirus transmission. The order, which would allow curbside pickup and delivery, would go into effect if ICU capacity reaches zero. Fines for non-compliance would range from $1,000 to $10,000.

title: Department of Justice Files Nationwide Lawsuit Against Walmart Inc. for Controlled Substances Act Violation
summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed a civil complaint against Walmart Inc. for alleged violations of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA) during the peak of the opioid crisis. The lawsuit claims Walmart unlawfully dispensed controlled substances from its pharmacies and failed to report suspicious orders as a distributor. Walmart denies the allegations, stating it is actively fighting the opioid crisis and plans to contest the lawsuit in court.

title: Costco Wholesale Corporation (NASDAQ:COST) Pays Huge Dividends
summary: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) has continued to pay lucrative dividends to shareholders, despite the COVID-19 pandemic, due to its success in selling essential goods. The company's unique membership-based business model allows it to sell inventory at cost, providing a competitive advantage. Outstanding financial results, including a 17% year-over-year increase in same-store sales and an 86% rise in e-commerce revenue, have enabled Costco to issue a record $4.4-billion special distribution to shareholders, contributing to a 32% year-to-date increase in COST stock.

title: Walmart Has Closed More Than 20 U.S. Stores for Deep Cleaning in Past Month
summary: Walmart has temporarily closed over 20 stores across the U.S. in the past month for deep cleaning due to employee COVID-19 cases or exposures, amid a surge in nationwide infections. These closures typically last 41 hours, allowing third-party crews to sanitize stores before reopening. The company has also implemented various safety measures like associate health screens, mask policies, and sneeze guards to protect staff and shoppers.

title: Gerard Dempsey Obituary - Sandy Springs, GA
summary: Gerard J. Dempsey, a former executive for Costco Wholesale Corp., passed away on January 7, 2021, at the age of 68 after a battle with cancer. He worked at Costco for 32 years, holding various management and vice president positions including Regional Operations Manager and VP of Operations. Gerard was known for his wit, wisdom, honesty, and passion for art, music, cooking, and travel, and is survived by his wife Joan, daughter Alison, and several siblings.

title: Covid-19 Propels Amazon to Top U.S. Grocery Retailer for the 2021 dunnhumby Retailer Preference Index
summary: Amazon has been named the top U.S. grocery retailer in dunnhumby's fourth annual Retailer Preference Index for 2021, surpassing H-E-B and Trader Joe's. This shift is largely attributed to Covid-19 driven momentum, with Amazon excelling in speed, digital offerings, and customer safety. The study emphasizes that while traditional factors like price and quality remain crucial for long-term growth, the ability to deliver on speed and digital experience became paramount during the pandemic.

title: Billboard at Kroger HQ Demands Retailer Eliminate Bee-killing Pesticides Used to Grow Food it Sells
summary: Environmental and consumer groups, led by Friends of the Earth, have placed a billboard near Kroger's Cincinnati headquarters demanding the retailer eliminate bee-killing pesticides from its food supply chain. Acknowledging previous commitments on live plants, the groups urge Kroger to extend this action to its broader food and beverage supply chains, where it currently lags behind competitors in addressing pollinator-toxic pesticides. They highlight the critical role pollinators play in food production and call on Kroger to leverage its market power to shift away from these harmful pesticides.

title: Costco closing photo centers at all warehouses
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. announced it will close all photo centers in its warehouses nationwide starting Feb. 14, 2021. The decision was made due to a decline in the need for printing photos since the rise of camera phones and social media. While many in-person services will cease, some products like prints, photo books, and calendars will remain available online for delivery.

title: Beyond Meat to Unveil $178M State-of-the-Art Facility & HQ
summary: Beyond Meat has announced a 12-year lease for a new, nearly 300,000 square foot global headquarters in El Segundo, Los Angeles, valued at over $178 million. This state-of-the-art facility will significantly expand its research capabilities, including the use of AI and machine learning, and support multiple product lines and a tripling of research personnel. The move signals the company's continued growth, defying current office leasing trends amidst the pandemic.

title: Lovesac: Thriving Through Innovation and Expansion in Challenging Times
summary: Lovesac, a US furniture retailer, experienced over 40% growth in 2019 and continued to innovate and expand in 2020 despite the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic. The company maintained strong revenue by moving online and also plans to open new retail locations, believing that physical showrooms are crucial for converting high-ticket item sales. Lovesac focuses on two main product lines, Sacs and Sactionals, and aims for continued growth through strategic partnerships, new product innovations, and a commitment to sustainability with its "Designed for Life" philosophy.

title: HubSpot Pledges $20 Million To Social Impact Investing, Including Support For Black-Led Financial Institutions
summary: HubSpot has committed $20 million to social impact investing, with an initial $12.5 million directed to the Black Economic Development Fund managed by the Local Initiatives Support Corporation (LISC). This investment aims to support Black-led financial institutions and foster economic empowerment, joining other major companies like PayPal and Netflix. The fund's impact treasury strategy will provide capital access for Black communities, aligning with LISC’s broader Project 10X initiative.

title: Target drops Chaokoh coconut milk after PETA's allegations of forced monkey labor, follows Costco
summary: Target has announced it is dropping Chaokoh coconut milk from its shelves due to PETA's allegations of forced monkey labor in coconut harvesting. This decision follows similar actions by Costco and other retailers, after PETA's ongoing investigation into Thai coconut producers. Chaokoh's maker, Theppadungporn Coconut Co. Ltd., denies these claims and states their plantations have been audited to confirm no monkey labor is used.

title: Costco buys land on far West Side in San Antonio
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has purchased land on the far West Side of San Antonio for a new store, located between a Walmart Supercenter and the Shops at Dove Creek. The 16.44-acre property is planned to include a 160,620-square-foot mercantile building with an open canopy and a gas station. This news follows previous rumors of a new Costco location in the area.

title: Costco buys land on San Antonio’s far West Side for new store and gas station
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has purchased 16.44 acres on San Antonio's far West Side for a new store and gas station, marking further development in the rapidly growing area. The project is estimated to cost $15.2 million with construction expected to finish in July. This expansion adds to the existing Costco presence in San Antonio and Selma, contributing to the retail growth alongside other recent developments in the area.

title: Express Briefing: New Costco planned for S.A.’s far West Side
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has purchased 16.44 acres on San Antonio's far West Side to build a new store and gas station, responding to rapid residential and retail development in the area. This news comes as USAA announces a significant cut in its annual employee bonus, reaching its lowest point since 2007. The briefing also reports that the coronavirus death toll in Bexar County is nearing 2,000, despite a recent drop in new cases and hospitalizations.

title: Costco Plans New Store, Gas Station In West San Antonio
summary: Costco is planning a new store and gas station in the rapidly growing West San Antonio area, specifically off the Loop 1604 access road, south of Potranco Road. The new facility will be a 160,000 square-foot store costing $13.2 million, with construction expected to begin on February 1 and finish by July 31. This development will be situated near other major retailers and aims to serve one of San Antonio's fastest-growing regions.

title: Clermont is the perfect location for Costco. Here's why.
summary: Clermont, Florida, is being considered as the location for a new Costco warehouse. A single Costco can generate $192 million in annual sales, suggesting this would be a significant development for the area. The article highlights other related developments and businesses in the region.

title: Costco logistics center would be Lewis County's largest building
summary: Costco is considering building a 1.5 million-square-foot logistics center in Lewis County, which would be the largest building in the county. This project, if it moves forward, would be the third major distribution center for Lewis County, a strategic location between Seattle and Portland. The Port of Chehalis is currently studying the feasibility of this massive development.

title: Wheels Up to go public via a merger with LVMH-backed SPAC
summary: Wheels Up announced it will go public through a merger with Aspirational Consumer Lifestyle Corp. (NYSE: ASPL), an LVMH-backed SPAC, valuing the company at $2.1 billion. This deal is expected to provide Wheels Up with up to $790 million in cash to fund operations and expansion, including potential international markets and luxury adjacencies. The merger positions Wheels Up as the first private aviation platform to list on the NYSE and capitalizes on strong demand in the private aviation sector.

title: Kroger, Walmart unveil funding recipients for racial equity initiatives
summary: Kroger and Walmart have announced the recipients of funding for their racial equity initiatives. Walmart and the Walmart Foundation are distributing $14.3 million to 16 groups as part of a larger $100 million commitment over five years, while the Kroger Foundation is awarding $3 million to four organizations selected from a competitive application process. These grants, announced during Black History Month, aim to support equitable and inclusive communities and bolster diversity efforts within the retail and grocery industries.

title: Animal rights activists lambaste Costco supplier over its rotisserie chickens
summary: Animal rights group Mercy for Animals has accused Lincoln Premium Poultry, a Costco supplier, of "cruel" animal practices in its rotisserie chicken operations. An undercover investigation allegedly revealed chickens crammed into filthy sheds, bred to an unnatural weight leading to health issues, and found "large piles of dead, rotting animals" on the facility's grounds. While Costco stated its commitment to high animal welfare standards and indicated it would use audit results and the investigation's findings for improvement, Mercy for Animals is urging Costco to adopt stricter "Better Chicken Commitment" standards, which over 200 other companies have already implemented.

title: HBC partners with Neo Financial to launch new Hudson’s Bay MasterCard
summary: Hudson's Bay Company (HBC) has partnered with Neo Financial to introduce a new Hudson's Bay MasterCard, following the end of its relationship with Capital One. This move is part of HBC's "digital-first strategy" to enhance customer experience through digital applications, cash back, and rewards. The partnership aims to combine technology and retail innovation, offering a more advanced and rewarding financial product to nearly two million existing Hudson's Bay credit card holders.

title: Walmart, Sam's Club pharmacies to begin COVID-19 vaccines Friday
summary: Walmart and Sam's Club pharmacies are set to begin administering COVID-19 vaccines on Friday across more than 1,000 locations in 22 states, focusing on underserved communities. This initiative is part of the Federal Retail Pharmacy Program, with Walmart aiming to deliver up to 13 million doses per month when supplies allow. The company emphasizes its commitment to providing vaccine access, particularly in rural and underserved areas, likening it to receiving a flu shot.

title: Agree Realty Sees Accelerated Growth by Investing in Top-Tier Net Lease Retail Assets
summary: Agree Realty has achieved accelerated growth by focusing on acquiring and developing net-leased properties with industry-leading retail tenants, resulting in a highly resilient portfolio, even during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company recorded record investment activity in 2020 and is strategically expanding its ground lease portfolio and partnering with top retailers. Analysts project continued strong FFO growth due to Agree Realty's robust balance sheet, cost of capital, and strategic execution.

title: Nicholas Kristof's chicken column misses the mark
summary: This article criticizes Nicholas Kristof's New York Times op-ed on animal agriculture, specifically targeting the chicken industry. The author argues that Kristof's piece, based mainly on information from an animal activist group, contains falsehoods and misleading statements regarding chicken welfare, breeding, and processing practices. The National Chicken Council and industry experts refute Kristof's claims, emphasizing the industry's commitment to animal welfare and the transparency efforts being made.

title: ALDI Sells Cheesecake Factory Pudding That Comes In Flavors Like Crème Brûlée And Cafe Mocha
summary: ALDI is selling Cheesecake Factory puddings in grocery stores, featuring complex flavors like crème brûlée and cafe mocha, inspired by their popular cheesecakes. Each cup costs about $1.69, allowing customers to enjoy the brand's desserts at home. These puddings contain milk, egg, and soy, and are found in ALDI's refrigerated section.

title: New Products Showcasing Side Dishes
summary: This article highlights new convenience-focused side dish products launched in February 2021, targeting consumer demand for quick, easy, and healthier meal solutions. Featured innovations include Green Giant's veggie fries and rings, Reser's single-serve chicken salad, Martha Stewart Kitchen's expanded line of frozen foods, La Tortilla Factory's microwaveable bean and rice dishes, and Idahoan's Honest Earth Mashed Sweet Potatoes. The products emphasize plant-based options, protein content, and clean labels to meet evolving consumer preferences.

title: Walmart temporarily closes hundreds of stores due to brutal winter storms
summary: Due to extreme winter storms causing widespread snow, ice, and dangerously low temperatures, Walmart announced the temporary closure of approximately 465 Walmart and Sam's Club stores. The retail giant prioritized the safety of its associates and customers, with its Emergency Operations Center monitoring the storms in real-time and providing updates through a publicly accessible map. The closures affected areas across the southern Plains, including Texas, and extended to the Gulf Coast.

title: Aramark, food service giant, joins 85 others to say no to genetically engineered salmon
summary: Aramark, one of America's largest food service companies, has agreed not to sell genetically engineered salmon, joining 85 other companies in a boycott campaign. This decision comes as AquaBounty, a biotech company, prepares to bring its AquAdvantage salmon to market in March. The genetically modified salmon, engineered to grow faster, faces significant opposition despite FDA approval, with consumer advocacy groups and environmentalists filing lawsuits and raising concerns about potential impacts on wild salmon populations and indigenous communities.

title: AC Brands' Emma Koehler Talks Sumo Citrus® Merchandising
summary: Emma Koehler, Assistant Brand Manager at AC Brands, shares merchandising strategies for Sumo Citrus to maximize sales, emphasizing eye-catching displays in high-traffic areas and separation from other citrus varieties. She highlights that Sumo Citrus, known for its unique size and shape and high Vitamin C content, has been on the market for 10 seasons. The company aims for consumers to discover this unique product during the winter months when health is a priority.

title: Fight for $15: US retailer Costco raises its hourly wage to $16
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp is increasing its minimum wage for hourly staff to $16, exceeding competitors Amazon and Target, and more than double the federal minimum wage. This move aligns with US President Joe Biden's plan to raise the minimum wage to $15 by 2025 and follows similar action by Walmart. The decision was announced by Costco's CEO Craig Jelinek at a Senate Budget Committee hearing, emphasizing the company's desire to retain employees, amidst broader debate on the federal minimum wage increase and its inclusion in the COVID-19 relief bill.

title: Five Below Planning to Open 5th Store in El Paso
summary: Discount retailer, Five Below, is expanding its presence in El Paso with a fifth store location at the Fountains at Farah. This new store will occupy the former Pier 1 Imports space and is anticipated to open in mid-June. Five Below primarily targets tweens, teens, and young adults with products mostly under $5, and some "extreme value items" priced at $10.

title: Costco is raising its minimum wage to $16 an hour for its U.S. store workers
summary: Costco is increasing its minimum hourly wage for U.S. store workers to $16, surpassing competitors like Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy. This decision comes as Congress debates a federal minimum wage increase to $15 an hour. The company previously instituted a $2 an hour premium during the pandemic, and this new raise converts part of that temporary premium into a permanent increase.

title: Costco raises minimum wage to $16 per hour
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp announced it will increase its minimum wage for hourly staff to $16 per hour, effective next week. This new wage is a dollar higher than what its major competitors, including Walmart, Amazon, and Target, currently pay their hourly employees. The move positions Costco with a leading minimum wage among large retailers.

title: Charlie Munger: It's 'absolute insanity' to think owning 100 stocks instead of five makes you a better investor
summary: Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway's vice-chairman, argues that owning a large number of stocks (e.g., 100) is "absolute insanity" and detrimental to investing success compared to focusing on a few well-understood companies. He champions "value investing" as always seeking more value than paid for and criticizes the wealth management industry's emphasis on diversification. Munger also shared how a charitable endowment he influenced achieved superior returns with just two assets: Li Lu's limited partnership and a Vanguard index fund.

title: Costco lifts minimum wage above Amazon or Target to $16 per hour
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp is raising its minimum wage for hourly staff to $16, surpassing competitors Amazon and Target. The decision was announced by CEO Craig Jelinek at a U.S. Senate Budget Committee hearing and comes as President Joe Biden aims to increase the federal minimum wage to $15 by 2025. Costco, which employs over 180,000 people in the U.S., had previously raised its minimum wage to $15 in 2019 and offered premium pay during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: US Retailer Costco to Base Fifth China Mall in Shenzhen
summary: US retailer Costco is expanding its presence in China by planning to open its fifth mega mall in Shenzhen, two years after its first store opened in Shanghai. Costco and Galaxy Holdings Group are investing CNY9 billion (USD1.4 billion) in the new mall and a regional head office. This expansion illustrates Costco's aggressive push into the Chinese market, despite lagging behind rival Sam's Club in terms of current store numbers.

title: Costco inks lease at Woodfield Preserve Office Center in Schaumburg
summary: Costco Wholesale Corporation and Costco Innovel Solutions have leased a 30,000-square-foot space at Woodfield Preserve Office Center in Schaumburg, with occupancy planned for April 2021. CBRE represented Zeller, the lessor, while Cushman & Wakefield represented Costco in the transaction. The office center has recently undergone significant renovations, including common area improvements, new amenities, and an upgraded outdoor courtyard.

title: Costco 4Q profits rise, helped by pandemic shopping habits
summary: Costco reported a slight rise in fourth-quarter profits, reaching $951 million or $2.14 per share, compared to $931 million or $2.10 per share a year earlier. This increase was driven by a surge in online shopping due to pandemic-related stocking up, with e-commerce revenues up 75%. However, profits were weighed down by wage premiums paid to employees during the pandemic, which trimmed profits by 41 cents per share, causing the results to fall below analysts' expectations.

title: Costco says it's spent more than $1B on Covid-related expenses
summary: Costco has reported spending over $1 billion on Covid-related expenses. This includes costs such as increased pay for employees, though a $2-per-hour premium recently ended, replaced by a permanent increase in starting wages to $16 per hour nationwide.

title: Urban Outfitters tests paid membership program to boost loyalty
summary: Urban Outfitters is testing a paid membership program called "UP" to boost customer loyalty, drive sales, and gather data. The program offers benefits across all its brands, including free shipping and discounts, and is being piloted in Atlanta and Dallas. This initiative aims to address declining sales post-pandemic and increase engagement in a competitive retail landscape.

title: Costco testing curbside pickup in Albuquerque
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is piloting curbside pickup services at three of its warehouses in Albuquerque. The company announced this initiative during its fiscal second-quarter earnings call, noting that the trial is progressing positively. This move follows rival BJ’s Wholesale, which launched its curbside pickup last year.

title: Kroger brings 80 Acres Farms vertically farmed produce to more stores
summary: Kroger is expanding its partnership with 80 Acres Farms to offer vertically farmed produce in over 300 stores across Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky, as well as online. This expansion follows a successful 15-month pilot and aligns with Kroger’s Zero Hunger | Zero Waste initiative. Other grocers, like Albertsons, are also increasing their offerings of vertically farmed produce, highlighting a growing trend in sustainable agriculture and fresh food accessibility.

title: City seeks foreclosure on CityGate properties; unpaid tax-related bills top $1.4M
summary: The City of Rochester is seeking to foreclose on several properties within the CityGate development due to over $1.4 million in unpaid tax-related bills. Developer Anthony J. Costello & Son, which built the shopping district, allegedly never paid its property taxes after its PILOT agreement was canceled in 2018. This action would give the city priority over other creditors amidst the developer's ongoing legal and financial troubles.

title: Sonos Car Audio and Other Surprises at Investor Event
summary: Sonos held a major investor event unveiling its new Roam portable speaker and providing a comprehensive overview of its financial performance and future strategy. The company is focusing on expanding its brand beyond the home into new categories like car audio, highlighted by a partnership with Audi, and gave optimistic financial guidance through 2024. Sonos believes its "software eating audio" approach and strong customer lifetime value will drive continued growth.

title: Mission Produce and Mr. Avocado send the first shipment of California avocados to China
summary: Mission Produce and China's Mr. Avocado have partnered to send the first-ever shipment of California avocados to China. This marks a significant expansion for Mission Produce, which was already sending avocados to China from Peru, Chile, and Colombia. The collaboration aims to provide a year-round supply of high-quality avocados to the Chinese market, leveraging California's premium late winter to early spring season.

title: 3 Stocks That Pass the Warren Buffett "Tides" Test
summary: This article identifies three companies, Microsoft, Costco, and American Express, that pass Warren Buffett's "tides test," meaning they are robust enough to perform well even during economic downturns. It discusses each company's business model, financial health, and reasons why they are considered strong, resilient investments, highlighting their ability to thrive amidst market volatility. The author suggests these stocks are suitable for those seeking safe-haven investments, especially during uncertain economic times.

title: Here's how much Wheels Up paid for each of its 5 acquisitions
summary: Wheels Up spent less than $100 million in cash to acquire five companies, building itself into the second-largest private jet operator with a $2 billion valuation ahead of its public offering via SPAC. The article details the cash, stock, and other considerations for each acquisition: Travel Management Company, Avianis Systems, Delta Private Jets, Gama Aviation, and Mountain Aviation. It reveals the financial breakdown of these strategic moves that transformed Wheels Up from a marketing organization into a major operator.

title: How Sam’s Club’s mobile app helped it compete during the pandemic
summary: Sam's Club leveraged its mobile app to gain a competitive edge during the pandemic, significantly outperforming Costco and BJ's Wholesale Club in app downloads and user ratings. Early investments in digital features like Scan & Go and curbside pickup, stemming from its role as a testbed for Walmart's digital initiatives, allowed Sam's Club to quickly adapt to changing consumer needs. The success is reflected in strong sales and membership growth, with plans for continued app expansion including virtual care services.

title: The Tiffany v. Costco Battle Wages On
summary: The legal battle between Tiffany and Costco over the use of the term "Tiffany Setting" continues, with the two companies now disputing punitive damages and Tiffany's right to a jury trial. After a federal appeals court vacated an earlier summary judgment and damages award in Tiffany's favor, the case has returned to a lower court where both sides are filing motions regarding the trial process and potential settlement discussions are ongoing.

title: General Mills Made the Whole ‘Shrimp in the Cereal’ Situation Way Worse
summary: A man found what appeared to be shrimp tails in his Cinnamon Toast Crunch cereal, leading to a viral social media exchange with General Mills. The company initially denied the claim, attributing the foreign objects to "cinnamon sugar accumulation," and later suggested it might be product tampering. This incident went viral largely due to General Mills' handling of the situation, drawing parallels to a past lawsuit where General Mills itself found shrimp pieces in blueberries they ordered.

title: Infrastructure work to start at Greenstone's Mead Works project
summary: Greenstone Corp. is set to begin infrastructure work later this year on its new Mead Works development, located on 420 acres north of Spokane. The project is expected to involve about $500 million in development over 20 years, including approximately 1,400 living units and 1 million square feet of retail space. The initial infrastructure phase, including roads and utilities, is anticipated to finish by late 2022, with vertical construction commencing next year.

title: Mitsui Chemicals’ MR™ High Refractive Index Ophthalmic Lens Monomers Picked Up by Costco as Standard Option for Glasses
summary: Mitsui Chemicals announced that Costco Wholesale Corp. has adopted its MR™ series of high refractive index lens monomers as the standard option for glasses. Costco, which previously offered mainly polycarbonate ophthalmic lenses, completed the full switch to Mitsui Chemicals' MR™ series in March 2021, recognizing the material's superior optical performance, lightness, and durability. Mitsui Chemicals aims to further expand the adoption of its MR™ series in the U.S. market, improving the "Quality of View" for consumers.

title: Kroger maps its new digital ‘ecosystem’
summary: Kroger plans to double its online sales to over $20 billion by the end of 2023, leveraging its Ocado automated customer fulfillment centers and expanding into new markets like Florida. The company aims to improve digital margins through technology, process improvements, and alternative profit streams, despite initial investor skepticism. Kroger is also focusing on enhancing its fresh assortment, private label offerings, and new meal options to drive market share.

title: Phoenix’s Paradise Valley Mall Will Become A Mixed-Use Development
summary: Macerich has sold its Paradise Valley Mall property in Phoenix for $100 million to a joint venture with RED Development. The 92-acre site, originally built in the 1970s, will be redeveloped into a mixed-use property featuring a grocery store, restaurants, residences, offices, and retail. This move reflects a broader trend among mall developers to diversify properties as traditional indoor shopping malls face declining foot traffic and increased online spending.

title: King Soopers reigns as Denver's top grocery store by market share
summary: King Soopers continued its dominance in the Denver area grocery market in 2020, holding the largest market share for at least the third consecutive year. The report by Chain Store Guide indicates that King Soopers, a Kroger subsidiary, increased its market share from the previous year. New grocery stores, including Sprouts Farmers Market and Costco, are expected to enter the competitive Denver market.

title: Costco to build first Houston-area Business Center in mixed-use district
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (Nasdaq: COST) is developing its first Houston-area Business Center in the Grid mixed-use redevelopment in Stafford, located at I-69 and Kirkwood Road. These Business Centers differ from traditional Costco stores by catering specifically to business customers and focusing on bulk-item sales.

title: Costco purchases land for first Houston-area Costco Business Center
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has acquired 13 acres in Stafford's Grid mixed-use development to establish its first Houston-area Costco Business Center, which is expected to open by the end of the year. This new center will cater to small businesses and is part of a larger 192-acre mixed-use development project on the former Texas Instruments campus. Local officials have expressed enthusiasm for the new addition, highlighting its expected benefits for the community and growing businesses.

title: AI Stock Picking Mutual Fund from IBM Watson
summary: This article features an interview with Chris Natividad, CIO and Co-Founder of EquBot, discussing AIEQ, the first AI-powered equity ETF. Developed in collaboration with IBM Watson, AIEQ utilizes AI to analyze vast amounts of investment data from over 5,000 U.S. companies daily, aiming to transform data into better investment outcomes. The system has shown strong performance, outperforming its benchmark and adapting to volatile market conditions like the COVID-19 pandemic by identifying appropriate investment opportunities.

title: Guide to Budget Rental Car's Fastbreak Program
summary: Budget Rent a Car's Fastbreak program is a free loyalty program that offers benefits like faster reservations, expedited car returns, and access to unique promotions and discounts. While it doesn't offer free rentals directly, members can earn rewards coupons (Budget Bucks) and accumulate points or miles with airline and hotel loyalty programs. The article also provides other tips for maximizing discounts on Budget rentals, such as using specific credit cards, linking an Amazon account, and comparing prices through third-party services like Costco Travel.

title: Aldi, Costco Among World's Most Reputable Companies
summary: Aldi and Costco have been recognized among the top 100 most reputable companies globally by RepTrak, making their first appearance on the list. The annual ranking, based on a survey of over 68,000 respondents, highlights the increasing importance of ESG initiatives and overall high reputation scores, especially in a challenging year. RepTrak's findings also show differences in perception across generations, with Millennials being the most positive and Gen Z the most skeptical.

title: The Biggest E-Commerce Players From China
summary: This article identifies the biggest e-commerce players in China, highlighting Alibaba's dominant position through Taobao and Tmall in terms of global merchandise volumes. JD.com is noted as Alibaba's closest domestic competitor, known for its drone delivery efforts. While Alibaba's newer global platform, AliExpress, exists, its sales do not match those of its regional Chinese platforms.

title: Naked Juice Rainbow Machine
summary: Naked Juice, a PepsiCo brand, has launched "Rainbow Machine," a new juice smoothie containing seven fruits and vegetables. This nutrient-rich blend provides vitamins B, C, E, calcium, and fiber, and is free of added sugar, gluten, and GMOs. Available in 15.2- and 64-ounce bottles, it can be found at major grocery retailers.

title: Why are McDonald’s restaurants leaving Walmart stores?
summary: McDonald’s is significantly reducing its presence in Walmart stores, downsizing from approximately 500 to 150 U.S. locations due to declining profitability and changing consumer habits accelerated by the pandemic. The shift reflects a growing preference for drive-thru and contactless options, making the in-store model less viable for McDonald's, while Walmart plans to repurpose the vacated spaces for diverse businesses and services.

title: The Honest Company Rides ‘Conscious Consumerism’ Wave Toward Potential $100M IPO
summary: The Honest Company, co-founded by Jessica Alba, has filed for an IPO aiming to list on Nasdaq under the symbol “HNST” with a valuation of $100 million. The ethical consumer goods brand, offering baby, beauty, and home cleaning products, saw significant revenue growth in 2020 but reported a net loss of $14.5 million and has yet to achieve profitability. The company is strategically positioned to capitalize on the increasing trend of conscious consumerism and plans to expand its e-commerce reach and international distribution.

title: 2 new Costco stores are in the works for Central Florida
summary: Two new Costco warehouses are planned for Central Florida, driven by the region's population growth. Construction has already started on a 156,000-square-foot warehouse in Brevard County's Viera community, following Costco's purchase of a 16.9-acre property for $6.7 million. This development marks Brevard County's first Costco location.

title: 2 Costco stores are in the works in Viera and Clermont
summary: Two new Costco warehouses are planned for Central Florida, specifically in Viera and Clermont. Each new Costco location typically creates over 300 jobs. This expansion highlights Clermont's appeal for large retail development.

title: How The Mastermind Behind LaCroix Puts The Fizz In Business
summary: This article from Investor's Business Daily highlights Nick Caporella, the driving force behind National Beverage, the company known for LaCroix sparkling water and other beverages. It notes how his strategies have resulted in a nearly $5 billion business, founded over 40 years ago with Shasta. The piece focuses on Caporella's ability to generate publicity and attention for his company.

title: Martin County Commission OKs Wawa, Tractor Supply Co. at former proposed Costco site in Palm City
summary: The Martin County Commission unanimously approved a new master site plan for a development in Palm City, replacing a previously proposed Costco site. The new plan includes a Wawa gas station, Tractor Supply Company, Aldi, a car wash, and undesignated hotel and retail space, with Wawa and Tractor Supply Co. expected to break ground around July. This development, known as Palm Pike Crossing, was approved after previous Costco plans faced significant local opposition and failed county review.

title: brekki Overnight Oats Expands Distribution
summary: brekki Overnight Oats has significantly expanded its distribution, adding Kroger, BJ's Wholesale Clubs, and Stop & Shop to its list of retail partners. This expansion is expected to bring the plant-based, ready-to-eat overnight oats brand to over 3,500 stores by the end of April 2021. The company attributes this growth to consumer demand for healthy, flexible, and plant-based snack and meal solutions.

title: Krispy Kreme-Glazed Popcorn Is Finally Available In The U.S.
summary: Smartfood's Krispy Kreme Original Glazed Doughnut flavored popcorn, previously available only in England, has launched in the U.S. This sweet and salty snack is available for a limited time at Sam's Club. The popcorn, which is certified gluten-free, combines the flavors of air-popped popcorn and Krispy Kreme's famous original glazed donuts.

title: USA Today Names Fresh Market, Hy-Vee, Lidl Best Supermarkets
summary: USA Today's 10Best Readers’ Choice Awards recognized The Fresh Market as the "Best Supermarket in America" for 2021, followed by Hy-Vee Inc. and Lidl U.S. in second and third place, respectively. The rankings were determined by a panel of local experts and contributors who nominated retailers based on value, selection, and service, with readers casting votes over a 28-day period. Aldi also received recognition, being named the No. 5 Best Supermarket and listed among the top 100 most reputable companies globally.

title: New Costco Requirement for All Shoppers Is Now in Effect
summary: Costco introduced new requirements for all shoppers, effective May 4, 2020, mandating face coverings for members and guests, with exemptions for children under 2 and those with medical conditions. Additionally, most warehouses and gas stations returned to regular hours, and special shopping hours were expanded for members aged 60 and older or with disabilities. Social distancing measures, including limiting the number of shoppers per membership card, also remained in effect, along with continued restrictions on returns for certain items.

title: How to get started reselling common products on EBay and other sites
summary: During the pandemic, many people began reselling common consumer products on sites like EBay due to financial concerns or excess items. This article provides a guide for aspiring resellers, addressing common questions about legality, sourcing products, and startup costs. It also highlights the increase in new sellers on platforms like EBay, which has partnered with liquidators to provide inventory.

title: Delta's stake in Wheels Up soars to $520 million
summary: Delta Air Lines' stake in Wheels Up has more than doubled to $520 million, making it Delta's largest equity ownership stake, surpassing its holdings in Korean Air and Air France-KLM. This valuation aligns with Wheels Up's planned SPAC merger at $2.1 billion. The article details Wheels Up's acquisition strategy under CEO Kenny Dichter and its goal to expand private aviation to a broader market segment.

title: Pots & Co accelerates US expansion plans with General Mills 301 INC backing
summary: Pots & Co, known for its upmarket desserts, is expanding its US presence with a significant investment of up to $20m from General Mills' venture arm, 301 INC. The company, founded by Julian Dyer, has seen substantial sales growth and is focused on bringing "restaurant-quality" desserts to the US market, despite initial challenges with distribution and market understanding. Dyer plans to eventually establish manufacturing facilities in the US and is committed to sustainable packaging solutions beyond plastics.

title: Viera's Lake Andrew Drive to open at Pineda Causeway near Costco construction site
summary: The Lake Andrew Drive extension in Viera, Florida, is set to open, connecting to the Pineda Causeway near a new Costco construction site. This $15.3 million road expansion improves access to Viera and opens up over 3,000 acres for future development, including a 156,000-square-foot Costco. The new roadway also provides a crucial north-south route linking key commercial areas and existing I-95 exits.

title: Plans for Scotts Valley Target head to Planning Commission
summary: The Scotts Valley Planning Commission is set to hold a public hearing on May 13 regarding plans for a new Target store. The Target will occupy the vacant 58,000-square-foot Kmart building at 270 Mount Hermon Road, a move Scotts Valley Mayor Derek Timm believes will be a significant uplift for the city both economically and visually. The project aims to re-energize the commercial plaza, though some local business owners and residents express concerns about increased traffic.

title: Jessica Alba-backed Honest Company IPO raises $412.8 mln
summary: Honest Company Inc, founded by actress Jessica Alba, raised $412.8 million in its initial public offering, pricing its shares slightly above the midpoint of its indicated range at $16 each. The IPO values Honest at $1.44 billion, with the company offering 6.5 million shares and existing stockholders offering 19.4 million shares. Honest sells baby and household products and will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol "HNST".

title: Jessica Alba-backed Honest Company IPO raises $412.8 million
summary: The Honest Company, co-founded by actress Jessica Alba, has priced its initial public offering, raising $412.8 million. The company sold 25.8 million shares at $16 each, valuing Honest at $1.44 billion. Honest, known for its baby and household products, faced scrutiny in 2016 over ingredient labeling.

title: Jessica Alba's Honest Co valued near $2 billion in strong market debut
summary: Jessica Alba's Honest Co (HNST.O) made a strong debut on the Nasdaq, with its shares trading 37.5% higher than the IPO price, valuing the company at approximately $2 billion. Alba, who co-founded the company in 2011, stated that becoming public would fuel product innovation and consumer accessibility for their eco-friendly baby products, vitamins, and sanitizers. Despite a previous lawsuit and never having turned a profit, the company saw a 28% surge in revenue to $300 million last year, with narrowing losses.

title: The Honest Company Founder Jessica Alba Rings The Bell
summary: Lightspeed Venture Partners celebrates The Honest Company's IPO, reflecting on its journey from a mission-driven startup founded by Jessica Alba in 2011 to a public company. The article highlights the company's initial rapid growth, subsequent challenges, and its return to profitability under CEO Nick Vlahos's leadership. Lightspeed expresses pride in supporting Honest Company's commitment to clean and conscious innovation.

title: Jessica Alba's Honest Co. surges in Nasdaq debut
summary: Jessica Alba's eco-friendly personal care brand, Honest Co. (HNST), saw its shares surge 44% in its Nasdaq debut, closing at $23 per share and giving the company a market value of about $2.1 billion. CEO Nick Vlahos viewed the successful IPO as validation of the company's mission-driven strategy focused on clean, sustainable, and socially responsible products. Despite its growth in sales to over $300 million in 2020 and narrowing net losses, the company has not yet turned a profit and has previously faced controversial lawsuits regarding its product labeling.

title: Confirmed: Costco buys south Orlando office building for subsidiary
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has purchased an office building in south Orlando for its subsidiary, Innovel Solutions. This acquisition marks a significant commitment to the Orlando market by Innovel Solutions, which will be opening an office there. The move indicates new growth and investment in the region.

title: Walmart, Tesla Added to S&P ESG Index, While Victoria's Secret-Owner and Facebook Get the Boot
summary: The S&P 500's ESG Index underwent its annual adjustments, adding 45 stocks including Tesla, Disney, Walmart, and Etsy, while dropping 21 companies such as Facebook, Victoria's Secret-owner L Brands, and Costco. Tesla was included due to its clean energy efforts, and Walmart for improvements in human rights. Facebook was removed for deteriorating environmental reporting, and L Brands for poor ESG performance compared to peers.

title: Graphic: Here’s where gas prices are increasing the most
summary: Gas prices are surging in the South due to the Colonial Pipeline shutdown, with Georgia and South Carolina experiencing nearly 10 percent increases. The national average breached $3 per gallon for the first time in seven years. Drivers are urged to be patient and only purchase necessary fuel as the pipeline restarts operations.

title: Costco will not require fully vaccinated customers to wear masks
summary: Costco announced it will no longer require fully vaccinated customers to wear masks. This decision follows new guidance from the CDC and an easing of mask restrictions by Washington Gov. Jay Inslee. The change reflects a broader trend of businesses adapting their mask policies in response to updated public health recommendations.

title: Target, CVS, Starbucks and other retailers ease mask mandates for fully vaccinated customers
summary: Following updated guidance from the CDC, retailers like Target, CVS, Starbucks, Walmart, and Costco are easing mask mandates for fully vaccinated customers, unless local laws dictate otherwise. While many companies are adjusting policies, some like Home Depot and Gap are maintaining precautions. The shift has sparked debate, with concerns about unvaccinated individuals potentially going maskless and the differential impact on employees, as some companies continue to require masks for their staff.

title: Target adding beer, wine and alcohol for curbside and in-store pickup at 1,200 stores
summary: Target is expanding its curbside and in-store pickup services to include beer, wine, and other alcoholic beverages at over 1,200 stores across 29 states by the end of May. This expansion follows successful pilots and significant digital growth in the adult beverage category, aligning with the retailer's goal to make shopping more convenient. The announcement also coincided with Target dropping its mask requirement for fully vaccinated customers.

title: Starbucks, Chipotle drop mask rule for vaxxed customers
summary: Starbucks and Chipotle Mexican Grill have lifted their mask mandates for fully vaccinated customers, following updated guidance from the CDC. McDonald's, however, is still reviewing its policy but is consulting with the Mayo Clinic. This move by major retailers reflects dropping coronavirus infection rates and increasing vaccination levels across the U.S.

title: 1st Cir.: Job description key in Costco’s triumph over ADA claims
summary: The 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in favor of Costco in an ADA discrimination case, finding that the company did not discriminate against a pregnant worker by placing her on temporary leave. The court emphasized the importance of a detailed job description, noting that the employee's doctor-imposed restrictions prevented her from performing essential functions, such as lifting 50 pounds, outlined in her job role. This case highlights how job descriptions are crucial in determining essential job functions in discrimination claims.

title: Kohl's joins Target and Walmart in ending mask requirement for fully vaccinated customers
summary: Kohl's has announced it will no longer require fully vaccinated customers to wear face coverings in its stores, aligning with other major retailers like Target and Walmart. This change follows new CDC guidelines stating that fully vaccinated individuals generally do not need to wear masks indoors. Kohl's will still encourage unvaccinated customers and associates to wear masks and will adhere to local mask mandates.

title: Costco strengthens position atop wholesale club sector
summary: Costco is increasing its dominance in the wholesale club sector, capturing 55.4% of visits in March, a rise of over 3 percentage points from the previous year. This growth highlights Costco's resilience and improved market standing post-pandemic, even as its competitors Sam's Club and BJ's Wholesale Club saw their market shares decline in March 2021. The overall wholesale retail sector is showing strength, with increased foot traffic across all major clubs, indicating a return to more normal consumer behaviors and a strong position for these retailers in an uncertain economy.

title: Masks optional: Kroger stores lift mask requirement for vaccinated customers
summary: Kroger announced it is lifting its mask mandate for vaccinated customers and most vaccinated associates starting May 20, aligning with CDC guidance. Non-vaccinated individuals and pharmacy/clinic employees will still be required to wear masks. Other major retailers like Walmart, Target, Home Depot, and Aldi are also making masks optional for vaccinated customers, while some, like Jungle Jim's and Whole Foods, continue to require them.

title: Sprouts sets opening date, hiring for new north Phoenix store
summary: Sprouts is preparing to open a new 25,000-square-foot store in the Deer Valley Center shopping plaza in north Phoenix. The store will be located at 43rd Avenue and Thunderbird Road, taking over the former Cotton Cactus space. Sprouts is currently hiring for positions at this new location.

title: Costco project, with 398 apartment units, gets first approval from Stuart City Commission
summary: The Stuart City Commission has given its initial approval to a controversial Costco project that includes a warehouse store, gas station, and a 398-unit apartment complex. The unanimous decision came after eight hours of discussion, but developers must meet over a dozen conditions before a final vote. The project is proposed for South Kanner Highway and also includes retail and restaurant space.

title: Costco Q3 FY 2021 Earnings Report Preview: What to Look For
summary: This article previews Costco's Q3 FY 2021 earnings report, highlighting analyst expectations for robust growth in EPS and revenue, driven by increased customer spending during the pandemic. A key focus will be on comparable sales growth, projected to be the fastest in over four years, indicating continued strength in the retailer's existing sales channels. The report also notes Costco's stock performance relative to the S&P 500 and its recovery from an early March low.

title: Luxury Goods Sales Projected to Recover to 2019 Levels This Year
summary: A new report from Bain & Company projects global luxury goods sales to fully recover to 2019 levels this year, with a 30% probability of exceeding $340 billion. This optimistic forecast is driven by strong economic rebounds in China and the United States, propelled by swift vaccine distribution and increased disposable income. The article highlights the U.S. Global Investors' Global Luxury Goods Fund (USLUX) as an attractive way to capitalize on this recovery, benefiting from the spending habits of affluent consumers, particularly in Asia.

title: Costco's free samples are finally making a comeback
summary: Costco is bringing back free food samples to its stores, with a phased return starting in early June across 170 U.S. locations and most others by the end of the month. The samples will be distributed with increased safety protocols, including plexiglass partitions, smaller batches, and one-customer-at-a-time service. Additionally, Costco's food courts will also see indoor seating return next month, though tables will be downsized for more physical separation.

title: Snackers rejoice! Costco to bring back free samples
summary: Costco is set to bring back free food samples to its stores in a phased approach starting in early June, after a 14-month hiatus due to the pandemic. The return will include increased safety protocols, such as samples prepared behind plexiglass and distributed one at a time. Additionally, Costco is reopening indoor seating at its food courts with more physical separation, introducing new churros, and replacing frozen yogurt with new ice cream.

title: Food Sampling Back At Michigan Costco’s; Will You Take A Bite?
summary: Costco stores in Michigan and nationwide are reintroducing food samples on toothpicks in June, a popular feature that was suspended due to the pandemic. While shoppers appreciate the return of these "vital sustenance" samples, the author raises questions about safety and a return to normalcy, also considering the future of buffets and smorgasbords.

title: Target is reopening fitting rooms after keeping them closed more than a year amid COVID-19
summary: Target has started reopening its fitting rooms across all stores, with most expected to be operational by Tuesday after being closed for over a year due to the coronavirus pandemic. This decision follows updated CDC guidelines on masks for vaccinated individuals and comes as other retailers, like Kohl's, also reopen their dressing rooms to improve the shopping experience. Target assures customers that frequent disinfection and cleaning protocols will remain in place, with a small number of fitting rooms potentially still used for vaccinations.

title: Target joins list of retailers reopening dressing rooms
summary: Target has announced the reopening of its fitting rooms, joining other retailers like Gap, Nordstrom, and Kohl's in signaling a return to pre-pandemic operations. This move comes as more Americans are vaccinated, leading to relaxed mask-wearing guidance and increased in-store shopping. Retailers are implementing continued cleaning protocols to ensure customer safety.

title: Sampling Makes Triumphant Return to Sam’s Club
summary: Sam's Club has relaunched its Taste & Tips sampling program nationwide, signaling a return to pre-pandemic shopping experiences. Initially, the program will operate on weekends with new safety measures, including sealed samples. In addition to in-club sampling, Sam's Club is introducing the Member’s Mark Summer Eats Food Truck which will tour the central U.S. and testing new roaming sampling events.

title: Costco is bringing back its sample stations this week
summary: Costco is reintroducing food sampling stations at 170 of its 550 locations, 14 months after suspending them due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
