Sam's Club is also bringing back sampling at all 600 of its stores with sealed samples and limited quantities. Health experts advise caution, especially for unvaccinated individuals, suggesting masks be kept on as much as possible and proper precautions from sample distributors.

title: Little Rock Costco applies for liquor license
summary: Costco has applied for a liquor license for its new West Little Rock location, currently only permitted to sell beer and wine. The United Beverage Retailers Association, primarily composed of liquor store owners, is opposing the application, citing competitive disadvantage and sufficient existing liquor stores. The Alcohol Beverage Control board is scheduled to review the matter on June 16th.

title: Report: Chipotle raises prices to cover increase in worker pay
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill has raised its menu prices by approximately 4% to help cover the cost of increasing employee wages to an average of $15 per hour. The company announced its intention to raise worker pay in May and had indicated that these costs would be passed on to customers. While ingredient costs are also rising across the industry, Chipotle is not currently planning further price increases to offset those specific costs.

title: How the return of in-store sampling is going over with consumers
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of in-store sampling, particularly focusing on food items, and how American consumers are responding to it post-pandemic. It highlights that people are now more inclined to sample food in stores compared to before the pandemic, as illustrated by an image of an employee distributing samples at Costco.

title: Kroger sees strong private label, digital sales even as pandemic surge fades
summary: Kroger reported a decline in identical-store and overall sales in Q1 2021 compared to the pandemic-fueled surge of Q1 2020, but showed significant growth when compared to Q1 2019. Despite the overall decline, the company saw strong digital sales growth and momentum in its private label business. Kroger is optimistic about continued consumer shifts favoring at-home cooking and premium products, and plans to double its digital business in the coming years.

title: Americans are dining out again. Target wants to lure them to the grocery aisle with deals
summary: Target is adding food and beverages to its Deal Days sales event, aiming to attract consumers back to its grocery aisles even as dining out resumes. This strategic move, which includes discounts and a gift card promotion, marks the first time Target is using the event to promote groceries, a category that significantly boosted its sales during the pandemic. The initiative is a direct response to Amazon Prime Day and reflects a broader effort by grocers like Walmart and Amazon to retain elevated grocery spending amidst shifting consumer habits.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club planning first Indiana store on area’s north side
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club is planning to open its first Indiana location in Noblesville, submitting construction plans for a 105,000-square-foot store, parking lot, and gas station. The proposed store, located on Tegler Drive, is currently undergoing revisions based on city feedback. BJ's is the third-largest warehouse club chain in the U.S., joining competitors like Sam's Club and Costco that already have a significant presence in the Indianapolis area.

title: Kroger Urged to Eliminate Pesticides from Supply Chain
summary: Environmental and consumer groups are pressuring Kroger to remove toxic pesticides from its food supply chain, citing pollinator declines and adverse human health impacts. On the eve of Kroger's annual shareholder meeting, the coalition highlighted that Kroger lags behind competitors like Walmart in pesticide reduction commitments, and their own store-brand foods contain harmful chemicals. They urge Kroger to expand organic offerings and adopt sustainable practices to protect pollinators and ensure consumer health.

title: LAURA ALBER NAMED TO BARRON’S TOP CEO LIST 2021
summary: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. President and CEO Laura Alber has been named to Barron’s Top CEO List 2021, recognized for guiding the company through the COVID-19 pandemic with robust e-commerce and relevant products. The list highlights leaders who successfully positioned their companies for future growth, with Barron's also acknowledging Williams-Sonoma's commitment to gender equity and environmental sustainability, including a goal of carbon neutrality by 2025.

title: How To Watch The Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest On July 4th
summary: The Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest is an annual American tradition held on July 4th at Coney Island. The article details the contest's rules, scoring, tie-breaking procedures, and historical folklore, noting that it will be broadcast on ESPN. It also highlights accomplished champions like Joey Chestnut and Miki Sudo.

title: Lifeway Foods Announces Expansion into French Market
summary: Lifeway Foods, Inc. has expanded its distribution into the French market, with its mango Lifeway Kefir now available at Costco France. This move positions the U.S. kefir leader to capitalize on the growing global kefir market, projected to reach $1.23 billion USD by 2027. The company aims to replicate its domestic success through this international expansion, supported by local marketing efforts.

title: 2021 State of the Beverage Industry: Bottled water bubbling over with growth
summary: This article details the continued growth of the bottled water industry in 2021, highlighting its expansion even during the COVID-19 pandemic. It emphasizes the role of health and wellness attributes, convenience, and the increasing popularity of sparkling and enhanced waters in driving this growth. The report includes sales figures and insights from industry experts on market trends and innovation within the water category.

title: Judge Releases Pharmacies and Retailers from Zantac Multidistrict Litigation
summary: A federal judge in Florida has dismissed pharmacies and retailers, including Albertsons, Walgreens, CVS, and Amazon, from the Zantac multidistrict litigation. The judge ruled that consumers failed to provide sufficient evidence that these companies' negligence caused the formation of carcinogens in Zantac or that they improperly stored the drug. The lawsuit, which began in 2019 after the FDA found cancer-causing NDMA in Zantac, will continue against brand name manufacturers and generic-drug makers.

title: Costco vs. Sam's Club vs. BJ's: Which wholesale club is best for you?
summary: This article compares Costco, Sam's Club, and BJ's, helping consumers decide which wholesale club best suits their needs. It details membership fees, perks, and the number of U.S. locations for each, highlighting how wholesale clubs offer lower markups compared to traditional retailers. The analysis aims to show if the annual membership fees are justified by the potential savings and benefits.

title: Target shortens hours in San Francisco due to ‘alarming rise’ in shoplifting
summary: Target has temporarily reduced operating hours at its five San Francisco store locations due to a significant and alarming increase in theft and security incidents. This move comes as other retailers in the area report similar issues, prompting Target to engage local law enforcement and officials to address the growing problem. The California Retailers Association notes that this is an ongoing issue that is now gaining national attention.

title: Surviving And Thriving –
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. continues to be a dominant force in beverage alcohol retail, especially amid the Covid-19 pandemic and a change in leadership. The company's global beverage alcohol sales topped $5 billion in 2020, doubling since 2010. Wine comprises half of these sales, followed by spirits and beer, with proprietary Kirkland Signature items being top performers.

title: Costco is coming to Queen Creek
summary: Costco Wholesale is set to open a new warehouse in Queen Creek, expanding its presence in the Valley. This new location, expected in 2022, signifies a significant development for the far East Valley area.

title: Costco in Viera: Excitement builds as walls start going up at wholesale warehouse site
summary: Construction is progressing on the new Costco Wholesale store in Viera, generating significant excitement among residents and community leaders. The store is expected to open in the fall and is seen as a major economic boost, bringing high-wage jobs and anchoring a new phase of retail development in the Pineda Interchange District. Costco purchased the 16.9-acre site for $6.65 million and its opening is anticipated to spur further commercial and residential growth in the Viera master-planned community.

title: Tiffany, Costco settle 8-year lawsuit over fake 'Tiffany' rings
summary: Tiffany & Co. and Costco Wholesale Corp. have settled an eight-year-old lawsuit regarding Costco's sale of diamond engagement rings labeled with the "Tiffany" name. The settlement follows a federal appeals court overturning a $21 million judgment Tiffany previously won. Terms of the settlement were not disclosed.

title: Costco Settles Longtime Dispute Over ‘Tiffany’ Diamond Rings
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. and Tiffany and Co. have agreed to settle a lawsuit that began in 2013 regarding Costco's sale of "Tiffany" diamond engagement rings. Tiffany had initially sued Costco, alleging trademark violation. The settlement was announced to U.S. District Judge Lewis Liman, leading to the dismissal of the long-running case.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock rises Tuesday, still underperforms market
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) shares increased by 0.95% to $226.41 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market's strong performance, with the S&P 500 rising 1.52% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 1.62%. This marked the stock's sixth consecutive day of gains and a new 52-week high for the company. Despite the rise, it showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Walmart, Costco, and Target, which also saw gains.

title: Tiffany, Costco settle 8-year lawsuit over fake 'Tiffany' rings
summary: Tiffany & Co. and Costco Wholesale Corp. have settled an eight-year-old lawsuit regarding trademark infringement and counterfeiting. The dispute centered on Costco selling generic diamond engagement rings labeled with the "Tiffany" name. The settlement, for which terms were not disclosed, comes after a federal appeals court overturned a previous $21 million judgment in Tiffany's favor.

title: Tiffany, Costco Settle Long-Standing Lawsuit
summary: Tiffany & Co. and Costco Wholesale Corp. have settled an eight-year-long trademark infringement lawsuit regarding Costco's sale of "Tiffany" rings not made by Tiffany. The terms of the settlement were not disclosed, and the case was dismissed with prejudice, preventing Tiffany from re-suing Costco on the same grounds. The legal battle involved rulings in Tiffany's favor, monetary awards, and subsequent appeals.

title: Costco to try out same-day delivery with Uber in Texas
summary: Costco is launching a pilot program for same-day delivery with Uber in select stores in Texas. This initiative marks another foray into same-day delivery services for the Issaquah-based wholesaler. The Puget Sound Business Journal reported on this development.

title: Uber's trucking unit to buy logistics planner Transplace for $2.25 bln
summary: Uber's trucking unit, Uber Freight, is acquiring transportation logistics company Transplace for approximately $2.25 billion from TPG Capital. This acquisition, comprising up to $750 million in Uber stock and the rest in cash, is expected to accelerate Uber Freight's path to profitability. The deal marks a strategic move for Uber, which has recently divested capital-intensive businesses, as it doubles down on its logistics and delivery services.

title: Websites back up after brief global outage linked to Akamai
summary: Many websites experienced a global outage for about an hour due to a glitch in Akamai Technologies Inc.'s systems, specifically a bug in its domain name system (DNS) service triggered during a software update. Akamai quickly implemented a fix by rolling back the update, confirming the disruption was not a cyberattack. This incident marked the second significant disruption linked to Akamai in approximately a month, affecting major sites including Delta Air Lines, Costco, American Express, and Home Depot.

title: Costco to close a Cincinnati-area location when newest store opens
summary: Costco Wholesale plans to close one of its Cincinnati-area locations when its new Liberty Township warehouse opens in 2022. This move is part of the bulk retailer's strategy as it expands its presence in the region. The article mentions related developments, including a $150M mixed-use project anchored by Costco.

title: Kroger Unveils the Future of Grocery in Florida
summary: Kroger has opened a new robotic fulfillment center in Groveland, Florida, marking its significant expansion into the Florida market without traditional stores. This 375,000-sq.-ft. facility, operational since March, is exceeding expectations and is part of Kroger's strategy to double its online business by 2023. The center utilizes advanced technology from Ocado and serves as a hub in a spoke model aimed at eventually covering all of South Florida.

title: Floor & Decor opens in former Target store in Commack
summary: Floor & Decor has opened its second Long Island store in Commack, occupying most of a former Target space. The Atlanta-based retailer plans at least two more stores on Long Island in Bohemia and Garden City, reflecting the home improvement industry's growth. The new 95,000-square-foot store employs about 50 workers and is located at 4 Henry St. in the Commack South Shopping Center.

title: Alabama utilities declare war on ‘flushable wipes’; fatbergs cause costly sewer system clogs
summary: Alabama utilities are confronting a major issue caused by so-called "flushable wipes," which are creating massive clogs known as "fatbergs" in sewer systems, leading to costly damage and environmental spills. Despite being marketed as flushable, these wipes do not disintegrate like toilet paper and contribute to an estimated $441 million in additional operational costs annually for wastewater utilities nationwide. Utility operators are launching public education campaigns and pursuing legal action, like a class-action lawsuit in Charleston, South Carolina, to mandate proper labeling and ensure wipes genuinely dissolve in water.

title: Uber, Lyft seen boosted by return of riders, but driver shortage, stubborn virus cloud outlook
summary: Ride-hailing companies Uber and Lyft are expected to show revenue rebounds in their second-quarter results, driven by reopening economies and cost-cutting measures taken during the pandemic. However, concerns about a persistent driver shortage and the spread of the Delta variant are clouding their outlook for achieving profitability this year. Both companies have been offering incentives to attract drivers, but rider demand continues to outpace supply, and the ongoing pandemic uncertainty poses a significant challenge to their financial targets.

title: Formula 1's Skyrocketing Popularity
summary: Formula 1 is experiencing a significant surge in popularity and revenue, with viewership increasing by 36% compared to the 2019 season and first-quarter revenue reaching $180 million in 2021. This growth is attributed in part to Netflix's "Drive to Survive" series and strategic partnerships. The article also touches on World Rugby's discussions with private equity firms, Clemson University taking its multimedia rights in-house, and NHL player Evander Kane denying gambling allegations.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) stock closed down 0.06% at $234.90 on Wednesday, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 fall 0.46% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average drop 0.92%. Despite the daily loss, the stock ended just $1.53 shy of its 52-week high achieved the previous day. Other competitors like Walmart Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., and Target Corp. also experienced declines.

title: Uber posts $509 mln adjusted loss on driver incentives even as trips rise
summary: Uber Technologies Inc reported widening losses of $509 million in the second quarter due to increased spending on driver incentives to meet rising trip demand. Despite the loss and ongoing driver shortages, Uber management expressed confidence in achieving profitability by the end of the year, driven by strong growth in both ride-hailing and food delivery segments. The company's shares fell 5% in after-hours trading following the announcement.

title: Proposed El Dorado Hills Costco store in county review
summary: El Dorado County officials are beginning the environmental review process for a proposed Costco store in El Dorado Hills. This would be the county's first Costco Wholesale Corp. store and is planned as part of a larger retail development on Silva Valley Parkway.

title: Long-awaited, long-debated, Costco wholesale store gets OK from Stuart City Commission
Costco to open its doors tomorrow
summary: Costco is set to open its new 160,000-square-foot store in Springfield, Missouri, marking a significant development for the city that has long sought its presence. The store, managed by Angela Bauer, will feature a wide range of products including organic items, a food court, tire center, travel agent, vision center, and a gas station. City officials and Costco's CEO, W. Craig Jelinek, will be present for the grand opening, celebrating the company's $166.8 billion revenue and 180 local employees earning an average of $25.50 per hour.

title: Economist Casey Mulligan: Employer-Sponsored Insurance is the 'Vital Centerpiece of American Health Care'
summary: Economist Casey Mulligan, a former chief economist at the White House Council of Economic Advisors, emphasizes the critical role of employer-sponsored health insurance in the American healthcare system. He highlights its significant value to both employees and employers, estimating it to be 75% to 84% above its cost, contributing $800 billion annually. Mulligan argues that this system fosters a healthier economy, encourages work, and offers substantial benefits compared to alternatives.

title: United Fresh Introduces Class 26 of the Produce Industry Leadership Program
summary: The United Fresh Produce Association has announced the members of Class 26 of its Produce Industry Leadership Program, sponsored by Corteva Agriscience™. This class includes 12 rising leaders from various fresh produce companies who will participate in a year-long fellowship focusing on leadership development, business relationships, government and public affairs, and media communications. The program will include educational events, hands-on training, and trips, starting with the United Fresh Washington Conference in September.

title: PNC raises hourly minimum wage to $18 amid labor shortage
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. announced it will raise its hourly minimum wage to $18 from $15, effective November 22, 2021, to address labor shortages. This increase will also apply to staff from Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria SA who will join PNC after its acquisition of the Spanish bank's U.S. business in October. With this acquisition, PNC is set to become the fifth-largest U.S. bank.

title: Costco Joins Chicken Antitrust Class-action Complaint
summary: Costco Wholesale Corporation has filed a lawsuit against major poultry producers, joining a multidistrict litigation. The suit alleges that poultry producers engaged in an illegal scheme to fix chicken prices from 2008 to 2019, restraining trade, reducing supply, and rigging bids. Costco is represented by several law firms, and the case involves defendants like Koch Foods, OK Foods Inc., and Sanderson Farms, with some companies already settling related class-action suits.

title: More Sephora at Kohl's locations opening ahead of Labor Day. See which stores are getting a makeover.
summary: Kohl's is expanding its partnership with Sephora by opening 78 new Sephora at Kohl's locations in September 2021, ahead of the Labor Day sale, in addition to the 77 stores that opened in August. The ambitious plan aims to have Sephora departments in 200 Kohl's stores by fall 2021, 400 more in 2022, and ultimately over 850 of Kohl's 1,150+ stores by 2023. These "store-within-a-store" concepts will replace Kohl's existing beauty sections, offering approximately 125 brands and over 8,500 products, with shoppers able to earn loyalty benefits from both Kohl's Rewards and Sephora Beauty Insider, though Sephora products are excluded from Kohl's coupons and Kohl's Cash.

title: CIBC strikes deal to be sole issuer of Costco Mastercards in Canada
summary: CIBC has secured a multiyear deal to become the sole issuer of Costco-branded Mastercards in Canada, acquiring the existing credit card portfolio from Capital One. This move is part of CIBC's broader strategy to revamp its consumer banking and enhance its credit card market share, which also involves increasing loyalty and cross-selling opportunities by targeting Costco's millions of members. The deal represents a significant shift in the Canadian credit card landscape amid changing customer preferences, new regulations, and increased competition from fintech companies.

title: CIBC to purchase Costco credit card portfolio in Canada
summary: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) has announced its agreement to acquire the Canadian Costco credit card portfolio, which boasts over $3bn in outstanding balances. This acquisition includes a long-term agreement for CIBC to be the exclusive issuer of Costco Mastercards in Canada, replacing the current issuer, Capital One. The deal is expected to close in early 2022, after which CIBC will issue new co-branded Mastercards offering enhanced rewards and doubling as Costco membership cards.

title: CIBC to acquire Costco co-brand credit card portfolio in Canada
summary: The Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) has agreed to acquire Costco's co-brand credit card portfolio in Canada, holding over C$3bn in outstanding balances. Upon closing in early 2022, CIBC will become the exclusive issuer of Costco Mastercards in Canada, aiming to enhance rewards and grow its market share in payments. This partnership will also integrate the new CIBC Costco Mastercard with Costco's membership card, offering expanded benefits to members.

title: Stamford-based furniture maker Lovesac sees ‘huge gains’ in 2021
summary: Stamford-based furniture maker Lovesac reported significant growth in the quarter ending August 1, 2021, with sales up 65% year over year to approximately $102 million and a profit of $8.4 million. This rebound follows temporary showroom closures due to COVID-19, with strong performance attributed to increased brand awareness and the reopening of all stores. The company, known for its Sactionals and Sacs, saw showroom sales jump 387% and plans for 28 new store openings in 2021, despite a decrease in internet sales as customers returned to physical locations.

title: Kroger gets hit by higher costs, theft—even as shoppers fill up grocery carts
summary: Kroger reported that shoppers continued to purchase large quantities of groceries in the fiscal second quarter, leading to sustained sales levels. Despite this, the company's shares fell due to investor concerns over shrinking profit margins driven by inflation, increased theft, and higher supply chain costs. JPMorgan analyst Ken Goldman suggested Kroger should pass on more costs to consumers rather than absorb them, especially given the stock's significant run-up during the pandemic.

title: Costco gets underway on $160M regional distribution center in Tumwater
summary: Costco has begun construction on a new $160 million regional distribution center in Tumwater, Washington. The 1.1 million-square-foot facility will be Costco's largest in the region upon its completion next year. This development highlights Costco's expanding logistical footprint and investment in the Puget Sound area.

title: Warby Parker Direct Listing: See Through This Optical Illusion
summary: This article analyzes Warby Parker's upcoming direct listing, valuing the company at $3 billion, which the author deems "very unattractive." The author argues that this valuation is an "optical illusion" as Warby Parker lacks consistent profitability, has a small market share in a fragmented industry, and faces challenges with its e-commerce strategy and costly retail expansion plans. The article details several financial and governance-related red flags for potential investors.

title: Costco’s stock set up to fall after earnings, and that’s the time to buy it, analyst says
summary: An analyst at Oppenheimer, Rupesh Parikh, suggests that Costco's stock is poised for a dip after its upcoming earnings report, despite strong sales trends. Parikh believes this post-earnings decline would present a buying opportunity for investors, as the current positive trends are already factored into the stock price. He advises investors to capitalize on any profit-taking that may occur.

title: InnerScope Hearing Technologies (OTC: INND) to Participate in the Virtual Home Health & Diabetes Care Program, Sept. 20–23, 2021
summary: InnerScope Hearing Technologies (OTC: INND) is participating in the virtual Home Health & Diabetes Care Program from September 20–23, 2021. The company is the only one presenting direct-to-consumer hearing devices and health products to 50 buyers from major U.S. retailers like CVS, Costco, and Kroger. InnerScope aims to build its distribution network and showcase its affordable, innovative hearing solutions to potential strategic partners.

title: Costco Q4 FY2021 Earnings Report Preview: What to Look For
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) is set to release its Q4 FY2021 earnings, with analysts anticipating robust growth in EPS and revenue, albeit at a slower pace than the previous quarter. Key metrics to watch include comparable sales growth, which is expected to expand at a healthy pace despite deceleration from Q3. The company's strong performance has been driven by increased consumer purchases of food and home goods amid the pandemic and the Delta variant, though rising costs due to supply chain issues could impact future profit margins.

title: H-E-B-anchored shopping center changes hands
summary: A shopping center in Austin, Texas, anchored by an H-E-B grocery store, was sold on September 20. The Springdale Shopping Center, located near the intersection of U.S. Highways 183 and 290, now has a new owner, marking the entry of a new player into the local real estate market. The article promises more details on the transaction and a list of the region's largest retail centers.

title: Costco growth hits highest annual totals since 1990s after record quarterly profit, revenue
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported its highest annual growth in profit and sales since the 1990s, driven by the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings reached $1.67 billion on sales of $61.44 billion, marking the first time it surpassed $60 billion in quarterly sales. This performance highlights Costco's strong financial year and rapid expansion.

title: Why Costco is rationing toilet paper and paper towels again, and what it says about supply chains everywhere
summary: Costco is once again imposing limits on the purchase of certain high-demand items, including toilet paper, paper towels, and bottled water, due to a surge in demand driven by the delta variant of COVID-19. This situation echoes the supply chain disruptions experienced in early 2020. The company's CFO, Richard Galanti, confirmed these new limitations during a recent earnings call.

title: Shamrock Foods Co.
summary: Shamrock Foods Co. is ranked 14th on the 2021 Distributor 15 list. The company specializes in manufacturing and distributing food and food-related products through its foodservice distributor Shamrock Foods and dairy operation Shamrock Farms. Headquartered in Phoenix, Ariz., Shamrock Foods Co. reported a U.S. sales volume of $3.9 billion.

title: Costco files early plans for Seattle store in old Sam's Club space
summary: Costco has filed early plans to open a new store in Seattle, taking over a former Sam's Club location at 13550 Aurora Ave. N. This new Seattle store would complement other upcoming Washington state Costco locations in Lake Stevens and Pasco, marking a regional expansion for the retailer.

title: HP’s Smartest Ink Tank Printer For People That Print A Lot
summary: HP Inc. has launched the new low-cost HP Smart Tank 7000 series printer, designed for individuals with high-volume printing needs. This series emphasizes sustainability, being HP's first ink tank printer made from over 25% recycled plastic, and offers smart features like self-healing Wi-Fi, automatic two-sided printing, and a spill-free refill system. The printers are available in the U.S. priced at USD$399 – $499.

title: A new Costco will open in the Triangle in November. The company is already hiring
summary: A new Costco store is set to open on November 17, 2021, in Garner, North Carolina, on an 18-acre site at 7800 Fayetteville Road. This will be the first Costco in Southern Wake County and the fourth in the Triangle area. The company has already begun hiring for various positions, and the development, called Rand Village, will eventually include retail, restaurants, apartments, and single-family housing.

title: Costco hires vessels for urgent deliveries
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has chartered three small ocean vessels for a year and leased several thousand containers to bypass clogged ocean shipping networks and avoid stockouts, as major shipping lines are unable to meet commitments. This move is part of several contingency measures the retailer is implementing to minimize supply chain disruptions, including ordering earlier, increasing inventories, and diversifying suppliers. Despite significant inflation and transportation challenges, Costco reported a 17.5% increase in net sales and a $280 million increase in net income year-over-year.

title: NovaBay Pharmaceuticals Agrees to Acquire Skin Care Brand DermaDoctor
summary: NovaBay Pharmaceuticals has reached a definitive agreement to acquire DermaDoctor, a privately-held skin care company, for $15 million. The deal includes $12 million in cash at closing and up to $3 million in earnout payments. This acquisition is expected to double NovaBay's top-line revenue and significantly expand its presence in the U.S. beauty market, with DermaDoctor's co-founders, Audrey and Jeff Kunin, continuing in leadership roles.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) stock increased by 0.69% on Wednesday, closing at $449.34 and outperforming the broader market, which also saw gains in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marked its second consecutive day of gains, though the stock remained below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed performance, with Walmart and Dollar General rising, and Target falling.

title: Cottonelle Wipes Maker Inks Deal to End Clogged Sewer Claims in Nationwide Class Action
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp., maker of Cottonelle wipes, has reached a deal with sewage system operators to address claims that its "flushable" wipes clogged sewers nationwide. The agreement, which has received preliminary judicial approval, mandates that Kimberly-Clark improve product performance and labeling to meet national flushability standards by May 2022. While this settlement resolves injunctive relief claims, it does not preclude claims for damages from other municipalities or defendants in the ongoing lawsuit.

title: Coca-Cola thinks ‘outside the box,’ books bulk vessels to ship supplies
summary: Coca-Cola is utilizing bulk vessels to transport materials, a non-traditional approach to navigate limited vessel space and keep production lines running globally. This strategy, adopted by other retailers facing supply chain congestion, involves carrying over 60,000 tons of material to non-congested ports to avoid delays and high demurrage fees. While individual company actions may not shift market dynamics, this move highlights the significant impact and overstretched state of current logistics.

title: Long Island's last Sears closes in Massapequa
summary: The last Sears department store on Long Island, located at Sunrise Mall in Massapequa, closed its doors on Sunday, marking the end of Sears' presence in the area after 62 years. Urban Edge Properties, which bought the mall, plans to redevelop the space, having paid $20 million to terminate Sears' lease and control the crucial anchor location. This closure is part of a broader trend of Sears and Kmart store closures nationwide, with only 35 Sears and 17 Kmarts remaining in the country.

title: Jerash Holdings Completes Acquisition of MK Garments
summary: Jerash Holdings (US), Inc. (NASDAQ:JRSH) announced the completion of its wholly owned subsidiary's acquisition of Mustafa and Kamal Ashraf Trading Company (Jordan) for Manufacture of Ready-Made Clothes LLC ("MK Garments"). The acquisition, valued at approximately $2.8 million in cash, includes a 71,000 square-foot apparel manufacturing facility in Amman, Jordan. Jerash Holdings has already taken over production and retained MK Garments' 500 employees as of August 2021.

title: Developer acquires Tumwater site for warehouse complex
summary: Crow Holdings has acquired an 83-acre site in Tumwater, Washington, for the development of a warehouse complex. The property is strategically located directly across from a future 1 million-square-foot Costco distribution center. This acquisition highlights the continued strong interest and activity in the Puget Sound industrial real estate market.

title: Court Preliminarily Approves Settlement In Charleston, SC, Flushable Wipes Sewer Damage Class Action
summary: A federal judge has preliminarily approved a settlement in a class action lawsuit filed by the Charleston Water System against Kimberly-Clark Corp. The lawsuit alleged that Kimberly-Clark marketed wipes as "flushable" when they were not, causing damage to sewer systems. The settlement includes enhanced product performance, testing, improved labeling, and public outreach regarding flushable wipes.

title: Walmart Denies Pressuring Its Chinese Suppliers Into Forced Exclusivity
summary: Walmart's Sam's Club in China has denied accusations of "forced exclusivity" from competitors like Carrefour China and Alibaba's Hema, stating an internal investigation found no such issues. This denial comes as Chinese regulators are increasing efforts to curb anti-competitive practices, particularly in the internet sector, with major revisions to the Anti-Monopoly Law underway. The allegations highlight the competitive landscape in China's members-only retail market and the complexities of defining monopolistic behavior.

title: Big Retailers Becoming Big Property Owners With Warehouse Deals - WSJ
summary: Major retailers such as Amazon and Costco are increasingly opting to own their warehouses rather than lease them. This strategy aims to boost e-commerce operations, save long-term costs, and gain more control over their logistics. It signifies a growing trend of retailers investing in commercial real estate's burgeoning warehouse sector.

title: Costco Auto Program sees surge in referrals
summary: The Costco Auto Program is experiencing a surge in referrals, indicating an increased demand for its services. This trend suggests that consumers are actively seeking opportunities for discounts and value in their automotive purchases. The program continues to be a notable player in connecting Costco members with automotive benefits.

title: Costco raises minimum starting wage to $17 an hour
summary: Costco has increased its minimum starting wage for new employees to $17 an hour, effective October 25, 2021. This marks its second raise in less than a year, with the company aiming to remain competitive in the retail job market. The raise also applies to current employees earning below the new minimums, with specific rates for service assistants, service clerks, and meat cutters.

title: Dermody Properties signs Costco's logistics company for West Sac industrial site
J&J, Costco settle lawsuits over recalled sunscreen
summary: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) and Costco Wholesale Corp (COST.O) have reached a tentative agreement to settle lawsuits concerning a cancer-causing substance found in several recalled J&J sunscreen products. The settlement, which is subject to court approval by November 19, aims to resolve all claims from lawsuits consolidated in a Florida federal court. J&J maintains it marketed its products appropriately and responsibly, despite voluntarily recalling the items after finding small amounts of benzene.

title: Johnson and Johnson, Costco settle lawsuits over recalled sunscreen products with cancer-causing chemical
summary: Johnson & Johnson and Costco Wholesale Corp. have reached a tentative settlement regarding lawsuits over recalled Neutrogena and Aveeno sunscreens found to contain traces of a cancer-causing chemical. J&J voluntarily recalled aerosol sunscreens last summer after detecting low levels of benzene, which is not an ingredient in their products. The settlement, which requires court approval, avoids an admission of liability from J&J, who maintains its products were marketed appropriately.

title: Costco is planning a new store for West San Jose
summary: Costco is reportedly planning to build a new store in the Westgate West shopping center in San Jose. The warehouse retailer is looking to expand its presence in the West San Jose area. This development is part of a larger trend of significant projects on the horizon for West San Jose.

title: BJ's submits plans to open store in Middle Tennessee, first location in the state
summary: Wholesale retail giant BJ's has submitted plans to open its first Tennessee location in Rutherford County, specifically in La Vergne. The proposed development includes a 108,000 square-foot building with a fuel center and space for additional retail/restaurant growth. La Vergne officials have been working for three years to secure this development, anticipating economic benefits for the city and Rutherford County.

title: BJ's Wholesale Club hopes to create shopping location in La Vergne
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club is exploring an expansion into La Vergne, Tennessee, with plans for its first store in the state. The proposed development includes a 108,000 square foot building, a fuel center, and additional retail outparcels, marking a significant win for local economic development. Discussions for this project have been ongoing since 2018.

title: Canadians Want Affordable Weed. Retailers Are Listening
summary: The legal cannabis industry in Canada is seeing a shift towards more affordable pricing, driven by consumer demand. High Tide Inc., a retail-focused cannabis company, is transitioning its stores to a discount club model to compete on price and attract customers from the illicit market. This strategy is proving successful for larger players but presents challenges for smaller retailers struggling with market saturation.

title: With sky-high consumer demand, Black Friday sales could set records this year
summary: Record consumer demand due to coronavirus relief spending and a strong economy is expected to lead to record-setting Black Friday and holiday sales, despite ongoing supply chain bottlenecks. While online shopping has driven much of this surge, experts anticipate a return to in-person Black Friday crowds due to nostalgia after last year's lockdowns. However, shoppers should be prepared for potential item availability issues and labor shortages in stores.

title: Costco finds 5 card skimmers at four Chicago-area warehouses
summary: Costco discovered five card-skimming devices at four Chicago-area warehouses in late August, compromising the payment information of fewer than 500 customers. The skimmers could capture names, card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV codes from magnetic stripes. Costco notified affected customers individually, offered free credit monitoring, and confirmed that no similar devices were found at other locations.

title: Kraft Heinz recalls some Country Time Lemonade and Kool-Aid Tropical Punch
summary: Kraft Heinz is recalling certain Country Time Lemonade and Kool-Aid Tropical Punch powdered beverages due to the possible presence of small pieces of metal and glass. The recall affects specific "Best When Used By" dates in 2023 for various sizes of the products. While the company states that accidental ingestion is unlikely to cause injury, consumers are advised not to consume the recalled products and to either discard them or return them for reimbursement.

title: Some Kool-Aid and Country Time drink mixes recalled due to glass and metal in powder
summary: Kraft Heinz has recalled certain Kool-Aid and Country Time lemonade powdered drink mixes due to the potential presence of tiny pieces of metal and glass. This recall affects products with "best when used by" dates between June 13, 2023, and Oct. 3, 2023, with consumers advised to check UPC codes for eligibility. No illnesses or injuries have been reported, and affected products should be returned for a refund or discarded.

title: Instacart Business Model
summary: This article details the Instacart business model, covering its history, ownership, mission, revenue streams (commissions, delivery fees, subscriptions, advertising), and a comprehensive Business Model Canvas analysis. It also examines Instacart's customer segments, value propositions, channels, key resources, activities, partners, cost structure, and a SWOT analysis, concluding on its market dominance despite growing competition.

title: Target, Walmart say holiday inventory is up despite supply chain disruptions
summary: Despite ongoing supply chain disruptions and shipping backlogs, both Target and Walmart have reported increased inventory levels ahead of the holiday season. Target's inventory rose 20% year-over-year, while Walmart's U.S. inventory increased by 11.5% in the third quarter, offering reassurance to shoppers concerned about product availability. This improved stock position comes even as inflation is a concern and other retailers are taking measures like chartering their own ships to mitigate supply issues.

title: Humana’s Preferred Medicare Part D Network to Include More Than 11,000 Retail Pharmacy Locations in 2022
summary: Humana announced that its Preferred Medicare Part D network will expand to include more than 11,000 retail pharmacy locations starting in 2022. This expansion adds Albertsons Companies pharmacies, providing members with more low-cost and convenient options for prescription medications. The new agreement aims to improve consumer experience and help members save money on prescriptions.

title: Costco Wholesale buys land in World Commerce Center in St. Augustine
summary: Costco Wholesale has purchased 17 acres in St. Augustine's World Commerce Center for $2.5 million to build a 162,000-square-foot store, which will include a tire center, liquor store, and gas station. Construction is expected to begin immediately with a projected opening in late second quarter of 2022. This will be Costco's third store in Northeast Florida, adding to its existing locations in Jacksonville.

title: Wayne Avenue Kroger property sells for $1.75 million
summary: The Kroger store property at 1555 Wayne Ave. in Dayton was sold for $1.75 million to OCV Dayton, a California-based limited liability company. The sale included the 26,806-square-foot store building and nearly three acres of associated parcels. A Kroger spokeswoman confirmed that it was an ownership change and Kroger will continue to lease the building, with no plans to close the store.

title: Amazon and Starbucks partner on coffee shop with cashierless technology
summary: Amazon and Starbucks have opened the first of three planned Starbucks Pickup with Amazon Go stores in New York City, marking their first collaborative effort. This new format integrates Starbucks' coffee shop experience with Amazon's cashierless technology. It is a partnership between the two Seattle-based companies to introduce a new retail concept.

title: Firing Up Growth –
summary: Chad Sokol, Costco's assistant vice president and general merchandise manager for beverage alcohol, has been instrumental in growing the company's alcohol sales to over $5 billion in 2020. Despite taking over the department at the end of 2019, just before the global pandemic, Sokol successfully navigated challenges and emphasized quality, value, and limited SKU offerings. Costco's beverage department, with wine dominating sales, continues to see strong growth and focuses on regional products and a treasure hunt shopping experience.

title: Kraft Heinz recalls some Kool-Aid, lemonade powdered beverages that may contain pieces of metal or glass
summary: Kraft Heinz is recalling certain Country Time Lemonade, Tang, Arizona Tea, and Kool-Aid powdered beverages due to the potential presence of small pieces of metal or glass. The affected products have "Best When Used By" dates between May 10, 2023, and November 1, 2023. Kraft Heinz is collaborating with retailers to remove these items from circulation, and consumers are advised to dispose of or return them.

title: Reed’s Launches Limited-Edition Real Cranberry Ginger Ale At Costco
summary: Reed's Inc. launched a limited-edition Reed's REAL Cranberry Ginger Ale exclusively for Costco members in the Northwest region, just in time for the holiday season. This non-alcoholic beverage is all-natural, Non-GMO Project Verified, contains organic pressed ginger, and is sweetened with cane sugar. The company plans to expand its ginger beverage portfolio further in 2022.

title: Pilgrim’s Gainesville, Georgia, gains from improvements
summary: Pilgrim's Pride Corp.'s facility in Gainesville, Georgia, has been recognized for its successful water pre-treatment and stormwater management efforts, preventing contamination from reaching Flat Creek and Lake Lanier. The plant, which processes 300,000 birds daily, uses advanced dissolved air floatation units and an upgraded stormwater system to manage 1.44 million gallons of wastewater and prevent runoff into vital water sources. These efforts earned the facility an honorable mention in the 2021 U.S. Poultry & Egg Association’s Clean Water Awards.

title: Costco gives Q1 preview in robust November sales report
summary: Costco reported robust preliminary net sales growth for its fiscal 2022 first quarter, with November comparable-club sales increasing by 14.1% overall, driven partly by higher fuel prices. Net sales climbed 15.7% to $18.13 billion for the four weeks ending November 28. The company is set to release its full Q1 fiscal 2022 sales and earnings on December 9.

title: How Kroger Beat the Supply Chain Crisis
summary: Kroger successfully navigated the supply chain crisis in Q3 2021, reporting impressive sales growth and raising its fiscal 2021 guidance. The company attributed its success to early planning, investments in its omni-ecosystem, and the strength of its private brands, which helped address consumer needs amidst inflation and national brand SKU reductions. Kroger also expanded its digital and delivery services while focusing on employee wages and diversity initiatives.

title: St. Johns County issues Costco building permits
summary: St. Johns County has issued building permits for Costco Wholesale to construct a new warehouse club and fuel facility in the World Commerce Center, totaling almost $13.6 million. The 157,317-square-foot facility, including a tire center, liquor store, and gas station, is expected to open by the end of the second quarter of 2022. This marks Costco's third retail club in the area.

title: Costco Copes with Supply Chain, Turns in Strong Q1
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. successfully navigated supply chain challenges and exceeded Wall Street expectations in its first fiscal quarter. The company reported a net income of $1.32 billion and comparable sales growth of 9.8%, driven by strong e-commerce expansion and new initiatives like e-commerce kiosks and the Costco Next program. CFO Richard Galanti noted the impact of supply chain issues but expressed confidence in Costco's ability to maintain stock levels and mitigate rising costs.

title: Texas Roadhouse to officially open in Henderson on Monday
summary: Texas Roadhouse is set to open its new Henderson location on Monday evening at 3531 St. Rose Parkway. This will be the second Texas Roadhouse in the Las Vegas valley, joining the North Las Vegas restaurant that opened in 2018. The new location has hired 250 team members.

title: T-Mobile announces $20 an hour minimum wage for all employees
summary: T-Mobile has announced a new minimum wage of $20 an hour for all full-time and part-time employees, effective nationwide. CEO Mike Sievert stated this move is about "inclusion" and ensuring all employees earn a competitive wage. This decision follows similar wage hikes by other major retailers to attract and retain workers.

title: Key executive for North Carolina-based grocer is stepping down
summary: Ron Freeman, CFO of Ingles Markets, an Asheville-based grocery chain, is set to retire from his executive post and board role. This departure marks a significant change for the North Carolina-based grocer.

title: Banana Boat Sunscreen Spray Recall Issued in Australia Due to Presence of Benzene
summary: Australia has issued a recall for several Banana Boat sunscreen spray products due to the discovery of high levels of benzene, a known carcinogen. Edgewell Personal Care Company, in conjunction with Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration, announced the recall after internal testing confirmed benzene contamination in specific batches. This follows earlier discoveries of benzene in other popular aerosol sunscreens in the U.S., leading to previous recalls and lawsuits.

title: Urban Edge Properties Acquires Woodmore Towne Centre in Metro Washington, D.C. for $193.4 Million
summary: Urban Edge Properties has acquired Woodmore Towne Centre, a 712,000-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center in Glenarden, Maryland, along with an adjacent 22-acre land parcel, for $193.4 million. The acquisition was funded by cash on-hand and a $117.2 million non-recourse first mortgage loan. The property was 97 percent leased at the time of sale to major tenants including Wegmans, Costco, and Nordstrom Rack.

title: Costco Finishes 2021 Strong With December Sales Gains
summary: Costco reported strong sales gains for December 2021, with net sales increasing by 16.2% to $22.24 billion and comparable e-commerce sales up 17.8%. Despite challenges like supply chain issues and inflation, the company achieved a 16.6% increase in net sales for the 18 weeks ending January 2, 2022, totaling $76.34 billion, and saw its Q1 net income rise.

title: New Report Shows Continued Growth in Hard Seltzer Market
summary: A new report projects the global hard seltzer market to reach USD 49.4 billion by 2028, growing at a CAGR of 31.4% from 2021 to 2028. This growth is driven by shifting consumer preferences for low-alcohol, low-calorie

title: Costco acquires Hoopili Business Park for more than $130M - Pacific Business News
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has acquired the Hoopili Business Park in West Oahu for over $130 million from an affiliate of Jupiter Holdings, LLC. The business park is being developed on 45 acres within D.R. Horton's master-planned Hoopili Community.

title: Filings: Construction nearing for 2 Costco stores in Central Texas suburbs
summary: New state filings suggest that construction could soon begin on two Costco Wholesale stores in Central Texas suburbs, specifically in Georgetown and Kyle. The retail giant has been largely quiet about these locations, which were first announced in 2019 and 2021, but the recently filed documents indicate progress. MG2 and Costco are involved in these developments.

title: Costco named MMR Retailer of the Year
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has been named MMR’s Retailer of the Year for its efficient business model, strong financial performance, and ability to provide an enjoyable shopping experience despite challenges. The company reported significant sales and net income increases in fiscal 2021 and the first quarter of fiscal 2022, driven by its limited product selection, operating efficiencies, and expansion efforts. Costco's Kirkland Signature brand and growing e-commerce presence also contributed to its strong growth and profitability.

title: Reed’s Zero Sugar Classic Mule
summary: Reed's Inc. has launched its new Reed’s Zero Sugar Classic Mule, which is now available at select Costco Wholesale locations across the Southeast United States. This ready-to-drink (RTD) canned mule features fresh ginger root, contains zero added sugar, and has a 7% ABV. It is handcrafted through a unique brewing and fermentation process, free from artificial colors, gluten, GMOs, or caffeine.

title: The 10 Best Consumer Cyclical Stocks to Buy for 2022
summary: This article identifies the top 10 consumer cyclical stocks to consider buying in 2022, based on the expectation of robust economic growth and strong consumer confidence. It highlights companies in recreation, retail, household durables, automotive, and media sectors, detailing their recent financial performance, stock movements, and market outlook. The list includes companies like Chewy, Coca-Cola, Costco, Ford, Home Depot, Nike, and Royal Caribbean, along with two relevant ETFs.

title: Kroger workers' strike in Colorado ends after 10 days, tentative deal reached
summary: A 10-day strike by King Soopers' workers, owned by Kroger, has concluded in Colorado after the United Food and Commercial Workers Local 7 announced a tentative agreement. The strike involved over 8,000 workers seeking better pay, health benefits, and improved Covid safety measures. While early details of the agreement are not public, union president Kim Cordova stated it addresses unfair labor practices and ensures workers receive the respect, pay, and protection they deserve.

title: LA Fitness Now Open At Woodmore Towne Centre
summary: Urban Edge Properties announced that LA Fitness has opened a 42,154-square-foot gym at Woodmore Towne Centre in Glenarden, Maryland. This addition further enhances the shopping center's offerings, which already include major retailers and restaurants. The gym features state-of-the-art equipment, a swimming pool, spa, sauna, and various fitness classes, with additional businesses like Ledo Pizza and European Wax expected to open soon.

title: Costco Pet Insurance Overview: Features, Pricing, and More
summary: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) offers pet insurance through a partnership with Figo, providing Costco members with a 15% discount. Figo's plans are highly customizable, feature no upper age limits for pets, and exclude pre-existing conditions, though some curable conditions might be covered. The article details policy options, customer service, pricing examples, and the application process, highlighting Figo's short waiting period for accident coverage as a competitive advantage.

title: United State Organic Food Market Retains Robust Growth Amid the Pandemic: Projected to Grow at a CAGR of 8.7% during 2021-2027 | BlueWeave
summary: The U.S. organic food market reached USD 52.3 billion in 2020 and is projected to grow at an 8.7% CAGR to USD 95.1 billion by 2027, driven by increasing health awareness and environmental concerns. Despite higher prices compared to conventional foods, the market is boosted by the growing shift towards organic farming and increased availability in major supermarket chains and online channels. Recent developments include Amara Organic Foods expanding into Walmart Canada and Daily Harvest partnering with AFT and CCOF to support underserved organic farming communities.

title: Fast Food Hot Dogs, Ranked Worst To Best
summary: This article ranks fast food hot dogs from worst to best, evaluating offerings from various chains based on taste, price, and overall quality. It highlights the strengths and weaknesses of each hot dog, from Dairy Queen's unpopular option to Shake Shack's top-ranked dog, also noting those from Costco, Sonic, and Nathan's Famous. The piece provides insights into different fast food hot dog varieties and their unique attributes.

title: Costco Shareholder Vote Signals Focus on Supply-Chain Emissions
summary: Costco shareholders have voted in favor of a resolution pushing the retailer to establish a plan for achieving net-zero greenhouse-gas emissions by 2050 or sooner. This vote highlights increasing investor scrutiny on supply-chain emissions, specifically Scope 3 emissions, which Costco identifies as the majority of its environmental impact. The resolution passed despite opposition from Costco's board, underscoring a growing focus on tougher climate commitments within the investment community.

title: BJ’s to acquire four cold distribution centers from Burris Logistics
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club announced its plan to acquire four perishables distribution centers and their transportation fleets from Burris Logistics, a long-standing partner. This deal, financial terms of which were not disclosed, includes refrigerated DCs in Rocky Hill, Conn.; Orlando, Fla.; Elkton, Md.; and Independence, Ky. The acquisition aims to in-source BJ's perishables supply chain and support its continued growth and expansion of fresh food offerings.

title: eBay Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: eBay Inc. (EBAY) stock fell by 1.75% on Thursday, closing at $56.70. This decline occurred during a generally poor trading session for the market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also seeing decreases. The stock underperformed compared to some competitors and closed significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Krispy Kreme Has A Line of Heart-Shaped Donuts Just In Time For Valentine's Day
summary: Krispy Kreme is offering a special line of heart-shaped donuts for Valentine's Day, available starting January 31st through the holiday. The collection includes four distinct flavors: Beary Best Valentine, Bee Mine, Cookie to My Kreme, and My Batter Half donuts. These festive treats can be purchased in a special box with pop-out Valentine's Day cards and are also available for delivery via DoorDash.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club Recruited to Mt. Juliet
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club plans to open a new 104,353 square-foot store in Mt. Juliet's Providence Central mixed-use development, with an anticipated opening in 2023. The Mt. Juliet Planning Commission approved the site plans on January 20, a goal the city has pursued for years to attract a wholesale retailer. The new store is expected to bring economic benefits to the community by retaining tax dollars and enhancing shopping options, though there are concerns about potential traffic congestion.

title: How Costco Affords To Sell Gas 20 Cents per Gallon Cheaper Than Average
summary: Costco is able to sell gas significantly cheaper than competitors due to the high volume of gas sold at each location, which can reach up to 1 million gallons per month. This strategy, despite narrow profit margins on gas, drives sales in their warehouses as many gas customers also shop inside. Additionally, Costco gas is TOP TIER licensed and contains five times the EPA-required detergent additive, ensuring high quality.

title: Weis joins crowded supermarket space in Warminster area. How grocers survive with so many options
summary: Weis Markets recently opened a new 46,000-square-foot store in Warminster, Pennsylvania, entering a highly competitive grocery market. The area already hosts numerous large retailers, and the new store faces challenges common to the industry, such as labor shortages and supply chain disruptions exacerbated by the pandemic. Despite these hurdles, Weis aims to differentiate itself with convenience, value, and community involvement in its expansion efforts in the Philadelphia area.

title: Costco Membership Benefits — Are They Worth the Annual Fee?
summary: This article examines the benefits and costs of a Costco membership, which ranges from $60 to $120 annually. It discusses how the value of membership depends on individual shopping habits, such as buying in bulk or purchasing specific high-discount items like tires or eyeglasses. The article also provides alternatives for non-members to shop at Costco.

title: Metal building systems provide Costco with cost and time savings
summary: Costco has embraced metal building systems for 90% of its warehouse stores due to significant cost savings—about $150,000 per store by eliminating bays, joists, and columns—and accelerated construction timelines, completing stores in 110 days compared to 160-180 days for conventional builds. Innovations in metal building technology, such as 60-ft spans and attractive, durable exterior finishes, also contribute to their widespread use. Additionally, in-plant coating of components saves painting costs, further enhancing efficiency and aesthetics.

title: Ashby: Costco in talks for new store in Natomas off I-5
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is reportedly planning a new store in Natomas, California, according to a Sacramento City Councilmember. The article, by Ben van der Meer, details the development without providing further specifics on the timeline or location beyond "off I-5". This news follows previous related reports concerning Costco's logistics and other store developments in the wider Sacramento area.

title: Two Austin shopping centers with major anchors sell for $189.3 million
summary: InvenTrust Properties Corp. of Illinois has acquired two major shopping centers in South Austin, The Shops at Arbor Trails and Escarpment Village, for a total of $189.3 million. These properties are anchored by significant retailers like Costco, Whole Foods, and H-E-B, highlighting the continued desirability and robust retail market in Austin. The acquisition underscores a strong recovery in the local retail sector, which has seen occupancy rates return to pre-pandemic levels despite challenges in 2020.

title: Bark teams up with Walmart as it builds out its wholesale network
summary: Bark, known for its subscription boxes Super Chewer and BarkBox, has partnered with Walmart to sell its products in nearly 2,800 stores and online. This new partnership, along with a recent collaboration with REI, expands Bark's wholesale network, which already includes major retailers like Target and Costco, bringing its total physical store presence to over 33,000 across the U.S. Amidst this expansion, Bark reported a 34% year-over-year increase in total revenue for its third quarter, reaching $140.8 million, demonstrating the company's success in growing its customer base through diversified retail channels.

title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers $7M Sale of Promenade Shopping Plaza in Valdosta, Georgia
summary: Marcus & Millichap has successfully brokered the $7 million sale of Promenade Plaza, a 64,523-square-foot shopping center in Valdosta, Georgia. The property, fully occupied by tenants like Shoe Carnival and Best Buy, was sold to an undisclosed buyer, with both seller and buyer represented by Marcus & Millichap brokers. The plaza is strategically located near Valdosta Mall and Valdosta State University.

title: JBS withdraws offer to buy rest of Pilgrim’s Pride
summary: JBS has withdrawn its offer to acquire the remaining shares of Pilgrim's Pride Corporation after failing to reach an agreement with a special committee of Pilgrim's Pride's Board of Directors. JBS, which is the majority shareholder, had initially offered $26.50 per share in August 2021, and later increased the offer by $2 per share, but the committee deemed it insufficient. JBS became the majority stakeholder in Pilgrim's Pride in 2009.

title: Walmart adopts long-term view on pricing, inflation
summary: Walmart Inc. executives shared their positive outlook for the coming year during their fourth-quarter earnings call. The company is forecasting a 3.0% increase in consolidated comps and for Walmart US sales, primarily driven by long-term pricing strategies, supply chain improvements, and business diversification beyond traditional retail. Walmart US sales hit $105 billion in Q4, and the company plans to focus on ensuring customer value despite expected increases in product and technology costs.

title: Costco took meat supervisor’s ‘secret invention’ but never paid him for it, GA suit says
summary: A Costco employee in Georgia is suing the retail giant, alleging they used his automated meat ordering system without compensation. The lawsuit claims his "secret invention" saved Costco hundreds of thousands of dollars and was implemented in multiple stores. The plaintiff, Ronald McLeod, is seeking payment and other benefits, citing fraudulent misrepresentation and breach of contract.

title: Tyson Files Complaint to Prevent Arbitration with Costco Over Broiler Chicken Antitrust Claims
summary: Tyson Foods, Inc. has filed a complaint against Costco Wholesale Corporation seeking to prevent arbitration over broiler chicken antitrust claims. Tyson argues that Costco has not established an enforceable agreement to arbitrate, disputing the validity of a 1995 "Vendor Agreement" and an unsigned 2019 document cited by Costco. Despite Tyson's objections, the American Arbitration Association (AAA) decided to proceed with arbitration, prompting Tyson's lawsuit for a declaratory judgment and an injunction.

title: Tyson Files To Stop Arbitration With Costco In Chicken Antitrust Suit
summary: Tyson Foods has filed a complaint against Costco Wholesale Corporation in the Western District of Washington, seeking a declaration that it has not agreed to arbitrate claims brought by Costco. The dispute stems from a class-action lawsuit, "In re Broiler Chicken Antitrust Litigation," where Tyson had previously reached a settlement with direct purchasers, but Costco was not part of that agreement. Tyson alleges that Costco's demand for arbitration, mirroring the antitrust conspiracy claim, is based on a 1995 vendor agreement and an unsigned 2019 document that does not mention Tyson.

title: Kroger, Safeway/Albertsons and Hawaiian Isles Agree to Settle in Kona Labeling Case
summary: Kroger, Safeway/Albertsons, and Hawaiian Isles Kona Coffee Co. have reached preliminary settlements in a class action lawsuit regarding the mislabeling and sale of "Kona" coffee products. The settlements, totaling over $15.25 million, include monetary relief for Kona-based coffee farmers and stricter labeling requirements for future sales. Hawaiian Isles Kona Coffee Co. will also change its name to remove "Kona" as part of its agreement.

title: Kroger Porter Five Forces Analysis
summary: This article provides a Porter Five Forces analysis of Kroger, a major multi-department supermarket chain in the United States. It evaluates the threat of new entrants (moderately high), threat of substitutes (high), bargaining power of customers (high), bargaining power of suppliers (very low), and competitive rivalry (high). The analysis highlights the intense competition in the retail market and the factors influencing Kroger's competitive environment.

title: The J.M. Smucker (SJM) Queued Up for Q3 Earnings: Things to Note
summary: The J. M. Smucker Company (SJM) is expected to experience a year-over-year decrease in both top and bottom lines for its fiscal third-quarter 2022 earnings, which are set to be reported on March 1. The company faces significant cost inflation, supply-chain issues, and labor shortages, which are anticipated to impact its gross profit and gross margin. Despite these challenges, management is implementing pricing actions, revenue growth strategies, and productivity initiatives, alongside a recovery in the "Away from Home" division, to mitigate negative effects.

title: Target to hike starting hourly wages
summary: Target announced a new starting wage range of $15 to $24 per hour, part of an up to $300 million investment in employee pay and benefits for 2022. This move applies to hourly associates across stores, supply chain facilities, and headquarters, with exact wages determined by job role and local market. The company also improved health care benefits, making more employees eligible and reducing waiting periods, alongside other enhanced wellness and family support programs.

title: Target Positions Itself as Benefits Leader With Up to $24 Starting Wage
summary: Target is investing $300 million in 2022 to enhance employee benefits, including raising its starting wage range to $15-$24 an hour and expanding access to health care for its team members. This initiative will make about 20% of Target's team newly eligible for comprehensive health care benefits, with reduced waiting periods and expanded wellness offerings. These changes are part of Target's ongoing strategy to create equity and opportunity, building on previous enhancements like debt-free college programs and permanent Thanksgiving Day store closings.

title: Target is serious about cutting employee turnover
summary: Target is significantly increasing its investment in employee wages and benefits, including raising its starting wage range to $15-$24 an hour and expanding healthcare access for more associates. This move is part of the retailer's strategy to reduce employee turnover and position itself as a leading employer in the retail sector. The company's chief human resources officer emphasized that these investments are a direct result of listening to team member feedback to foster rewarding careers at Target.

title: CIBC rolls out Canadian Costco credit card portfolio
summary: CIBC is taking over Costco's credit card business in Canada, aiming for a smooth transition for existing cardholders. This move comes as Costco shifts its credit card provider, impacting numerous customers who use the co-branded cards for purchases.

title: Costco Wholesale Names New Chief Merchant
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has appointed Claudine Adamo, a 30-year veteran, as EVP, COO, merchandising, succeeding Ron Vachris. The announcement coincided with Costco's Q2 earnings report, showing a 16.1% increase in net sales to $50.94 billion and a 11.3% rise in same-store sales, despite ongoing inflationary and supply chain pressures which the company is actively mitigating through chartered vessels.

title: San Dimas: Doctor, family sue Costco, alleging live worms were found in Kirkland halibut product as 13-year-old daughter ate it
summary: A doctor and his family are suing Costco, alleging that halibut purchased from a San Dimas store contained live worms that were discovered as their 13-year-old daughter was eating it. The lawsuit, filed in Los Angeles Superior Court, alleges negligence, breach of warranty, products liability, failure to warn, and violation of the state Unfair Competition Law, seeking at least $200,000 in damages. The family claims Costco has known about this defect and failed to warn consumers, and that employees lack adequate food safety training.

title: Costco Business Center site in Arden-Arcade sold
summary: The Costco Business Center at 3360 El Camino Ave. in Arden-Arcade was sold for $23.5 million to a publicly traded real estate investment trust. This marks a new owner for the first local Costco Wholesale Corp. Business Center concept, which specializes in selling business supplies.

title: Just own it: why Nike looks significantly undervalued
summary: Alfred Tadros, a portfolio manager at Aoris Investment Management, discusses why Nike appears significantly undervalued and his positive outlook on Costco. The article also touches on Aoris's interest in IDEXX Labs and how the Russian invasion of Ukraine has impacted their portfolio.

title: Lisa Frank X Crocs: How can I buy the clogs?
summary: The Lisa Frank X Crocs collaboration released on March 15, 2022, offering limited-edition clogs in purple and aqua with classic Lisa Frank designs. Fans could enter a lucky draw from Tuesday to Thursday, March 17, at 9:30 pm local time to purchase the shoes. Winners would be notified by email, charged $59.99 plus tax, and needed an EQL account to participate.

title: Costco settles ERISA case for $5.1 million
summary: Costco Wholesale has agreed to a $5.1 million settlement in an ERISA lawsuit as reported by Bloomberg. The article briefly mentions other unrelated financial news stories including SEC work on private credit, university endowment performance, Carlyle's AUM, and CalPERS' voting against Elon Musk's pay package.

title: Costco workers to receive NT$30 hourly wage hike
summary: Costco Wholesale Taiwan will implement a NT$30 hourly wage increase for all employees starting next week, marking its second wage hike in six months. This increase will raise hourly wages for new part-time employees by 14% and monthly salaries for new full-time employees from NT$36,849 to NT$42,039. Supermarket chain PX Mart also announced salary increases and incentives, following the government's wage hikes for civil servants, teachers, and military personnel.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club launches same-day delivery
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club has launched Same-Day Select, a membership add-on that offers unlimited or package-based same-day grocery deliveries. This service, which was rolled out chainwide after a six-month successful testing phase, allows members to receive groceries in as little as two hours while continuing to benefit from in-club pricing, rewards, and coupons. It aims to provide greater convenience and value to members by offering options like 12 free deliveries for $55 or unlimited free deliveries for $100 per year.

title: Best Places To Work: Seattle Metropolitan Area 2022
summary: Comparably has released its list of the Best Companies in the Seattle Metropolitan Area for 2022, based on anonymous employee ratings collected over the past year. The rankings consider nearly 20 workplace culture categories, including compensation, leadership, and work-life balance. Microsoft, Smartsheet, and T-Mobile topped the list of 15 companies acknowledged for their positive work environments.

title: Costco to open in Amherst
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is set to open a new store in Amherst, New York, on Ridge Lea Road, at the former site of Tony Roma's restaurant. The big-box retailer plans to proceed with the design and approval process this year and aims to begin construction around spring 2023. This development follows years of rumors about a Costco location in the Buffalo area.

title: Costco is coming to Amherst
summary: Costco is planning to open a new store in Amherst, with construction projected to begin in spring 2023. This development was confirmed by the Amherst town supervisor. The article, published by Buffalo Business First, highlights the upcoming arrival of the big-box retailer to the Buffalo area.

title: Costco ruling: Stuart City Commission failed in its analysis of Kanner Highway site
summary: An administrative law judge ruled against the city of Stuart concerning a key element of the proposed Costco project. Judge Francine Ffolkes found that the city's analysis for the land-use designation was not supported by a professionally acceptable methodology regarding water supply, wastewater services, and traffic impact. The ruling suggests the project's future is uncertain, with the recommended order now awaiting a final determination from the state Administration Commission.

title: Kimberly-Clark to Pay $20M Settlement to Consumers Nationwide Over Flushable Wipe Claims
summary: Kimberly-Clark has agreed to a $20 million settlement to resolve two class-action lawsuits alleging its "flushable" wipes clog pipes and septic systems. The settlement, if approved, would benefit consumers nationwide who purchased the wipes since May 2011, with payments up to $50.60 for those with proof of purchase. This agreement follows lengthy litigation and other related lawsuits against flushable wipe manufacturers.

title: Filing shows Costco planning retail location in Natomas
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has filed an application with the City of Sacramento for a new 160,526-square-foot store in the Natomas area at 3881 E. Commerce Way. This filing indicates the company is moving forward with its plans for a new retail location in the area.

title: Walmart Hires PayPal’s John Rainey as CFO
summary: Walmart Inc. has named John Rainey, PayPal Holdings Inc.'s Chief Financial Officer, as its new finance chief, effective June 6. Rainey will replace Brett Biggs and his appointment comes as Walmart focuses on developing a financial-technology venture and expanding its paid membership program, Walmart+. He will also address challenges such as inflation, supply chain issues, and rising labor costs.

title: Costco Worker in N.Y. Sues Over Biweekly Pay Scheme, Unpaid OT
summary: A Costco worker in New York has filed a lawsuit against Costco Wholesale Corp., alleging violations of the Fair Labor Standards Act and New York law. The complaint claims that Costco failed to compensate hundreds of store employees for missed meal breaks and improperly delayed paychecks by automatically deducting 30 minutes for meal periods, even if breaks were not taken, leading to unpaid overtime wages.

title: Shoppers give views on PriceSmart Portmore
summary: With the opening of PriceSmart's 50th location in Portmore, shoppers shared their views on whether they would switch their allegiance from other supermarkets and wholesalers. While many appreciated the convenience and bulk buying options, several noted that they would not commit exclusively to PriceSmart due to the need for smaller purchases and competitive pricing elsewhere. The article highlights a mixed reception to the new store, balancing bulk savings with daily shopping needs.

title: Chipotle approved for Natomas Crossing development
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill has received approval to open a new restaurant in the Natomas Crossing area of Sacramento. The new location, planned for next spring, will feature a drive-thru pickup window, which the company calls a "Chipotlane," for preordered food. This development is part of a larger plan for the area and follows related news about other businesses, including Costco, also filing plans for Natomas.

title: Is First Trust Capital Strength ETF (FTCS) a Strong ETF Right Now?
summary: This article evaluates the First Trust Capital Strength ETF (FTCS), a smart beta ETF designed to invest in well-capitalized companies with strong market positions, financial strength, and earnings growth. It details the fund's expense ratio, sector allocation, top holdings, and performance, noting its medium-risk profile and diversification among 51 holdings. The article also suggests alternative market cap weighted ETFs for investors seeking lower-cost options.

title: The winners, losers and ones to watch in Detroit's grocery wars
summary: Kroger dominates the Southeast Michigan grocery market with the largest market share, despite having no stores within Detroit itself.
