The article highlights the competitive nature of the grocery industry, shifting consumer trends, and the ongoing challenge of food insecurity and food deserts within Detroit, where residents often shop outside the city. Amazon Fresh is poised to enter the metro Detroit market, indicating continued evolution in the local grocery landscape.

title: The winners and losers in Chicagoland's grocery wars
summary: Despite the rise of various grocery store formats, Jewel remains the market leader in Chicagoland's grocery sector. The analysis highlights that while mainstream stores like Jewel still dominate, specialty and discount grocers are also strong contenders. In 2021, Chicagoland's grocery sales hit $24.5 billion, with households spending 4.5% of their income on food and drink for the home.

title: Walmart Boosts Fuel Discount for Premium Members
summary: Walmart is expanding its fuel discount program for Walmart+ members, offering up to 10 cents off per gallon at participating stations. The discount will now be available at 12,000 Exxon and Mobil stations, in addition to Walmart and Murphy's stations and Sam's Club locations. This move aims to help members save money amidst rising fuel prices and enhance the value of the Walmart+ membership.

title: Costco set to anchor new Queen Creek development
summary: Costco will be the anchor tenant for Queen Creek Crossing, one of three new retail centers being developed by Vestar in the region. The new warehouse store marks Costco's expansion into the East Valley. Initial details on the two main sub-tenants for the project are also planned for release.

title: Progress being made on retail complex in southeast Fresno
summary: After 16 years, significant progress is being made on the Fancher Creek mixed-use development in southeast Fresno, starting with two senior housing complexes. The complex aims to create a "20-minute neighborhood" with retail, entertainment, and housing, similar to Fresno's River Park, and is expected to open in early to mid-2023. This development, which will include a movie theater and a Burlington Coat Factory nearby, is projected to increase local property values.

title: Costco Stock Split May Be Coming After More Than Two Decades
summary: Costco Wholesale (COST) stock has not split in over two decades, despite its significant price increase of over 187% in the last five years. While there is no official confirmation, analysts suggest a stock split could be imminent to make shares more accessible to small investors, although it would not change the company's value. Costco has a history of three stock splits, with the last one in 2000, and is considered a solid, fairly valued investment due to its strong growth and high membership renewal rates.

title: The PG 100: Ranking Top Food Retailers in North America
summary: The "PG 100" report ranks the top 100 food retailers in North America, highlighting an 11% increase in combined sales to $2.275 trillion in 2021. The report discusses challenges and benefits faced by retailers due to COVID-19 and rising fuel prices, as well as significant merger and acquisition activity in the industry. It provides a detailed table with sales, store counts, and top executives for each of the ranked companies.

title: Costco 401(k) mismanagement $3.2M class action settlement
summary: Costco has agreed to a $3.2 million class action settlement to resolve claims that it mismanaged its 401(k) plan, leading to higher-than-necessary fees for participants. The settlement benefits current and certain former Costco 401(k) plan participants who had account balances over $1,000 for at least 12 months between May 30, 2014, and March 17, 2022. Eligible individuals could file a claim by July 1, 2022, to receive a payment, though the settlement is now closed.

title: J. M. Smucker recalls some Jif peanut butter products
summary: J. M. Smucker Co. is recalling some Jif peanut butter products in the US and Canada due to potential Salmonella contamination. The company expanded its recall to Canada after announcing a voluntary recall in the US, advising consumers to dispose of affected products immediately. This recall comes as J.M. Smucker recorded net sales of $2.06 billion in the quarter ended Jan. 31, with peanut butter and other consumer foods accounting for about a fifth of revenue.

title: Jif issues voluntary recall of certain peanut butter products due to potential Salmonella contamination
summary: The J.M. Smucker Company has issued a voluntary recall for select Jif peanut butter products in the U.S. due to potential Salmonella contamination. The FDA reports 14 people across 12 states have fallen ill, with two hospitalized, after consuming the affected products. Consumers are advised to discard Jif products with lot code numbers 1274425 through 2140425.

title: Costco Hiding the Dollar’s Dirty Secret?
summary: This article discusses several key economic and investment topics, including the potential rollback of Trump-era trade tariffs, the investment opportunity in global shipping ETFs as trade normalizes, and the unusual pricing strategy of Costco's hot dog to illustrate the difficulty of fighting inflation. It also touches on how negative economic news might already be "priced in" by markets and draws parallels between current tech stock trends and John Templeton's legendary trades.

title: How Amazon, Microsoft, Costco and more Seattle-area brands rank by reputation
summary: Amazon ranked highest among Seattle-area companies in a recent Axios and Harris Poll survey assessing the reputations of the 100 most visible corporate brands in the U.S. Conversely, Costco, based in Issaquah, experienced a 17-place drop in the same survey. The article highlights how local companies performed in this national reputational ranking.

title: Natural Grocers lends hand as shoppers grapple with high food prices
summary: Natural Grocers is helping customers combat high food prices by offering various savings programs, including store-brand products, "Good4u Meal Deals," and its {N}power loyalty program. The company emphasizes its "Always Affordable Pricing" principle, which has been central to its operations for over 67 years, and provides free nutrition education. This initiative comes as food-at-home Consumer Price Index rose 10.8% year over year in April.

title: Costco sales top estimates by $1 billion, but misses on same-store sales
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported fiscal third-quarter earnings, beating revenue estimates by $1 billion and putting the company on track for its first $200 billion year. However, same-store sales rose by just 10.8%, falling short of estimates. The company's earnings per share were in line with analyst expectations.

title: Hawaii Visitors: Don’t Waste Time Buying Gas at Costco
summary: The article advises Hawaii visitors to reconsider buying gas at Costco, as the significant price advantage Costco once held has diminished. This change is attributed to Hawaii's shift from cheaper Russian oil and other retailers adjusting their prices to compete. The author suggests alternatives, highlights the inconvenience of long lines and membership requirements at Costco gas stations, and notes that the savings are often minimal compared to the time wasted.

title: Costco enters dawn delivery service market in S.Korea
summary: Costco has launched dawn delivery services in South Korea, making it the first country outside the US where the retail giant offers this service. This move signifies a reversal of Costco's previous no-delivery policy and aims to compete with local e-commerce leaders like Coupang and Kurly, despite the increased cost pressures. The decision comes as e-commerce dominates South Korea's grocery retail market, a stark contrast to Lotte Group's recent withdrawal from the same service.

title: How Costco became a staple for Asian American families
summary: Costco has become a staple for Asian American families due to its bulk shopping model aligning with their larger household sizes and purchasing habits. The retail giant has also started to recognize and cater to this demographic by offering specialty Asian products, contributing to its growth and consumer loyalty within this community. This trend highlights the significant market shift created by the rapid growth and purchasing power of Asian Americans.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. stock falls Wednesday, still outperforms market
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) stock declined by 0.80% on Wednesday, closing at $467.99. Despite the fall, the stock still outperformed the broader market, as both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced larger drops. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for Costco, with its stock trading significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Buckeye looks to boost industrial development across 4,000 acres in city
summary: The City of Buckeye is actively working to expand industrial development across 4,000 acres, with 25 million square feet of industrial space already in the pipeline. This initiative follows a period of significant industrial growth, including large facilities for companies like Five Below and Funko Inc., and is also bringing the city closer to securing a Costco location.

title: New American Fortune 500 in 2022: The Largest American Companies and Their Immigrant Roots
summary: A report from the American Immigration Council finds that 43.8% of the 2022 Fortune 500 companies were founded by immigrants or their children. These "New American" firms generated over $7 trillion in revenue and employed 14.8 million people in fiscal year 2021, demonstrating a significant impact on the U.S. economy. The report highlights the critical role of immigrant entrepreneurs in job creation and economic growth.

title: Kroger is now delivering in South Florida
summary: Kroger has launched online grocery delivery services in South Florida through a new 60,000-square-foot spoke facility in Miami, which supports its automated customer fulfillment center in Groveland, Florida. This expansion is part of Kroger's aggressive growth strategy in Florida, utilizing a hub-and-spoke network to deliver groceries to areas hundreds of miles from its CFCs. The company aims to compete with rivals like Amazon and Walmart by focusing on next-day delivery, a wide assortment, competitive pricing, and its partnership with Ocado, particularly in markets where it lacks physical stores.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. stock falls Friday, still outperforms market
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) stock fell 1.85% on Friday, closing at $463.31, despite a broader market decline where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also dropped. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high but showed a mixed performance compared to competitors like Walmart (WMT), which rose, and Target (TGT) and Dollar General (DG), which also fell. Trading volume was lower than its 50-day average.

title: eBay Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: eBay Inc. (EBAY) stock dropped 0.82% to $42.58 on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw declines. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for eBay, with the stock closing significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed performance, with Amazon.com Inc. falling, while Walmart Inc. and Costco Wholesale Corp. rose.

title: Home Depot, Costco and 3 More Retail Stocks to Buy
summary: The article identifies five retail stocks poised for success despite recent declines in retail sales. It highlights companies like Home Depot, Costco, AutoZone, Academy Sports + Outdoors, and Dollar General, explaining why each is a promising investment opportunity in the current economic climate.

title: How Home Depot’s Pro Xtra Program Alone Helped Me Save $1,400 This Year
summary: The author details how Home Depot's Pro Xtra program helped him save $1,400 this year through perks, coupons, and special offers, highlighting that individuals don't need to be licensed contractors or business owners to sign up. The article also suggests exploring similar discount programs at other retailers and leveraging small business status for additional savings. It emphasizes asking for volume discounts and considering licensing for industry-specific benefits.

title: CIBC forecasts higher profits as CEO Victor Dodig pitches bank’s transformation
summary: CIBC has raised its profit growth target and adjusted return-on-equity, with CEO Victor Dodig emphasizing the bank's transformation into a more stable and client-focused institution. The bank is expanding its U.S. commercial banking and wealth management segments, investing in retail banking, and targeting growth in its innovation banking and direct financial services units. Despite economic uncertainties, Dodig asserts that CIBC's strategy is built on consistent client relationships rather than cyclical trends.

title: Shareholders hit Costco with animal abuse lawsuit
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is facing a lawsuit filed by shareholders Krystil Smith and Tyler Lobdell, who allege the grocery chain is neglecting livestock and violating animal abuse laws in Nebraska and Iowa. The suit claims Costco's directors and officers have breached their fiduciary duty by overlooking unlawful practices, primarily at the Lincoln Premium Poultry plant, where chickens allegedly endured starvation, dehydration, and untreated illnesses. Much of the evidence cited in the lawsuit comes from an undercover investigation by Mercy for Animals.

title: Biggest US Supermarket Chain Boosts Outlook as Inflation-Weary Shoppers Focus on Groceries
summary: Kroger, the largest supermarket chain in the U.S., has increased its financial outlook for the year after a rise in first-quarter sales. This boost is attributed to inflation-weary shoppers redirecting their spending towards essential groceries, a trend that has conversely impacted other big retailers with excess inventory. The company's results underscore a national shift in consumer purchasing habits and highlight grocers' increasing importance to retail landlords and investors.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) stock rose 3.68% to $463.11 on a strong trading day for the overall market, outperforming the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This gain snapped a two-day losing streak for Costco, although the stock remained below its 52-week high. Competitors Walmart, Target, and Dollar General also saw gains.

title: BJ's Wholesale breaks ground in Middle Tennessee, first location in the state
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club has broken ground on its first Tennessee location in Rutherford County, specifically in La Vergne. The new membership-only retail store, similar to Sam's Club or Costco, will include a 108,000 square-foot building, a fuel center, and space for additional retail. This development follows over three years of discussions between BJ's and local La Vergne officials.

title: Demo work first step in redeveloping former Art Van site in Royal Oak
summary: Demolition work has begun at the former Art Van Furniture store in Royal Oak, marking the first step in its redevelopment into a new headquarters for Agree Realty Corp. The $20 million project will transform the 50,000-square-foot building into a high-end office space, relocating 100 jobs from Bloomfield Hills to Royal Oak. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology, environmentally friendly features, and amenities like a cafe, wellness center, and training facilities for employees.

title: Costco buys remaining 45 percent of Taiwan joint venture
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has acquired the remaining 45 percent stake in its Taiwan joint venture for US$1.05 billion, making it the sole owner of the Costco warehouse club in Taiwan. This purchase was announced on Thursday. The full details are available to subscribed members of the CNA English news archive.

title: Costco gains complete control over Taiwan branch
summary: Costco Wholesale has taken complete control over Costco Taiwan by purchasing the remaining 45% stake it did not already own for US$1.05 billion. This transaction signifies a major shift in Taiwan's retail landscape, with Costco now owning all 14 of its stores across the island, which serve over 3 million members. The sale by the President Group provides them with significant capital for new projects.

title: US’ Costco buys out its local partner for US$1.05bn
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp has acquired the remaining 45 percent stake in its joint venture, Costco President Taiwan Inc, for US$1.05 billion, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary. This move is expected to add 1 to 1.5 percent to Costco's earnings per share. Three of Taiwan's Costco stores are among the top 10 most profitable worldwide, highlighting the market's success.

title: Costco Wholesale Corporation Acquires Minority Interest In Costco-Taiwan
summary: Costco Wholesale Corporation has acquired the remaining 45% minority interest in its joint venture Costco-Taiwan for $1.05 billion (€1 billion), now owning the entity entirely. This purchase is expected to boost Costco's earnings per share by one to one and a half percent. The company continues its international expansion, with plans for new stores in Australia and considering China as a growth market, despite recent challenges like declining gross margins due to increased freight and labor costs.

title: What’s the Most Expensive Twin Cities Supermarket Chain?
summary: This article investigates which Twin Cities supermarket chain is the most expensive by comparing prices for a 31-item grocery list across Lunds & Byerlys, Kowalski's, Target, Cub Foods, and Hy-Vee. The study found Target to be the cheapest at $123.92, while Lunds & Byerlys ($164.63) and Kowalski's ($158.25) were the most expensive. The piece also delves into the market share, history, and "vibes" of each grocery store, noting the impact of inflation on food prices.

title: Brambles bows out of Costco's plastic pallet transition
summary: Brambles Ltd. has decided to discontinue its plastic pallet program for Costco warehouse stores, citing excessively high costs. The company had been involved in facilitating Costco's transition to plastic pallets, but found the endeavor to be financially unfeasible. This decision marks a significant development in the logistics and retail sectors' efforts toward sustainable packaging solutions.

title: Costco Raises Prices on Two of Its Food Court Mainstays
summary: Costco has increased the prices of its chicken bake and 20-ounce soda at its food courts nationwide. The chicken bake went from $2.99 to $3.99, and the soda price increased by 10 cents to $0.69. Despite these changes, the iconic $1.50 hot dog and soda combo remains unchanged, a price it has held since the mid-1980s.

title: Costco Sales up 20.4 Per Cent in June
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported significant financial growth in June, with net sales increasing by 20.4 per cent to $22.78 billion. This surge was partially attributed to higher gas prices and an additional shopping day in the U.S. Comparable sales rose by 18.1 per cent overall, with strong performances in the U.S. and other international markets, while e-commerce comparable sales also saw an increase.

title: Parker Shi
summary: Parker Shi, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of East West Bank (EWB), discusses the community ties influencing EWB’s digital journey, its commitment to the underserved, and the importance of consistency in its operations. The article highlights EWB's growth from a niche institution into a mainstream commercial bank and its innovative approach to digital transformation, aiming to create a "financial Costco" for its customers.

title: Two single-tenant North Carolina retail properties sell for $23.93M
summary: JLL Capital Markets announced the $23.93 million sale of two single-tenant retail properties in Durham, North Carolina: a 120,000-square-foot Home Depot and a 148,663-square-foot Costco. Armada Hoffler Properties sold the properties to a New York-based buyer at a blended 4.0 percent cap rate. Both retailers operate under long-term absolute NNN ground leases in a high-visibility location near Duke University.

title: How US businesses are cashing in on the 'made in Hawaii' label
summary: Many products marketed with a "made in Hawaii" label are not actually produced in the state, leading to consumer confusion and a lack of economic benefits for Hawaii. Brands like Frito-Lay and King's Hawaiian use misleading branding, hindering local entrepreneurship and job creation. Initiatives like Mana Up are working to help authentic Hawaiian businesses thrive and educate consumers on identifying genuine local products.

title: Walmart partnership expands The Honest Company’s reach
summary: The Honest Company is expanding its distribution network by partnering with Walmart, making its products available on Walmart's website and in physical stores this fall. This move aims to increase accessibility for customers and generate capital to support the company's growth, which has historically relied significantly on retail partnerships, including Target, Amazon, and Costco. The expansion is part of Honest Company's omni-channel retail strategy and Walmart's effort to offer trustworthy products.

title: Няколко акции с висок растеж за млади инвеститори
summary: This article identifies several high-growth stocks suitable for young investors, emphasizing the power of long-term investing and compound interest. Despite recent market challenges, the piece argues that growth stocks historically outperform and will lead a recovery. It highlights specific companies like Airbnb, Booking, Costco Wholesale, and Monster Beverage, detailing their recent financial performance and strategic moves.

title: Walmart Cuts Full-Year Profit Outlook
summary: Walmart Inc. has cut its annual profit outlook for the second time this year, citing the need to lower prices to clear out bloated inventories. The company now expects adjusted earnings per share to fall as much as 13% in the current fiscal year due to consumers shifting spending to necessities amid soaring inflation. This follows a previous forecast of only a 1% dip and mirrors similar challenges faced by other retailers like Target.

title: How a little-known stock soared 21,000% to overtake Costco
summary: AMTD Digital, a previously little-known Hong Kong-based financial services startup, saw its stock surge by 21,000% since its IPO less than a month ago, becoming the latest focus for Reddit traders on WallStreetBets. This dramatic rise, which saw its market cap surpass Shell and Costco, echoes the GameStop and AMC frenzies of January 2021. The company itself stated it was unaware of "material circumstances" driving the sudden increase.

title: How is grocery delivering on DEI?
summary: The article examines the progress of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives within the grocery industry, highlighting how the antiracist protests of summer 2020 served as a catalyst for change. It discusses the mixed responses from major grocers like Kroger and Publix, noting the tensions between corporate messaging and store-level policies. The piece emphasizes the growing focus on supplier diversity, corporate transparency, and consumer-led pushes for inclusion, with Walmart cited as a gold standard for its comprehensive ESG reporting and diverse hiring goals.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market Surpasses Expectations in Q2
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market reported strong second-quarter results, with net sales reaching $1.6 billion, a 5% increase year-over-year, and comparable-store sales growth of 2.0%. The healthy grocer's performance was attributed to disciplined execution of its long-term strategy, including new store openings and strategic partnerships like those with Pod Foods and Instacart for SNAP payments. Despite inflationary pressures, Sprouts remains cautiously optimistic and reaffirmed its full-year 2022 outlook, planning continued investment in new stores and capital expenditures.

title: UNFI Produce Implements New Technologies and Processes; Expands Private Label Options
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) Produce has implemented new technologies and processes to enhance freshness and shorten delivery times by over a day. These initiatives include a redesigned sourcing strategy and the use of the real-time quality control program, Share-ify. Concurrently, UNFI is expanding its Wild Harvest organic private label line with additional items following the successful launch of organic bananas.

title: Nehal Modi Sentenced to 3-9 Years in Grand Larceny Case
summary: Nehal Modi has been sentenced to three to nine years in state prison for grand larceny. Modi defrauded LLD Diamonds of millions by falsely claiming a deal with Costco to obtain diamonds, which he then pawned for personal gain. His attorney plans to file an appeal.

title: This Specialty Grocery Chain Is Making a Comeback After Closing Locations
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market, a specialty grocery chain, is making a comeback despite inflation and consumer reluctance to spend on higher-priced organic produce. After struggling with sales and closing 15 locations, the company reported a positive 5% sales increase in the second quarter of the year. While Sprouts remains cautiously optimistic about the economic outlook, convenience-focused items and online sales have contributed to its recent growth.

title: Costco COBRA $750K class action settlement
summary: Costco has agreed to a $750,000 class action settlement over allegations that it failed to adequately notify almost 40,000 current and former employees of their COBRA eligibility. The settlement aims to compensate class members who did not elect COBRA coverage due to insufficient notification between June 9, 2018, and June 9, 2021. Eligible class members are expected to receive around $9.72 from the settlement fund after attorney fees and administration costs.

title: Save money on your next flight by purchasing Southwest gift cards at Costco
summary: Costco is offering a deal on Southwest Airlines eGift cards, allowing members to purchase a $500 gift card for $449.99, saving $50 on future travel. These eGift cards can be used for flights booked through Southwest but not for vacation packages, hotels, rental cars, or merchandise. There's a limit of five per customer, potentially saving up to $250.

title: Weis Markets hires John Driscoll as construction VP
summary: Weis Markets has appointed John Driscoll as Vice President of Construction and Store Development, reporting to Rusty Graber, senior vice president of real estate and development. Driscoll brings 20 years of experience, previously leading teams at H-E-B for new stores, remodels, and expansions. This hire follows Weis Markets' decision to increase its capital expenditures budget by 11% to $150 million for 2022, focusing on new stores, remodels, and IT upgrades.

title: Costco project development underway in Jackson Township
summary: Development for a new Costco warehouse store, convenience store, and gas station is underway in Jackson Township, Ohio, on an 18.25-acre site. Costco acquired the land for $5.83 million, and building construction is expected to begin in September, with an anticipated opening in 2023. The project will anchor the Creekside Crossing development, with additional land still available for future development.

title: CoCo carves out a new RTD category with coconut vodka and rum
summary: CoCo, a Toronto-based startup, has successfully created a new ready-to-drink (RTD) category with its CoCo Vodka and CoCo Rum, which combine spirits with real coconut water. Founded by a lawyer and a sales consultant, the brand leveraged the health-conscious image of coconut water and innovative influencer marketing to gain widespread distribution. Despite impending competition from major players like Diageo, CoCo has established a strong market presence and built a strategy to protect its brand.

title: Mann Packing Company Brings Mèzete Hummus to Costco Canada East Club Stores
summary: Mèzete Hummus is expanding into the Canadian market through a partnership with Mann Packing Company, bringing its gourmet hummus variety pack to select Costco Canada East Club Stores in Ontario and Quebec. The shelf-stable product, made with 100% natural ingredients and no preservatives, includes Zesty Mixed Herbs and Fire Roasted Red Pepper flavors. This expansion highlights Mèzete's mission to offer authentic Eastern Mediterranean flavors and health-conscious foods globally.

title: Costco $3.2M ERISA Class Action Settlement Granted Final Approval
summary: A $3.2 million class action settlement against Costco has received final court approval. The lawsuit alleged that Costco mismanaged its 401(k) plan, leading to excessive administrative and investment management fees, in violation of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Current plan participants will receive an administrative fee reduction, and former participants can claim payments based on their account balance during the class period.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) stock fell 0.06% on Wednesday, underperforming the broader market and several competitors like Walmart, Costco, and Target. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for the company, with its shares closing $14.76 below its 52-week high. The trading volume for Dollar General also exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Buying a Sam’s Club membership is about to get more expensive
summary: Sam’s Club is increasing its membership fees for the first time in nine years, with the basic Club membership rising to $50 and the Plus membership to $110, effective October 17. To mitigate the impact of the price hike during a period of high inflation, Sam’s Club will return the extra cost to members in the form of Sam’s Cash for renewals made through mid-October 2023. This move comes as warehouse stores, including competitor Costco, are seeing increased demand, and speculation grows that Costco may also raise its fees soon.

title: Nvidia’s Red Scare, Costco’s Going “There” & No Campbell’s Soup For You!
summary: Nvidia experienced a significant stock drop after the U.S. Commerce Department restricted the sale of its AI-related chips to China and Russia, citing national security concerns, which is expected to cost the company $400 million quarterly. Meanwhile, Costco is rumored to be considering a membership fee increase following a similar move by Sam's Club, and Campbell's reported earnings highlighted the impact of inflation on food production costs. The article also touches on Micron's investment in a new chipmaking plant and Signet Jewelers' mixed quarterly results amidst inflation fears.

title: It’s not just you. Tommy Bahama beach chairs are everywhere
summary: Tommy Bahama has unexpectedly dominated the beach chair market, controlling an estimated 80% of chairs priced over $30, despite initially struggling as a brand. Their success stems from a savvy licensing deal with ShelterLogic Group, strategic distribution through Costco, and innovative chair features like backpack straps. The chairs have become a powerful marketing tool, reinforcing Tommy Bahama's lifestyle brand and driving sales for other beach gear.

title: Sales Per Square Foot: Retail Calculations & Metrics (2024)
summary: This article explains the retail metric "sales per square foot," detailing its calculation and importance for brick-and-mortar stores. It covers how this metric helps measure store performance, inform merchandising decisions, analyze staff productivity, and identify sales trends over time. The article also discusses the limitations of sales per square foot, particularly in the age of omnichannel retail, and provides strategies to increase it, such as improving store layout, building loyalty programs, and leveraging online audiences.

title: Costco proposes new store in west Roseville
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is reportedly planning to open a new store in west Roseville, according to recent plans filed with the city. This potential expansion indicates Costco's continued interest in the greater Sacramento area, following previous discussions and plans for other regional locations.

title: Dollar General’s $1 Groceries Are Here to Stay
summary: Dollar General's CEO, Todd Vasos, announced that the company will continue to offer and expand its $1 grocery items, emphasizing their importance to core shoppers who rely on these low-priced goods to bridge the gap until payday. This strategy comes despite a competitor raising prices and reflects Dollar General's understanding of its customer base and their needs amid economic pressures. The company also continues to expand its DG Fresh initiative for fresh and frozen foods, driving margin growth and attracting new shoppers.

title: Costco's Prescription Program Now Offers Discount Pricing for Glucose Monitoring System
summary: Costco's Member Prescription Program (CMPP) now offers discount pricing for Intuity Medical's POGO Automatic Blood Glucose Monitoring System and POGO Automatic Test Cartridges, aiming to simplify diabetes management for its members. This FDA-cleared system automates blood glucose testing, reducing the financial barrier through CMPP discounts. The program, which is a value-added benefit for Costco members, previously added a migraine treatment device and reflects Costco's broader expansion in health offerings, amidst strong financial performance.

title: Earnings Previews: Costco, FedEx
summary: This article provides earnings previews for Costco (NASDAQ: COST) and FedEx (NYSE: FDX) ahead of their quarterly reports. It details analyst expectations for revenue and EPS for both companies, along with stock performance, price targets, and key factors to watch such as Costco's membership fees and FedEx's operational challenges amidst a global economic slowdown.

title: Costco Gets Conflicted Counsel Disqualified in Slip-and-Fall Row
summary: A federal judge in California has disqualified the Downtown L.A. Law Group from representing a woman in a slip-and-fall case against Costco. The disqualification occurred because one of the firm's attorneys, Anthony Werbin, previously represented Costco in 21 similar cases, creating a conflict of interest due to his access to confidential information. Costco successfully argued that this conflict extended to his new firm.

title: Costco proposes to build distribution center in Mesa
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has submitted plans to the city of Mesa to construct a "merchandise transfer building" near Elliot and Ellsworth roads. The project involves a distribution warehouse, marking a significant development for the retailer in the Phoenix area. This proposal is part of ongoing commercial real estate activity in the region.

title: Smithfield to pay $75M in latest pork antitrust deal
summary: Smithfield Foods has agreed to pay $75 million to settle a price-fixing case involving millions of indirect consumer purchasers, adding to previous settlements with direct purchasers and restaurant owners. This settlement follows a $20 million deal by JBS and stems from a 2018 class-action lawsuit alleging collusion among pork producers to inflate prices. Consumers who purchased pork products from resellers may be eligible for compensation.

title: UNFI executes against its growth strategy, ramps up warehouse automation investment
summary: UNFI ended fiscal year 2022 on a strong note, with net sales of $28.9 billion, an increase of 7.8% from the previous year. The grocery wholesaler plans to significantly invest in warehouse automation and robotics, including a partnership with Symbotic Inc. to implement AI-powered systems in five distribution centers over the next four years. This strategy aims to enhance efficiency, improve customer service, and boost long-term profitability amidst an inflationary environment and supply chain challenges.

title: Costco Hot Dog and Soda Combo Still $1.50, And It Will Be “Forever”
summary: Costco's iconic hot dog and soda combo will remain at its $1.50 price point indefinitely, a promise upheld since 1985. Despite inflation affecting other food court items, Costco CFO Richard Galanti stated that well-performing parts of the business allow them to maintain this aggressive price. The founder, Jim Senegal, famously threatened CEO Craig Jelinek over the price of the hot dog, reinforcing its symbolic importance.

title: Local rapper says he'll take legal action over alleged profiling at Las Vegas retail store
summary: Recording artist Ray “Bay Blu” Ivory is pursuing legal action against Bath & Body Works after an employee allegedly racially profiled him at a Las Vegas retail location. Ivory claims an employee forcibly took shopping bags from him. While the employee has been terminated and Bath & Body Works issued an apology, Ivory and his spokesperson, Rev. Stretch Sanders, state that legal action will still be taken to ensure accountability and promote racial equity training within the retail industry.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Dollar General Corp. stock increased by 3.00% to $246.48 on a strong trading day for the stock market. The company's stock outperformed competitors like Walmart Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., and Target Corp. This rise marked the second consecutive day of gains for Dollar General Corp.

title: Costco sets date to close Springdale store location, open Liberty Township
summary: Costco has scheduled the closure of its Springdale, Cincinnati-area store and will open a new location in Liberty Township the following day. This move consolidates the company's presence in the region. The article highlights the timeline for this transition and references previous related news about Costco's plans in Cincinnati.

title: How Skelly the 12-foot Home Depot skeleton became a breakout Halloween hit
summary: Home Depot's 12-foot skeleton decoration, affectionately known as Skelly, has become a massive Halloween hit since its debut in 2020. Despite its large size, customers eagerly buy it, with some even facing a "skeleton black market." The article explores the cultural phenomenon behind Skelly and how Home Depot has expanded its line of oversized holiday decorations due to its popularity.

title: As Inflation Rages, Retailers Pump Up Private Label
summary: Amidst rising inflation, retailers are increasingly focusing on developing their private label brands, which are gaining significant market share. While Walmart's private labels reach the most consumers, retailers like Aldi, Target, and Amazon are seeing the fastest growth in household penetration for their own brands. This trend is driven by consumer desire for savings and retailers' pursuit of higher margins and shopper loyalty, impacting purchasing habits across all income levels.

title: You Don't Need a Membership to Shop at Costco Thanks to These Hacks!
summary: While Costco operates as a members-only club, there are several clever ways for non-members to access their products and services without paying the annual fee. These methods include using the pharmacy, buying alcohol, purchasing from the food court, shopping via Instacart (with a surcharge), or using a Costco Shop Card gifted by a member. Additionally, non-members can shop with a member as their guest.

title: Kroger wants people to ‘discover a career’ as it embarks on another hiring spree
summary: Kroger has launched a new hiring campaign aimed at filling "thousands" of jobs ahead of the holiday season, emphasizing long-term career opportunities over temporary roles. The company is actively recruiting across various sectors including retail, e-commerce, and supply chain, and is engaging with prospective employees through virtual hiring events and an "early talent career series." Kroger is also highlighting benefits such as tuition reimbursement, on-demand training, and health resources to attract and retain talent.

title: Kroger To Buy Albertsons, Creating Grocery Giant
summary: Kroger and Albertsons are reportedly in merger discussions that would unite the two largest supermarket chains in the U.S. Kroger announced on Oct. 14 that it is acquiring Albertsons for $24.6B, assuming $4.7B of Albertsons’ debt, in a deal that would create a grocery giant but likely face antitrust review. The companies plan to divest stores in overlapping markets to facilitate regulatory approval.

title: Kroger and Albertsons plan merger to combine 2 largest supermarket chains
summary: Kroger plans to acquire Albertsons in a $24.6 billion deal, merging the two largest U.S. grocery chains. The merger is expected to face intense scrutiny from federal regulators and critics due to concerns about competition and soaring food costs. The companies plan to invest savings in price reductions for customers and increased wages for workers.

title: Kroger and Albertsons Plan $25 Billion Supermarket Merger That May Face Hurdles (Published 2022)
summary: Kroger announced its plan to acquire Albertsons for $24.6 billion, creating a supermarket giant with over $209 billion in annual revenue and approximately 5,000 stores. The merger aims to compete more effectively with big-box retailers like Walmart and Amazon, potentially passing on up to $500 million in savings to customers. However, the deal quickly drew criticism from consumer advocates and politicians concerned about reduced consumer choice, higher prices, and increased corporate concentration in the grocery market.

title: Gerbes parent company Kroger intends to buy Albertsons for $25 billion
summary: Kroger announced its intention to acquire Albertsons in a nearly $25 billion deal, aiming to create one of the largest grocery store chains in the United States and boost its scale against competitors like Amazon and Walmart. The merger, expected to close in 2024, faces significant antitrust scrutiny from regulators, consumer watchdogs, and unions, despite plans to spin off nearly 400 stores. Kroger anticipates using half a billion dollars in cost savings from the merger to invest in lower prices amid high food inflation.

title: 5 things to know about Kroger, which plans to merge with Idaho’s largest company
summary: Kroger and Albertsons announced plans to merge, making Kroger Idaho's largest company. Kroger, the nation's largest traditional grocery retailer, operates under many different brand names and is investing heavily in e-commerce. Despite its size and profitability, Kroger has faced criticism for low wages, which it disputes.

title: Costco receives liquor license approval for potential Noblesville store
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has received approval for a beer, wine, and liquor license for a potential new store in Noblesville, Indiana. The proposed store would be located at the intersection of East 148th Street and North Pointe Boulevard, near State Road 37 and 146th Street. While Costco has not yet made official filings with the city and declined to comment on future warehouses, a Hamilton County Alcoholic Beverage Commission approval was followed by state commission approval.

title: What the Kroger-Albertsons merger means for the retail media landscape
summary: The proposed merger between Kroger and Albertsons, valued at $24.6 billion, poses a significant shift in the retail media landscape by combining their first-party data and expanding their retail footprint. This consolidation could allow the new entity to challenge major players like Walmart in the retail media space, offering brands a more compelling advertising platform with a broader reach and richer data for ad targeting. Experts suggest this merger will highlight the growing importance of physical stores and data scale in the future of retail media, potentially benefiting the combined company in a challenging economic environment.

title: Kroger Bets $25 Billion on Bulking Up to Be More Like Walmart
summary: Kroger is making a $24.6 billion bid to acquire Albertsons, aiming to compete more effectively with Walmart and Amazon by investing in lower prices, enhanced technology, and data utilization. The merger faces significant antitrust scrutiny from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, as critics and analysts debate its potential effects on consumer prices, competition, and the retail landscape. Despite regulatory hurdles and immediate stock drops for both companies, Kroger asserts the deal will ultimately benefit customers through price reductions and improved services.

title: Fresh Del Monte Produce Rolls Out Grandissimo Gold™ Pineapple
summary: Fresh Del Monte Produce has introduced its new Grandissimo Gold™ pineapple in North America, a larger-sized offering that provides more fruit while maintaining the quality and sweetness of their traditional pineapples. This new product is targeted at retailers and shoppers looking for versatile, larger fruit for cooking and is available at select BJ’s Wholesale Club, Costco, and Sam’s Clubs locations in 13 states. Fresh Del Monte emphasizes sustainable practices in its production and distribution.

title: Will my grocery store close? Here’s what a Kroger-Albertsons merger could mean for California
summary: A proposed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons could significantly impact California grocery shoppers and workers. The deal, which involves major California brands like Ralphs, Safeway, and Vons, faces scrutiny from antitrust regulators and concerns from unions and community advocates about potential store closures, job losses, and the creation of "food deserts," especially given the troubled history of the 2015 Albertsons-Safeway merger.

title: Sprouts prepares to debut its first in-store coffee bar
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market is piloting its first in-store coffee bar at a Phoenix location, partnering with local roaster Press Coffee. This initiative aims to enhance the customer experience and align with Sprouts' strategy of focusing on smaller, more efficient store formats and a wider selection of prepared foods. The pilot is part of Sprouts' ongoing efforts to boost sales growth and engage health-conscious shoppers.

title: Mortgages in Walmart – what’s behind the relationship?
summary: Lenders One Cooperative has launched its first in-store mortgage branch locations within select Walmart stores in Florida and New Jersey, aiming to provide easier access to mortgage origination services for shoppers. This initiative is unique, as other major retailers have not pursued similar programs. The strategy leverages Walmart's high customer traffic and trusted brand to connect potential borrowers with loan officers for face-to-face assistance and education.

title: Sam’s Club finishes chainwide deployment of inventory-scanning robots
summary: Sam's Club has completed the chainwide deployment of Inventory Scan automated robots across its nearly 600 stores. These robots, originally used for floor scrubbing, have been upgraded to also collect product availability, pricing data, planogram compliance, and stock levels. This initiative aligns with parent company Walmart's broader push into automation and AI technology to improve efficiency and free up associates for member engagement.

title: Costco buys land in Chaska; store could open in fall 2023
summary: Costco has purchased land in Chaska for a new 164,500-square-foot store, which is anticipated to open in fall 2023. The new location will be situated near Hazeltine National Golf Club. This development follows previous reports of Chaska being a potential site for a Costco store.

title: Just Sold: Costco site in Chaska sells for $8 million
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has acquired an $8 million site in Chaska, Minnesota, for a new 164,000-square-foot store, closing the deal on October 7th. This purchase is part of ongoing development near the former Oak Ridge Hotel and Conference Center, which is being redeveloped. Additionally, a 19,777-square-foot Goodwill retail store in Chanhassen sold for $5.7 million to a private investor.

title: Flows Into Consumer Staples ETFs Rebound on Economic Uncertainty
summary: Investors are increasingly moving back into consumer staples ETFs, a defensive strategy during economic uncertainty. The Invesco S&P 500® Equal Weight Consumer Staples ETF (RHS) has seen significant net inflows, indicating a preference for equal-weighted approaches to mitigate company-specific risks that are common in market-cap weighted funds dominated by a few large companies. This shift reflects advisors' search for downside protection while still participating in market upside in the current economic climate.

title: Tilray Brands Add Montauk Brewing Company To Its Growing Beverage Roster
summary: Tilray Brands, a global cannabis company, has acquired Montauk Brewing Company to further

title: Cannabis company Tilray to buy New York brewer Montauk Brewing Company
summary: Tilray Brands Inc., a cannabis company, has acquired Montauk Brewing Company to expand its U.S. alcohol division. The acquisition is expected to be accretive to Tilray’s adjusted EBITDA. Tilray also plans to leverage these beverage brands to create THC-infused products if cannabis becomes federally legal in the U.S.

title: Cannabis Business Tilray Brands Acquires Montauk Brewing Company
summary: Tilray Brands, a global cannabis lifestyle and consumer packaged goods company, has acquired Montauk Brewing Company for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition strengthens Tilray's U.S. beverage-alcohol segment and is part of their long-term strategy to introduce THC-based products upon federal legalization. Montauk Brewing, founded in 2012, has seen significant growth, distributing its beer across 6,400 points and is described as the fastest-growing beer brand and #1 craft brewer in Metro New York.

title: Tilray Brands Acquires Montauk Brewing Company
summary: Tilray Brands Inc. has acquired Montauk Brewing Company, aiming to strengthen its U.S. footprint and expand its beverage-alcohol segment. This acquisition is expected to be accretive to adjusted EBITDA, leverage SweetWater's nationwide infrastructure for distribution, and position Tilray for future THC-based product launches upon federal legalization. Ty H. Gilmore has been appointed President of Tilray's U.S. beer business to optimize the growing craft beer portfolio.

title: Costco Balances Daily Ops With Commitments to People and the Planet
summary: Costco is actively balancing its business growth with strong commitments to its employees, communities, and the environment. The company highlights its premium employee benefits, high wages, and low turnover rates, alongside significant charitable contributions. Environmentally, Costco is pursuing ambitious climate action goals, including pilot programs for decarbonization and efforts to ensure sustainable and humane practices in its unique vertically integrated poultry operations.

title: How Costco Leverages Loyalty to Drive Growth
summary: Costco's success is attributed to its strong membership loyalty, evidenced by high renewal rates and top rankings in customer and employee surveys. The company maintains robust financial performance with significant net sales and income, attributing growth partly to value-seeking shoppers during inflation and stable pricing on popular food items. Despite rising operating costs, Costco continues its global expansion and sees increased traffic, adapting to evolving consumer purchasing habits.

title: Costco reveals possible opening date for Kyle store
summary: Costco is expected to open a new store in Kyle, Texas, in March at the northwest corner of I-35 and Kohlers Crossing. The big-box retailer is projected to create hundreds of jobs and contribute $14.4 million in annual payroll, attracting more tenants to the Dry River District. This opening is anticipated to significantly impact the local retail landscape.

title: Appeal filed disputing approvals for Natomas Costco project
summary: A local resident has filed an appeal disputing the Sacramento Planning and Design Commission's approval of plans for a new Costco Wholesale Corp. store in Natomas. This development comes after previous reports of Costco's intentions to build a store in the area and related retail development sales. The project faces a new hurdle with this official challenge to its approvals.

title: Core-Mark deal, inflation fuel surge in PFG’s c-store segment
summary: Performance Food Group's convenience-store division experienced a significant boost in its most recent fiscal quarter, driven primarily by the acquisition of Core-Mark a year ago and rising inflation. The c-store division's net sales grew 98.2% year over year to $6.3 billion, largely due to Core-Mark's contribution of $4.7 billion and growth in non-tobacco categories. PFG expects continued growth in this segment, although inflation-driven gains are anticipated to moderate.

title: Del Monte expands availability of Pinkglow pineapples
summary: Del Monte Fresh Produce has announced an expanded retail availability for its exclusive Pinkglow™ Pineapple across select U.S. markets. Previously available online, the unique pink-fleshed fruit, grown in Costa Rica over 24 months, can now be purchased at various grocery chains including Ingles, Lowe's, and Giant Martins Ahold. Del Monte expects the expansion to meet consumer demand for the sweet and juicy pineapple, which is also promoted as a holiday gift item.

title: FDA approves Costco for verified importer program
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has become the first participant approved by the Food and Drug Administration for its Voluntary Qualified Importer Program (VQIP). This fee-based program allows Costco to expedite the review and importation of foods into the U.S. by demonstrating the safety and security of its supply chains. Participants must also ensure their foreign suppliers are certified through the FDA’s Accredited Third-Party Program.

title: I found four items at Dollar Tree for your Thanksgiving meal
summary: A DIY professional, Christinia Renee, shared four budget-friendly Thanksgiving items available at Dollar Tree for just $1.25 each. These items include serving bowls, decorative pumpkin clips, fall harvest cookie cutters, and a cupcake kit. The article emphasizes that while these items are affordable, shoppers should still compare prices and check local store availability.

title: Fresh Del Monte Produce launches large-size pineapple branded Grandissimo Gold
summary: Fresh Del Monte Produce Inc. has launched a new large-sized pineapple called Grandissimo Gold. This new product offers the same quality and sweetness as the traditional Del Monte Gold Extra Sweet pineapple but provides approximately 25% more fruit per pineapple. Grandissimo Gold is currently available at select club stores in 13 states.

title: Walmart’s Grocery Gains Power Sales Beat and Stock Jump
summary: Walmart Inc. saw its stock jump after reporting strong third-quarter results and raising its annual forecast, largely driven by significant grocery sales gains. The retail giant's profit and sales exceeded analyst expectations, leading to a 7.7% stock increase, its largest since September 2020. CEO Doug McMillon highlighted improved inventory and market share gains in the grocery category, especially with Walmart U.S. comparable sales climbing 8.2%.

title: Walmart lifts annual forecast, announces $20 bln share buyback
summary: Walmart increased its annual sales and profit forecast due to sustained grocery demand and successful inventory reduction through discounts ahead of the holiday season. The company also announced a new $20 billion share buyback plan, boosting its stock and those of other major retailers. Despite macroeconomic uncertainties and high food inflation, Walmart expects to gain market share, although it anticipates a more promotional holiday period and potential slowdown in general merchandise spending.

title: Costco closes its Springdale location, opens in Liberty Township
summary: Costco closed its Springdale, Cincinnati location on November 15, 2022, and concurrently opened a new retail store in Liberty Township on November 16, 2022. This move consolidates Costco's presence in the Cincinnati area.

title: eBay Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: On Thursday, November 17, 2022, eBay Inc. stock (EBAY) fell by 0.04% to $45.47, underperforming the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones. Despite this daily loss, eBay outperformed competitors such as Amazon.com Inc., Walmart Inc., and Costco Wholesale Corp., which experienced larger declines. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, with trading volume also below its 50-day average.

title: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings Third Quarter 2023 Earnings: Beats Expectations
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings reported strong third-quarter 2023 earnings, surpassing analyst expectations for both revenue and earnings per share. The company's revenue increased by 12% year-over-year to US$4.79 billion, and net income grew by 3.8% to US$131.4 million. Despite a slight decrease in profit margin due to higher expenses, future revenue growth is projected to outpace the industry average.

title: Costco could put delivery warehouse in Cedar Park
summary: Costco is reportedly looking to establish a new delivery warehouse in Cedar Park, a northern suburb of Austin, Texas. This move is part of the expansion of Costco Logistics, the company's division responsible for home delivery of large items, aiming to operate more like Amazon. The proposed facility would enhance Costco's national network of logistics hubs.

title: Inflation Drives Holiday Bargain Hunt
summary: A Morgan Stanley Research survey indicates that holiday shoppers are greatly influenced by inflation, leading 70% to wait for discounts before purchasing. Consumers are prioritizing experiences like travel over big-ticket items such as electronics and luxury goods. Retailers are expected to offer competitive prices due to oversupply, potentially impacting their profit margins.

title: Costco buys land for future store in growing West Valley city
summary: Costco (COST) has purchased land in a rapidly growing West Valley city in the Phoenix metropolitan area, signaling plans for a new store. This move solidifies the company's expansion strategy within the Valley. The article highlights several related developments including other retail expansions and new businesses coming to the West Valley.

title: How High Tide Became the ‘Costco of Cannabis’
summary: High Tide, a retail-focused cannabis company, has achieved significant growth despite market challenges by adopting a discount club retail model, similar to Costco. Their Canna Cabana brand offers market and member pricing, and the company plans to launch a paid membership called Cabana Elite, building on its successful loyalty program with over 825,000 members. High Tide is also eying expansion into the U.S. and European markets, particularly Germany, if cannabis legalization progresses.

title: Albertsons-Kroger mega-deal raises questions from lawmakers about higher food prices
summary: Lawmakers on a U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee panel have expressed serious concerns over the proposed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons, two of the largest U.S. supermarket chains. Senators, including Amy Klobuchar and Mike Lee, grilled the CEOs of both companies, fearing the merger could lead to higher food prices for consumers and a monopoly on groceries. Concerns also included potential layoffs, store closures, and the impact on competition, particularly given a problematic past merger between Albertsons and Safeway in 2015.

title: PriceSmart Confirms New Colombia Unit
summary: PriceSmart will open a second store in Medellín, Colombia, in 2023, bringing its total to 10 locations in the country and 52 in Latin America. The company also plans to open a warehouse club in San Miguel, El Salvador, in spring 2023. PriceSmart, owned by Costco, emphasized its commitment to local brands and its strategy of offering a limited number of products without extensive advertising to compete in the wholesale market.

title: Kroger, Albertsons CEOs Face Senate Questions Over Merger
summary: The CEOs of Kroger and Albertsons faced questioning from Senators regarding their proposed $24.6 billion merger. Lawmakers, including Senators Amy Klobuchar and Mike Lee, expressed concerns that the deal, which aims to create a supermarket giant, could lead to higher food prices and reduced competition in the grocery market. Despite company assurances of lower prices and enhanced competition, opposition from consumer groups and a labor union, along with the FTC's scrutiny, suggest a challenging antitrust review for the merger expected to close in early 2024.

title: Kyle's Dry River District fills with food, retail tenants
summary: The Dry River District in Kyle is seeing its second phase fully leased, with construction underway and plans for a third phase. Despite potential recession concerns, the retail market is showing optimism, with new food and retail tenants moving into the mixed-use development south of Austin. The project by Endeavor is expected to grow to approximately 300,000 square feet.

title: Costco named Yahoo Finance's company of the year
summary: Costco has been named Yahoo Finance's Company of the Year, marking it as the 11th company to receive this prestigious award. The CEO of Costco believes the company could double in size within the next decade.

title: The Best Time to Shop at Ross Is in January—Here’s Why
summary: Bargain hunters suggest that January is the optimal time to shop at Ross Dress for Less, despite the store's popularity during the holiday season. This is due to Ross following a retail calendar that typically ends in late January, leading to significant markdowns as low as $0.49 to clear out merchandise before new inventory arrives in February. While some former employees corroborate this annual sale, current employees and other shoppers note that deep discounts might be store-specific or simply part of continuous markdowns rather than a formal company-wide event.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) shares declined 0.20% on a generally poor trading day for the stock market, though the company still outperformed several key competitors like Amazon, Walmart, and Costco. Despite the daily loss, the stock broke a two-day winning streak and closed below its 52-week high. Trading volume was higher than its 50-day average.

title: Holiday hours 2022: When Walmart, Target, Best Buy are open through Christmas Eve
summary: Major retailers like Target, Best Buy, and Kohl's are extending their store hours through Christmas Eve 2022 to accommodate holiday shoppers. Walmart, however, is maintaining its normal operating hours but will close by 6 PM on Christmas Eve. The increase in physical store visits this holiday season highlights a resurgence in in-person shopping, contrasting with a continued but slower growth in online purchases.

title: Costco 'purposely coy' on when it will hike membership fees
summary: Issaquah-based wholesaler Costco has been hinting for months at an increase in its annual membership dues, which would be the first such hike in over five years. The company remains intentionally vague about the exact timing of this potential fee increase.

title: Kroger Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Kroger Co. (KR) stock fell 2.70% on Tuesday, closing at $45.45, despite an overall positive trading session for the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones. This performance saw Kroger underperform against some key competitors, including Amazon.com Inc. which rose, and Walmart Inc. and Costco Wholesale Corp. which experienced smaller movements. The stock traded below its 50-day average volume and remained significantly below its 52-week high.

title: DI wealth advisor hits Wall Street, launches fund on NYSE
summary: Daniel Island resident Adam Curran, founder of Curran Financial Partners, has launched a new ETF on the NYSE called the "God Bless America ETF" under the ticker "YALL." The fund, valued at over $25 million, invests in American-based companies that prioritize profits over political activism. This achievement marks a lifelong dream for Curran, who plans to ring the NYSE bell in January to celebrate.

title: 10 unique last-minute holiday gifts you can score on Groupon — up to 90% off
summary: This article highlights 10 unique last-minute holiday gift ideas available on Groupon, with potential savings of up to 90%. Recommendations include custom canvas prints, wine samplers, daycation gift certificates, meal kits, flower delivery, personalized photo cards, custom puzzles, Krispy Kreme gift cards, personalized children's books, and Groupon gift cards. The article also provides instructions on how to gift Groupon vouchers and emphasizes their affordability and convenience for thoughtful presents.

title: Target SWOT Analysis (2025)
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of Target Corporation for 2025, examining its strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats within the retail industry. It details Target's history, diverse store formats, financial performance, and strategic initiatives, while also highlighting challenges such as perceived high prices, data security issues, and intense competition. The analysis concludes with an assessment of Target's potential for future growth amidst evolving market dynamics and increasing e-commerce trends.

title: Is Costco open on New Year’s Day 2023?
summary: Costco will be closed on New Year’s Day 2023, making it one of seven days out of the year the warehouse store is not open to shoppers. This means bulk shoppers will need to wait until January 2nd to visit Costco. Alternative grocery options are available for those needing supplies on January 1st, with most operating under normal business hours.

title: Dollar General CEO to Retire, Names Successor
summary: Todd Vasos, Dollar General's CEO, will retire in November after serving since 2015, during which time he oversaw the addition of approximately 7,000 new stores and an 80% increase in annual sales. He will be succeeded by Chief Operating Officer Jeffery Owen, age 52, who will take over on November 1. Mr. Vasos helped expand the company into new categories like fresh produce, further strengthening the discount retailer's reach.

title: Costco could be planning a new business center in East Valley
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is reportedly planning a new business center in the East Valley, potentially backfilling a former Fry's Electronics store in Tempe. This proposed 148,000 square-foot center on a 15-acre site could open in late 2023, though the timeline is uncertain. While plans were submitted to the city to modify the building's exterior, no formal permits have yet been requested.

title: Costco buys land for future store in growing West Valley city
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. recently purchased 22 acres of land in Buckeye, Arizona, for $5.7 million to build a new wholesale and retail store. This new Costco will anchor Buckeye Commons, a 411,000-square-foot shopping and retail center. While a Queen Creek location is set to open in January 2023, the Buckeye store's opening date has not yet been announced.

title: Costco proposes to build distribution center in Mesa
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has submitted plans to the city of Mesa to construct a new distribution warehouse. This 120,000-square-foot facility would primarily be used to store and ship large, bulky items like furniture and appliances directly to customer homes, rather than serving as another retail store. The proposed "merchandise transfer building" will include an office component and be located near Elliot and Ellsworth roads.

title: Costco set to anchor new Queen Creek development
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is constructing a new 165,000-square-foot store with a gas station in Queen Creek, Arizona, expected to open this fall. This Costco will serve as the anchor tenant for Vestar's 300,000-square-foot Queen Creek Crossing development, which is also under construction. The project is located at the northwest corner of Queen Creek and Ellsworth roads.

title: Costco forecast to be huge magnet for One Daytona. Here's why
summary: A new Costco store is expected to open at One Daytona in 2024, anticipated to be a significant draw for the area, much like a recent opening in St. Augustine. Industry experts predict the store will generate over $100 million in sales annually and create 250 new jobs. The arrival of Costco is also generating increased interest from other potential tenants for One Daytona.

title: Inland Private Capital Corporation Delivers 192% with Sale of BJ's Wholesale Club in Gainesville
summary: Inland Private Capital Corporation has sold the BJ's Wholesale Club property in Gainesville, VA, achieving a 192.80% return for investors. The sale was facilitated by DC MSA Retail DST, one of IPC's 1031 investment programs, capitalizing on increased investor demand for warehouse clubs since the pandemic. Since 2021, IPC has monetized over $2.2 billion in real estate through its 1031 exchange platform.

title: Costco to sell Beyond Meat's steak product
summary: Beyond Meat announced that its plant-based steak product would be available at select Costco locations in Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Colorado, and Southern California. This partnership comes as Beyond Meat faces weaker demand and increased competition in the plant-based market, leading to a 22.5% revenue fall in the third quarter and significant operational cost reductions and layoffs. The company aims to highlight the health and environmental benefits of its products to boost sales.

title: Beyond Meat’s Steak Is Now Available at Select Costco Stores. The Stock Got a Lift.
summary: Beyond Meat's stock rose after the company announced its plant-based steak product, Beyond Steak, will be available at over 50 Costco Wholesale stores in the Southwest. This expansion into a major retailer provides a significant boost for the company.

title: Beyond Meat Expands Beyond Steak and Popcorn Chicken to Costco and Sam’s Club
summary: Beyond Meat is expanding the availability of its Beyond Steak and Popcorn Chicken products to wholesale retailers Costco and Sam’s Club. Beyond Steak will be sold in over 50 Costco locations across several Western US states, while Popcorn Chicken is now available in all US Sam’s Club stores, allowing consumers to purchase both in bulk quantities. These plant-based options offer high protein content and are positioned as healthier alternatives to traditional meat products.

title: Costco to buy land for warehouse at expanding Mesa industrial park
summary: Sunbelt Investment Holdings Inc. is expanding its Mesa Elliot Technology Park, with plans including selling 12 acres to Costco for a new warehouse. The development will also feature data centers and speculative buildings. This move indicates significant industrial growth in southeast Mesa.

title: David Chang Slams Costco's $5 Rotisserie Chicken: 'It's Inedible'
summary: Celebrity chef David Chang criticized Costco's $4.99 rotisserie chicken on his podcast, calling it "inedible" due to lack of seasoning, especially when cold. He expressed general satisfaction with other Costco products, like frozen lobster tails and brisket, and advocated for microwave cooking for its simplicity and efficiency. This comes amidst a separate animal welfare lawsuit against Costco concerning its rotisserie chicken suppliers.

title: State rules in favor of Costco, reversing judge's ruling against Stuart in lengthy appeal
summary: A state commission has ruled in favor of a mixed-use Costco project on South Kanner Highway in Stuart, allowing it to proceed. This decision reverses a previous judicial ruling against the city's land-use designation. However, a local resident who challenged the project plans to appeal the commission's ruling in court.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) shares rose 0.31% on Tuesday, closing at $486.77, despite a general market decline for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock outperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Walmart Inc. (WMT), which both saw declines. Costco's trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: SD500 2022: Robert Price
summary: This article profiles Robert Price, co-founder of PriceSmart Inc., a successful warehouse-retail firm with 47 stores in 12 countries. Price, alongside his father Sol Price, originally founded Price Club, which was sold to Costco Wholesale in 1993. He is also manager of The Price Group LLC and president of Price Charities and Price Philanthropies Foundation, supporting charitable activities locally and internationally.

title: Animal rights protesters project images of dying pigs at San Francisco Costco
summary: Animal rights activists protested at a San Francisco Costco, projecting video of pigs dying in a Southern California slaughterhouse and calling on Costco to stop sourcing from Smithfield Foods. The footage, obtained secretly, allegedly shows pigs suffering during carbon dioxide stunning, which activists claim violates the Humane Slaughter Act. Smithfield Foods, however, staunchly defended its practices, stating that carbon dioxide stunning is recognized as a humane method by multiple animal health authorities and that they adhere to all regulations.

title: Walmart Plays Catch-Up As Amazon Pulls Further Ahead Of Its E-Commerce Competitors
summary: Amazon continues to lead the e-commerce sector due to its ongoing innovation and expanding scale, maintaining a widening competitive moat. While Walmart dominates traditional retail, it is aggressively investing to close the e-commerce gap by leveraging its assets and emulating Amazon's strategies. Although Amazon's stock has recently pulled back, the author believes it still offers significant long-term growth potential, whereas Walmart's future growth hinges critically on the flawless execution of its e-commerce strategy.

title: Fresno’s Valley Wide Beverage expands as customers remain thirsty
summary: Valley Wide Beverage, a leading distributor in the Central Valley, has expanded its operations with an additional 150,000 square feet of warehouse space and 20 new loading docks. This expansion follows increased demand during the pandemic and the acquisition of Constellation Brands' product line, including popular beers like Modelo and Corona. Despite concerns about a looming recession, the company anticipates continued growth, citing new developments such as the Great Wolf Lodge and increased retail presence in the region.

title: Association of Food and Drug Officials - 16 People Who Have Shaped the Last 30 Years of Food Safety
summary: This article highlights 16 individuals who have significantly influenced food safety over the past three decades, following the 1992-93 Jack in the Box E. coli outbreak. Authored by Steven Mandernach of the Association of Food and Drug Officials, it discusses changes in food safety practices, technology, and understanding, emphasizing prevention and human behavior. The piece celebrates these leaders for their courage and persistence in improving national and global food supplies.

title: Walmart to raise minimum wage for U.S. hourly workers to $14
summary: Walmart announced it will raise its average hourly wage for U.S. store workers to $17.50, up from $17, with the minimum wage increasing to a range of $14-$19 per hour depending on location. This move, affecting approximately 340,000 workers across 3,000 stores, aims to attract and retain employees in a competitive labor market, though its new minimum still lags behind some rivals like Amazon and Costco. The decision comes amidst moderating U.S. wage growth but a robust labor market.

title: The Makers of Cadet Brand Launch Line of New, Patent-Pending Bully Chews for Dogs
summary: Cadet, a brand under Central Garden & Pet, has launched a new line of patent-pending Bully Hide chews for dogs. These chews combine a bully stick exterior with a beef hide interior, offering an all-natural, highly palatable, and digestible long-lasting option at an affordable price point. The unique technology aims to provide a wholesome treat for pets and their parents.

title: Internet Records Historic $1 Trillion Consumer Milestone
summary: Comscore announced that the internet surpassed $1 trillion in U.S. online retail consumer spending in 2022, marking a 21% year-over-year increase. Mobile devices played a crucial role, accounting for almost 40% of the total digital commerce and growing faster than desktop spending. This milestone highlights the accelerated adoption of online purchasing, with significant growth in categories like event tickets, digital content, and apparel.

title: Amazon’s holiday sales growth outpaced superstore competitors in 2022
summary: Amazon's U.S. consumer sales during the 2022 holiday season grew by 9 percent year-over-year, surpassing its performance in the previous three years. This growth rate outpaced several major superstore competitors like Target and Costco, matching only Walmart. Other retailers such as Best Buy and Bed Bath & Beyond experienced declines in holiday sales.

title: Costco January Comps Fall 15.4 Percent
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported net sales of $16.84 billion for January 2023, a 6.9 percent increase year-over-year. The timing of Lunar New Year negatively impacted January's sales by approximately 0.25 percent for the total company. For the 22 weeks ending January 29, 2023, net sales reached $99.00 billion, up 7.5 percent from the previous year.

title: Costco Comps Gain in January Despite Non-Foods Drop
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported a 6.9% gain in net sales for January, reaching $16.84 billion, with comparable store sales up 7.4% excluding gasoline and foreign exchange volatility. While U.S. comps increased by 6.9% and traffic by 5.1%, e-commerce comps declined by 14.4%. Non-foods categories saw a slight dip, though apparel, health and beauty, and tires performed well, while food and sundries grew in the low single digits and fresh food in the mid-single digits.

title: What Food Retailers Made World’s Most Admired Companies List?
summary: Fortune magazine released its 25th annual World’s Most Admired Companies list, featuring several food retailers. Amazon ranked No. 2, while Costco Wholesale Corp. secured No. 7, and Publix Super Markets placed No. 44, recognized for their customer value, employee support, and social responsibility efforts. Walmart Inc. and Target Corp. also made the list.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) stock fell 1.83% on Thursday, closing at $231.31, despite a mixed trading session with the S&P 500 rising. The stock underperformed several competitors, including Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) which rose, and Walmart Inc. (WMT) and Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) which had varied performances. This decline ended a two-day winning streak for Dollar General, leaving it $30.90 below its 52-week high.
