title: Costco boosting Holbrook store's size for up-to-date layout
summary: Costco is planning to expand its 30-year-old warehouse club in Holbrook, New York, by 18,357 square feet to 147,923 square feet. This expansion aims to modernize the existing services, including pharmacy, administrative offices, and shelf space, bringing the store more in line with Costco's larger standard store model. The project still requires several approvals from local authorities.

title: Pricesmart To Increase Dividends By 7% Appoints Former Costco Executive To Board
summary: PriceSmart (NASDAQ: PSMT) announced a 7% increase in its annual cash dividend, bringing it to $0.92 per share, payable in two installments. The company also appointed John D. Thelan, formerly of Costco, to its expanded board of directors, highlighting confidence in its business model and growth strategy. Interim CEO Robert Price, who is serving without compensation, expressed excitement about re-engaging with the company's daily operations and the strategic value Thelan brings to the board.

title: Jerash Holdings to Report Financial Results for Fiscal 2023 Third Quarter on Monday, February 13, 2023
summary: Jerash Holdings (US), Inc. announced it will release its fiscal 2023 third-quarter financial results before market open on Monday, February 13, 2023. The company will also host an investor conference call the same day at 9:00 a.m. ET to discuss the results. A webcast of the call will be available on Jerash's investor relations website.

title: Israel invites US retail giant Costco to make foray into local food market
summary: Israel's Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has invited US retail giant Costco to enter the Israeli food market in an effort to reduce the high cost of living and increase competition. Smotrich believes this would be mutually beneficial for Costco and Israeli consumers, who face high prices due to a concentrated local market and import barriers. The invitation was met with some ridicule for its poor English phrasing.

title: Judge declines to dismiss lawsuit over Costco's 'dolphin safe' tuna claim
summary: A United States court has allowed a class-action lawsuit against Costco Wholesale Corp. to proceed, challenging its "dolphin-safe" tuna claims. The lawsuit, filed by consumer Melinda Wright, alleges that Costco's canned tuna is falsely advertised as "dolphin-safe," as the fishing methods used reportedly harm and kill dolphins and other marine life. This legal action puts Costco in a challenging position regarding its product labeling and sourcing practices.

title: Costco buys land for Natomas store from Alleghany Properties for $12.8 million
summary: Costco has purchased approximately 19 acres in North Natomas from Alleghany Properties for $12.8 million to build a new store. The parcel is located southeast of Interstate 5 and Arena Boulevard, and Costco has already applied for building permits for the project. This new development is part of Costco's plans for at least three more local stores in various stages of planning.

title: National Black Owned Brewery and Cidery Partner with U.S Black Chambers for Black History Month.
summary: Full Circle Brewing and Sonoma Cider have partnered with ByBlack, powered by U.S. Black Chambers, Inc. (USBC), to release a special beer and cider for Black History Month. This collaboration aims to increase the visibility of Black-owned breweries and address the underrepresentation of Black individuals in the craft beer and cider industry. The new products, "Juicy Vibes Hazy Pale Ale" and "The Sickle Pineapple Cider," will be available at Full Circle Brewing and national retailers, marking the third year of Black History Month releases for Full Circle.

title: Costco Customers Are Confused by Pricey Roast Beef Sandwich
summary: Costco customers are expressing confusion and "sticker shock" over the new $9.99 roast beef sandwich, which is significantly more expensive than other popular food court items like the $1.50 hot dog or $4.99 rotisserie chicken. While some attribute the price to inflation, many patrons are comparing its value unfavorably to an entire pizza for the same price. The sandwich, currently only available in select warehouses, has received mixed reviews, leading some to believe Costco might be testing higher-priced menu items.

title: Are dogs allowed in Costco? (2023 store policy updates)
summary: This article clarifies Costco's policy regarding dogs in their stores, stating that only service animals are permitted. This policy is in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, and employees are allowed to ask two specific questions to verify a service animal's status. The exclusion of other animals is primarily due to state and local health and safety regulations concerning food sanitation in grocery stores.

title: Costco reveals possible opening timeframe for first Georgetown store
summary: Costco is expected to open its first Georgetown store, north of Austin, within months. The new 160,000-square-foot location at 2201 N. I-35 will join existing grocery competitors and may attract other retailers to the area.

title: Costco to Expand into Two New Countries
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported second-quarter earnings that surpassed Street estimates, despite acknowledging a softening in discretionary sales. The company plans to open 24 new warehouses in its current fiscal year, including its first stores in New Zealand and Sweden, which have already opened. Costco also expects to open additional locations in China, with its capital spending estimated to be between $3.8 billion and $4.2 billion for fiscal year 2023.

title: With Retail Theft Rampant, Will New Deterrents at Walmart, CVS and More Drive Consumers Away?
summary: Retail shrink, primarily due to organized retail crime (ORC), has surged to nearly $100 billion, prompting major retailers like Walmart and CVS to implement new anti-theft measures. While these deterrents aim to combat significant losses, they risk alienating customers who find the shopping experience inconvenient. The industry faces the challenge of balancing security needs with consumer satisfaction, with potential broader responses including legislation and retail-crime associations.

title: Costco Is Having a Truly Unbelievable Deal on Internet-Famous Lovesacs for a Limited Time
summary: Costco is offering a significant discount on Lovesac beanbag chairs and Squattoman bundles, allowing members to save nearly $1,000. The sale, running until April 9th, features the popular furniture filled with shredded Durafoam and covered in faux fur. This limited-time offer makes the comfortable and durable Lovesacs available at a major price reduction, starting at $450.

title: What we know about Costco's potential Gwinnett County store
summary: Costco is reportedly considering the former Stone Mountain Tennis Center in Gwinnett County, Georgia, for a new store location. The company already operates 16 locations across the state. This potential development comes as other areas in metro Atlanta are also seeing significant redevelopment efforts.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market in The Villages
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market has opened its 37th Florida location in Laurel Manor Plaza, The Villages, offering organic, keto, plant-based, and gluten-free foods. The store focuses on fresh, organic, and natural foods at affordable prices, sourcing products from local farms and providing extensive produce and bulk food sections. Sprouts also offers various natural and organic products, private label brands, and educational resources for healthy eating.

title: Beloved clothing store closes - leaving customers scrambling for new options
summary: The clothing retailer Buckle is closing one of its North Carolina stores at Northlake Mall on March 26, following Apple's recent departure from the same location. This closure is linked to a period of scrutiny for the mall due to a series of shootings, which council members say has led to 25% vacancy rates. Despite not citing the shootings as a reason, Buckle will continue operating in nearby malls.

title: Lovesac net sales up 22% in Q4 amid industry pressures
summary: Lovesac reported a 21.7% increase in net sales for Q4, reaching $238.8 million, despite broader industry pressures. The company's full fiscal year net sales grew 30.8% to $651.5 million, attributed to its omnichannel strategy and proprietary products. Lovesac aims for $700 million to $740 million in net sales for fiscal 2024 and is eyeing future international expansion while focusing on domestic market share growth.

title: News | Fresno-Based Nut Producer Cracks Notable Sale-Leaseback Transaction
summary: A Fresno-based nut producer, Caro Nut, completed a significant sale-leaseback transaction with real estate investment trust Stag Industrial for its 233,840-square-foot industrial facility. The deal, valued at approximately $30 million, won a CoStar Impact Award for sale of the year in Fresno, highlighting a growing interest in the city's market from institutional capital. This transaction allowed Caro Nut to retain its operations while gaining financial resources for growth, benefiting the company, its employees, and the local tax base.

title: Costco is spending $4.3M on its Kennewick store. It sounds delicious
summary: Costco is investing $4.3 million to remodel its Kennewick, Washington store, focusing on expanding and upgrading the bakery, rotisserie, dairy, produce, meat prep, and deli areas. This extensive renovation, spanning nearly 10,400 square feet, is being managed by Lydig Construction Inc. and highlights Costco's commitment to improving its only Tri-Cities location. Despite this investment, the city of Pasco continues to hope Costco might build a larger store in their Broadmoor Development, having recently broken ground on infrastructure for future retail expansion.

title: Casselberry approves zoning change for proposed BJ’s Wholesale site
summary: The Casselberry City Commission approved a rezoning request, moving BJ’s Wholesale Club closer to opening a new 101,113-square-foot store at the intersection of U.S. Highway 17-92 and S.R. 436. This new location will be part of the Casselberry Exchange shopping center, repurposing a site previously occupied by Staples and Bed, Bath and Beyond. The development is expected to create approximately 150 jobs and open by the first quarter of 2024.

title: Costco’s Self-Watering Garden Bed Is Back in Time for Spring Planting
summary: Costco is offering a self-watering raised garden bed planter, perfect for spring planting, which is currently on sale. The CedarCraft Self-Watering Elevated Spruce Planter features a 6-gallon irrigation system, is made from sustainable Canadian Spruce, and boasts wheels for easy movement. Manufacturer CedarCraft also plants two trees for every planter purchased on Costco.com, making it a sustainable choice.

title: Costco Falls on Lowest US Sales Growth in Almost Three Years
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. experienced its slowest US comparable sales growth in almost three years, with a mere 0.9% gain in March excluding gasoline impacts. This slowdown has raised concerns about the strength of US consumers and led to a drop in the company's stock. The March results mark the smallest advance since April 2020.

title: iShares Global Consumer Staples ETF (KXI) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides an in-depth look at the iShares Global Consumer Staples ETF (KXI), detailing its stock price, holdings, dividend yield, and key statistics. It highlights top holdings such as Costco, Nestle, PepsiCo, and Philip Morris International, along with historical performance metrics and asset allocation. The report also includes information from its latest N-PORT filing, showing 95 total holdings with a portfolio value of $854.00 million.

title: Legal battle over key aspect of Stuart Costco project drags on, with appeal filed in court
summary: A legal battle concerning a key aspect of the Stuart Costco project is continuing, with resident Robin Cartwright filing an appeal with the Fourth District Court of Appeal. This appeal signals further delays for the controversial mixed-use development, which includes a Costco store, gas station, apartments, and other commercial spaces. The project's future remains uncertain as the court process unfolds.

title: Kroger phasing out mailed circulars across the country
summary: Kroger is transitioning from printed weekly ad circulars to a digital format across various markets due to rising distribution costs and changing consumer habits. While physical copies will still be available in stores, the company views this as a cost-cutting measure and a response to the increasing adoption of digital shopping. Other grocers have also made similar shifts, with digital circulars proving effective in attracting new customers.

title: Costco Unveils New Issaquah Headquarters Addition
summary: Costco has completed a significant expansion of its Issaquah headquarters, adding a 624,788 square-foot, nine-story office tower (Building 4) and a parking garage (Building 5) with an exhibition center and fitness facility. This expansion will allow the company to consolidate approximately 3,750 employees, including IT staff currently in leased buildings, and supports Costco's collaborative culture and hybrid work model. The project represents a substantial investment, valued at around $214 million, and was designed by Seattle-based MG2 with input from the city of Issaquah to ensure functionality, efficiency, and sustainability while integrating with the community.

title: 40 Under 40: Champions of Construction 2022
summary: This article celebrates Autodesk's 40 Under 40: Champions of Construction for 2022, highlighting 40 individuals who are making significant contributions to the construction industry through innovation, leadership, and digital transformation. It details their roles, achievements, and impact on their respective companies and the broader AEC sector. The honorees are recognized for advancing digital maturity, implementing new technologies, and fostering collaborative and sustainable practices.

title: My dad founded one of the world’s biggest gas and oil companies with just $10k
summary: The Duncan family's net worth has grown to $22 billion in two generations, stemming from Dan Duncan's founding of Enterprise Products Co. with just $10,000 in 1968. His daughter, Randa Duncan, now serves as the company's non-executive chairwoman, while her siblings have invested their substantial inheritance. Dan Duncan, who grew up poor, built the company into a major oil and gas entity, owning 51,000 miles of pipeline.

title: Five Below rival with 85 stores 'to file for bankruptcy' after 50 years
summary: Christmas Tree Shops, a discount retailer with 85 stores known for low-priced home furnishings and decorations, is reportedly preparing to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. This comes after 50 years in business and follows its sale by Bed Bath & Beyond in 2020. The potential bankruptcy highlights a trend of financial hardship for "category killer" brands from the early 2000s.

title: FSTA Top Holdings List & Exposure (Fidelity MSCI Consumer Staples Index ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the Fidelity MSCI Consumer Staples Index ETF (FSTA). It lists the top 25 stocks held by the ETF, ranked by weight, which collectively make up 81.38% of the fund. Key holdings include Walmart, Costco Wholesale, and Procter & Gamble, providing a snapshot of FSTA's investment strategy in the consumer staples sector.

title: What drives investment results?
summary: This article explores the various drivers of investment returns based on different time horizons, from short-term sentiment changes and multiple expansions to long-term factors like return on incremental invested capital (ROIIC) and corporate culture. It uses examples like Walmart, Westpac, and Costco to illustrate these concepts, quoting legendary investors Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger on the importance of return on capital. The author emphasizes that while quantitative metrics are important, qualitative aspects like culture play a significant role in long-term success.

title: Grove Collaborative adds Costco, Kroger and Hannaford to list of retail partners
summary: DTC brand Grove Collaborative has expanded its retail presence by adding Costco, Kroger, and Hannaford to its list of partners, bringing its products to 450 new brick-and-mortar stores. This move is part of the company's omnichannel distribution strategy, increasing its total store count to over 5,700 locations. Despite recent financial challenges and a delisting notice from the NYSE, Grove Collaborative aims for profitability in 2024, supported by its growing wholesale network and a refinancing deal.

title: Costco earnings miss estimates as shoppers curb discretionary spending
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) missed quarterly earnings estimates as consumers reduced non-essential spending due to inflation and economic uncertainties. The retailer experienced a drop in demand for high-margin products like home furnishings and electronics, despite a rise in membership revenue. This trend also impacted other major retailers such as Target and Home Depot.

title: Another Drop in E-Commerce Sales for Costco
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. saw a 10% drop in online sales in its third quarter, ending May 7, despite a 1.9% increase in overall net sales to $52.60 billion. The company is actively working on improving its e-commerce platform and mobile apps, including hiring a new VP of digital transformation and implementing a two-year roadmap for improvements. While shopping frequency was up, the average daily transaction value decreased, influenced by weaker sales of big-ticket non-food discretionary items.

title: Costco earnings miss estimates as shoppers curb discretionary spending
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp missed quarterly earnings estimates as shoppers reduced discretionary spending due to high inflation and economic uncertainty. The warehouse retailer, like others, saw a decline in demand for high-margin non-essential items, leading to lower-than-expected profits and revenue. Despite this, membership revenue, which accounts for most of Costco's gross margin, increased.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club to expand to Tennessee
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club announced the opening of its newest club in La Vergne, Tennessee, on June 14, 2023, marking its first location in the state and expanding its footprint to 19 states. The new club will offer various shopping options, including in-club shopping, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery, along with a BJ's Gas location. BJ's is also partnering with the Second Harvest Food Bank of Middle Tennessee to support hunger relief initiatives.

title: More retailers lower sales outlook, say customers are pulling back spending
summary: Macy's and Dollar General reported disappointing first-quarter results, attributing it to customers pulling back spending due to high inflation. Macy's saw a 7% decline in net sales, while Dollar General's earnings fell short of expectations, leading to a stock drop. Other retailers like Costco, Target, and Best Buy have also reported sluggish consumer spending and downgraded outlooks, with a Federal Reserve survey indicating that fewer U.S. adults feel financially secure compared to previous years.

title: Tuesday's Top Analyst Upgrades and Downgrades: Aflac, Comerica, Costco, Dollar General, Dominion Energy, Ford, Meta, T-Mobile, Walmart and More
summary: This article details top analyst upgrades, downgrades, and initiations from Tuesday, June 6, 2023, for various companies including Aflac, Comerica, Costco, Dollar General, Ford, Meta, T-Mobile, and Walmart. It also provides a market overview influenced by debt ceiling resolution, upcoming Federal Reserve meetings, and recent economic data.

title: Plans advance for Charlotte region's fourth Costco store at Crosland Southeast project in Indian Land
summary: Crosland Southeast is moving forward with plans to bring the Charlotte region's fourth Costco store to Indian Land. The developer is seeking to rezone a 28-acre site adjacent to The Exchange at Indian Land for the new wholesale club. This development follows other major mixed-use projects in the Indian Land area.

title: The 20 Best Egg Brands, Ranked
summary: This article ranks the 20 best egg brands, based on quality, ethical practices, and consumer reviews. It differentiates between various egg labels like organic, pasture-raised, and Certified Humane, explaining their significance. The ranking provides insights into each brand's practices, transparency, pricing, and availability to help consumers make informed purchasing decisions.

title: Dozens of frozen fruit products sold at 6 major retailers recalled by FDA
summary: SunOpta Inc.'s subsidiary, Sunrise Growers Inc., has issued a voluntary recall for various frozen fruit products due to potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination, which stems from pineapple supplied by a third party. The recalled products were distributed to major retailers including Walmart, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, Target, Aldi, and AWG across more than 30 states. Consumers are advised to discard or return the affected products, though no illnesses have been reported to date.

title: MEC, Costco are most trusted brands in Canada: UVic survey
summary: A survey conducted by the University of Victoria’s Gustavson School of Business found that Mountain Equipment Co. (MEC) and Costco Wholesale Corp. are the most trusted brands in Canada. The survey assessed brand trust across five dimensions and included over 13,000 Canadians. While MEC has faced recent controversy, its commitment to value and customer service, alongside Costco's, resonated with consumers.

title: Proposal for new Costco store in region takes a step forward
summary: A proposal to bring a new Costco Wholesale Corp. store to Indian Land, S.C., has moved closer to reality after a second reading of a rezoning request was approved. The Lancaster County Council approved the request for a 28-acre site adjacent to The Exchange at Indian Land, a mixed-use development by Crosland Southeast. Three readings are required for final approval of the rezoning request.

title: Costco in Georgetown sets opening date
summary: The sixth Costco Wholesale Corp. location in the Austin metro area is scheduled to open on July 14th in Georgetown. This new big-box store is anticipated to create 270 jobs initially and attract smaller retailers to the area. The report also includes the Austin Business Journal's latest ranking of local retail real estate brokers.

title: Costco Chooses California as Site of Largest Club
summary: Costco is proposing to build its largest club globally in Fresno, California, measuring 241,000 square feet, which would replace an existing smaller store. The project is currently undergoing an environmental review process. Meanwhile, Costco is also cracking down on membership card sharing and continues to see membership growth, with 69.1 million paid household members and 124.7 million cardholders as of Q3.

title: Efforts to bring fourth Costco store to Charlotte region win final approval
summary: Lancaster County Council has given final approval for a rezoning request, paving the way for a new Costco Wholesale Corp. store in Indian Land, South Carolina. This will be the fourth Costco location in the Charlotte region. The project is led by Crosland Southeast and will be adjacent to their mixed-use development, The Exchange at Indian Land.

title: Costco pays $40 million for Fulton property near airport - Atlanta Business Chronicle
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has acquired approximately 33 acres of land along Roosevelt Highway in Fulton County for $40 million. The purchase suggests Costco may be planning a new project in the area. This acquisition aligns with recent developments and interest in the Southside communities of Atlanta.

title: MultiCare buys land for future development
summary: MultiCare Health System has purchased a 30-acre vacant land parcel north of Spokane for $15.7 million for future healthcare development. The property, located at 12115 N. Mellon Parkway, is currently zoned for heavy industrial uses and its development will coincide with the completion of U.S. Highway 395. This new MultiCare facility will be adjacent to the 400-acre Mead Works mixed-use neighborhood being developed by Greenstone Corp.

title: Costco is coming to the Buffalo area. Here's what to expect.
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is moving forward with plans to open a store in Amherst, New York, despite a policy of not commenting on future locations until closer to opening. The Amherst Planning Board is scheduled to discuss the project, which is expected to be located on Ridge Lea Road at the former Tony Roma's restaurant site. This development indicates that Western New York can anticipate the arrival of a Costco store.

title: 'I've been waiting for Costco to be here for years': Jackson Township has grand opening
summary: Costco Wholesale has opened its first store in Stark County, Ohio, in Jackson Township, drawing significant local excitement and a record number of pre-opening memberships for the Midwest region. The 160,000-square-foot store is expected to employ up to 250 people and represents a $28.5 million project. Local officials and developers celebrated the opening, highlighting the economic benefits and community enthusiasm for the new warehouse.

title: 100 new places: These stores, restaurants and warehouses are opening in central Pa.
summary: Numerous businesses, including stores, restaurants, and warehouses, are opening or soon to open across central Pennsylvania. The Boohoo Group has leased a significant 1.1 million square-foot facility in Londonderry Township, reported by developer First Industrial Realty Trust. In Cumberland County, BJ’s Wholesale Club is set to relocate and anchor the upcoming Beltway Commons shopping center.

title: Walmart promotes CEO of Sam's Club to head International division
summary: Walmart Inc. has promoted Kathryn McLay, CEO of its Sam's Club unit, to lead its $100 billion international business. McLay will take over from Judith McKenna on September 11, facing challenges like high inflation and slowing economies in key global markets, including China. Christopher Nicholas will succeed McLay as CEO of Sam's Club.

title: The Supply Side: Entrepreneur’s allergy-friendly snacks land in 1,800 Walmart stores
summary: Blake Sorenson, founder of Blake's Seed Based, successfully launched his allergy-friendly snack brand in 1,800 Walmart stores. Sorenson, an athlete with a nut allergy, developed the seed-based snacks to solve a personal and broader social need. His persistence over several years, including raising initial capital via Kickstarter and securing placement in major grocery chains, led to this significant expansion with Walmart.

title: Grocery shadow-anchored strip center in Los Angeles area sells for $8M
summary: JLL Capital Markets announced the sale of a 23,598-square-foot grocery shadow-anchored strip center in Thousand Oaks, California, for $8 million. The shopping center is strategically located adjacent to a Whole Foods store. This transaction highlights continued investment in retail properties in the Los Angeles area.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Walmart, The Home Depot and Costco Wholesale
summary: The Zacks Analyst Blog highlights Walmart, Home Depot, and Costco Wholesale as top blue-chip retail stocks for stable, long-term investment. These companies are praised for their financial resilience, consistent growth, and ability to weather economic downturns, making them dependable choices for investors. Each company's strategic initiatives, market capitalization, earnings expectations, and dividend payouts are detailed to showcase their strong investment potential.

title: Coeur d'Alene city council considering land deal with Costco
summary: The Coeur d'Alene City Council is set to consider a land deal with Costco Wholesale Corp. regarding a small, triangular city-owned parcel of land. This land, valued at $30,000, is currently used by Costco as a swale for stormwater collection under a lease agreement. The council will decide whether to approve the land exchange with Costco.

title: Clorox product shortage: What it means for you
summary: The Clorox Company is experiencing product shortages for various household items due to a cyberattack in August that damaged its internal systems. This has led to slower order processing, and while production has resumed at most manufacturing sites, system repairs and reintegration are ongoing. The company anticipates a "material" effect on its business in the current fiscal quarter ending September 30, but it is uncertain if financial impacts will extend beyond that.

title: What are 'reasonable accommodations'?
summary: This article discusses the nuances of "reasonable accommodations" for disabled employees, using a Costco court case as a primary example. It emphasizes the importance for HR professionals to engage in a documented "interactive process" with employees to determine suitable accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), warning against common pitfalls that could lead to litigation. Employment lawyer Rafael Nendel-Flores highlights the need for thorough documentation and proactive investigation into all possible accommodations, including alternative job placements.

title: Costco ‘on a roll’, boosted by back-to-school, according to foot traffic data
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is experiencing a surge in foot traffic, particularly boosted by the back-to-school season, according to data from Placer.ai. The analytics company notes that Costco has steadily increased its visit share within the superstore space and led its category in year-over-year visit growth during this period, indicating a strong recovery for the retailer. Costco is scheduled to report its fourth-quarter results on September 26.

title: Home Depot is selling a tiny home for $6,000 - customers say it's 'very sturdy'
summary: Home Depot is selling a Colonial Williamsburg DIY shed kit that can be converted into a tiny home for just over $6,000. Customers praise its sturdiness and ease of assembly. The kit measures 8 by 12 feet, includes a floor, and features fungal decay and termite-resistant paneling with a 50-year rot-resistant warranty.

title: Costco Offers Members $29 Online Health Care Visits
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is expanding into healthcare by offering its members access to medical care through a partnership with the online marketplace Sesame. This deal provides Costco members with discounted services, including online primary care visits for $29 and mental health visits for $79. This move aligns Costco with other retailers also broadening their healthcare footprints.

title: Costco could expand South Florida warehouse distribution hub
summary: Costco is exploring the expansion of its distribution center in West Palm Beach, Florida, by adding another warehouse at 5851 45th Street. This proposed expansion could lead to the creation of over 100 new jobs at the site. The article suggests this move would bolster Costco's logistical footprint in South Florida.

title: Costco’s Q4 Profits Climb 15 Percent
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported a 15.4 percent increase in earnings for its fiscal fourth quarter ending September 3, with sales rising 9.4 percent. Net income for the quarter reached $2.160 billion, or $4.86 per diluted share. For the entire 53-week fiscal year, net income was $6.292 billion, on net sales of $237.71 billion.

title: Costco delivers strong Q4; to open nine U.S. clubs in Q1
summary: Costco reported strong Q4 results, surpassing earnings and revenue estimates due to increased store traffic despite a decrease in average transaction size and weaker spending on big-ticket items. The company saw a significant rise in net income and membership fees, with e-commerce sales slightly down. Costco plans to open 10 new stores in the next quarter, including nine in the U.S., and the CFO hinted that a membership fee increase is a matter of "when, not if."

title: Target announces nine store closures, cites 'organized retail crime'
summary: Target announced it would close nine stores in major cities across the U.S., explicitly blaming retail theft and organized retail crime for the decision. The closures, representing less than 1% of Target's total stores, will affect locations in New York City, Seattle, San Francisco, Oakland, and Portland. This move comes after Target's CEO previously noted a worsening trend in retail theft affecting safety, product availability, and business performance.

title: Costco teams with Sesame to offer low-cost doctor visits - Bizwomen
summary: Costco (Nasdaq: COST) has partnered with health care startup Sesame to provide its nearly 120 million cardholders with access to low-cost virtual doctor visits. This new benefit includes virtual primary care, check-ups with blood tests, and mental health visits at discounted rates, aiming to add value for members as Costco delays raising membership prices. Sesame, which does not accept insurance and caters to those with high deductibles or no insurance, will also offer discounted in-person services to Costco members.

title: This is why Costco shares are down despite fourth-quarter beat
summary: Despite Costco Wholesale Corp. reporting better-than-expected fourth-quarter results, its stock was down 1.7% in premarket trades. Analyst Rupesh Parikh suggests this is typical for Costco shares post-earnings, and the lack of a membership fee increase might also be a factor. He advises investors to capitalize on any profit-taking.

title: Costco’s 1-ounce gold bars selling out ‘within a few hours’ — again
summary: Costco is reportedly selling one-ounce gold bars that are consistently selling out within hours of being listed online. The warehouse retailer limits purchases to two bars per member due to high demand. This new offering expands Costco's already diverse product range, which includes unexpected items like caskets and caviar.

title: FitLife Brands to Acquire Substantially All of the Assets of MusclePharm Corporation
summary: FitLife Brands announced its acquisition of substantially all of MusclePharm Corporation's assets for $18.5 million, funded by cash on hand and a new $10 million term loan. The all-cash transaction, approved by the US Bankruptcy Court, is expected to be highly accretive and close by October 16, 2023. FitLife plans to revitalize the iconic sports nutrition brand by focusing on online sales and expanded wholesale distribution.

title: Costco Cake Resellers in Mexico Net Up to $1,700 Over Four Days
summary: People in Mexico are buying Costco cakes and pies to resell them by the slice, sometimes earning up to $1,700 over four days. This trend, amplified by social media, has led some Costco stores to limit purchases to five cakes per person, with resellers even waiting overnight. One reseller uses her profits to pay for chemotherapy.

title: Costco membership-fee hike is coming
summary: Costco (COST) has confirmed that a membership-fee increase is planned, following hints over the past several months. While the exact timing and magnitude of the increase remain unknown, CFO Richard Galanti stated that it is a "matter of when, not if." The last membership fee hike for the warehouse retailer was in 2017.

title: Check Out Costco's New HQ Addition — Contours, Cafeterias, Cubicles, and Cardio
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has completed a significant addition to its Issaquah headquarters, designed by Seattle-based MG2, which accommodates over 3,700 employees. The new expansion features two connected buildings, a new parking garage with a gym and exposition center, multiple cafeterias, and promotes an open work environment with cubicles for all staff, including executives. This development aims to consolidate Costco's 7,000 Issaquah employees onto one campus, showcasing modern facilities and a connection to nature.

title: Best Buy joins growing list of retailers entering the healthcare space
summary: Best Buy has entered the healthcare sector by offering a continuous glucose monitoring system, becoming the latest retailer to expand into medical services. Other major retailers like Costco, Amazon, Walmart, and CVS have also significantly invested in healthcare, providing services ranging from virtual primary care and online pharmacies to in-store clinics and health insurance. This trend highlights a broader movement among large retailers to diversify their offerings and tap into the growing healthcare market.

title: Find out what's next at Jordan Creek Town Center and which stores opened this year
summary: Jordan Creek Town Center is thriving as it approaches its 20th anniversary, despite a national trend of struggling shopping malls. The center is almost at full capacity, with only a few retail spaces remaining available. Its footprint extends beyond the main mall to include surrounding businesses and restaurants.

title: Instacart To Accept Some Medicare Advantage Plans
summary: Alignment Healthcare plans to offer Instacart as a benefit for certain Medicare Advantage plans in California and Nevada starting next year, pending regulatory approval. These plans will provide quarterly grocery allowances, a complimentary Instacart+ membership, and access to a virtual storefront for chronically ill members. This initiative aims to address food insecurity and transportation barriers for seniors, marking Instacart Health's first agreement with a Medicare Advantage plan.

title: Walmart to close stores on Thanksgiving for fourth consecutive year
summary: Walmart has announced it will close its stores on Thanksgiving for the fourth consecutive year, a trend that began during the COVID-19 pandemic. This decision, aimed at allowing employees to spend the holiday with family, is expected to be followed by other major retailers. Prior to the pandemic, many companies capitalized on Thanksgiving for early Black Friday sales, but this has since shifted to prioritizing employee well-being.

title: Costco Sued, Accused Of Sharing Confidential Health Data With Facebook
summary: Costco is facing a lawsuit in a Seattle federal court, accused of sharing sensitive customer health information with Meta Platforms Inc. through the Meta Pixel tracking tool used on its website. The lawsuit, filed by four California residents, claims Costco violated Washington State's privacy laws by not disclosing its data-sharing practices, especially concerning susceptible health data of pharmacy users. Plaintiffs are seeking a jury trial and financial damages, while Meta states its policies prohibit advertisers from sending sensitive information.

title: Walmart pouring $350M into new dairy facility
summary: Walmart plans to invest $350 million into a new milk processing facility in Valdosta, Georgia, set to open in 2025 and create almost 400 jobs. This move continues Walmart's strategy to gain more control over its fresh food supply chain, similar to its existing milk facility in Indiana and beef processing efforts in Kansas and Georgia. The new Georgia facility will process various milk types for Walmart's Great Value and Sam's Club's Member's Mark brands, supplying over 750 stores in the Southeast.

title: Costco’s CEO Craig Jelinek stepping down
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. announced that CEO Craig Jelinek will step down on January 1st and be succeeded by COO Ron Vachris. Jelinek has led the company since 2012, overseeing significant growth in shares and revenue. Vachris, who started as a forklift driver 40 years ago, was considered a leading candidate for the position.

title: Costco jilted Pasco. One Tri-Cities official hopes to rekindle the spark
summary: Pasco officials are still hoping Costco will build a new store in their city at Broadmoor, despite Costco's current negotiations to lease a 28-acre site in Richland. The spot in Pasco is being reserved for Costco, even though a Costco representative previously confirmed that the price of the land was not the reason for their decision to exit an agreement to purchase property there in mid-2021. Meanwhile, Costco confirmed ongoing negotiations for a 55-year lease in Richland.

title: Costco's CEO Is Stepping Down After 11 Years – He Has 'Total Confidence' in His Successor
summary: Costco CEO Craig Jelinek is stepping down after 11 years in the role, effective January 1, 2024, to be succeeded by current president and COO Ron Vachris. Jelinek, who has been with the company for 40 years, will remain on the Board of Directors and assist with the transition. The succession plan has been in the works, and Jelinek expressed full confidence in Vachris.

title: Opinion: Why the Kroger-Albertsons Merger Is Good for Union Workers
summary: Industry expert Burt P. Flickinger III argues that the Kroger-Albertsons merger is beneficial for union workers, customers, and communities, particularly given the rapid growth of large, non-unionized food retailers. He highlights a significant decline in union membership across UFCW, Teamsters, and BGTCMI over the past two decades, attributing it to the expansion of companies like Walmart and Amazon. Flickinger asserts that Kroger has historically supported unions and that the merger is the best outcome to level the playing field, prevent job losses, and ensure the long-term viability of unionized grocery chains against aggressive competition.

title: Costco Business Center opens in north St. Louis County
summary: A new Costco Business Center has opened in north St. Louis County, marking a new kind of Costco presence in the St. Louis area. This opening is highlighted by the St. Louis Business Journal, indicating local business interest in the new retail format.

title: Costco Business Center opens in north St. Louis County
summary: A new Costco Business Center has opened in St. John, north St. Louis County, offering a different selection of bulk food and office supplies catering to small businesses. Operated by Issaquah, Washington-based Costco Wholesale Corp. (NASDAQ: COST), this location is one of 25 business centers nationwide, with over 70% of its inventory differing from typical Costco warehouses. The company often repurposes former big-box stores for these business centers.

title: Here's how much Costco's incoming CEO could make next year
summary: Ron Vachris, Costco's current president and chief operating officer, is set to take over as CEO on January 1, succeeding Craig Jelenik. Vachris has been with Costco for over 40 years. This article indicates that Costco has disclosed his incoming salary, although the specific amount is not detailed in the provided text.

title: Costco class action alleges Kirkland nasal decongestant product ineffective
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Costco Wholesale Corp., alleging that its Kirkland-brand Multi-Symptom Cold & Flu Severe is falsely marketed as an effective nasal decongestant. The lawsuit claims the product's active ingredient, phenylephrine, has been deemed ineffective at relieving nasal congestion by an FDA advisory panel. Plaintiff Eduardo Flores seeks to represent a nationwide class of consumers, accusing Costco of unjust enrichment, breach of implied warranty, and violating California consumer protection laws.

title: Mass merchandisers capitalize on grocery items, services
summary: Mass merchandisers are increasingly capitalizing on grocery items and diverse services, driven by consumers' focus on value and convenience amid economic pressures. Companies like Walmart and Costco are seeing significant growth in grocery sales and are expanding into non-retail services such as healthcare and pet care to offset retail slumps and mute sales volatility. This shift also includes offering enhanced omnichannel shopping experiences and stocking more functional beverages.

title: Cracker Barrel and Costco offering similar Thanksgiving dinner for 8
summary: Cracker Barrel and Costco are both offering comparable Thanksgiving dinner packages for around eight people, aiming to provide convenience for holiday meals. Cracker Barrel's Heat n' Serve Family Dinner costs $154.99 and includes traditional sides, while Costco's Fortune Gourmet Thanksgiving Dinner is priced at $199.99 (or $149.99 with an early bird discount) and offers a similar spread, with the choice often depending on availability.

title: Costco class action alleges retailer shared customer health info with Meta
summary: Costco is facing a class action lawsuit alleging that it shared customers' personal health information with Meta through embedded tracking tools like Facebook Pixel, without consent. The lawsuit claims that this data, gathered from Costco's pharmacy website where customers manage prescriptions, is not anonymous and is linked to specific Facebook user profiles. The plaintiffs argue that Costco's actions violate HIPAA regulations designed to protect private health information.

title: Costco Korea on verge of falling into low-growth trap
summary: Costco Wholesale Korea is facing a potential low-growth trap as its sales have plateaued at the 5 trillion won level for three consecutive years. The company is facing intense competition from e-commerce players in Korea and is observed to be shifting its focus to the rapidly expanding Chinese market, which is seeing much faster store expansion. This comes despite assurances from Costco's CFO about continued investment in Korea, with the relocation of core Korean staff to China and a potential store closure in Seoul signaling a change in strategy.

title: Costco hit with 1.5 billion yen tab for undeclared consumption tax
summary: Costco's Japanese arm has been ordered to pay 1.5 billion yen ($9.9 million) for undeclared consumption taxes. The charges stem from improper duty-free sales, including bulk purchases for resale and sales to ineligible long-term foreign residents, as well as an error in tax form calculations. This incident highlights issues with tax compliance in duty-free transactions and corporate accounting.

title: Discover 8 Things Cheaper At Target Than Costco
summary: This article compares prices of eight common items sold at both Target and Costco, highlighting instances where Target offers a better deal despite Costco's reputation for bulk savings. It delves into specific product comparisons across categories like toilet paper, electronics, and household goods, considering variations in packaging, features, and brand. The comparison aims to show consumers where they might find more affordable options at Target.

title: Discover 6 Things Cheaper At Costco Than Target
summary: This article identifies six items that are cheaper at Costco than at Target, comparing unit costs and specific product models. While Target (TGT) has more stores and a higher gross margin, Costco (COST) generates significantly more revenue due to its focus on low prices and bulk sales, despite requiring a membership fee. The comparison details price differences for items like dishwasher detergent, stand mixers, flannel shirts, air purifiers, cotton sheets, and Bluetooth speakers.

title: Target earnings up, food sales slip
summary: Target Corporation reported a 36% increase in net earnings for the third quarter ending October 28, despite a 4.2% drop in revenue. The company's CEO, Brian C. Cornell, attributed the earnings growth to lower freight costs, efficient inventory management, and operational efficiencies, which helped offset a decline in discretionary spending. While overall sales decreased, Target's food and beverage category saw only a slight dip, with seasonal snacks performing well, and the company plans to offer holiday deals on turkeys and side dishes.

title: Black Friday 2023 store hours for Walmart, Target, Macy's and more
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of Black Friday 2023 store hours for numerous major retailers, including Walmart, Target, and Macy's. It details which stores are closed on Thanksgiving Day and their opening times for Black Friday, helping shoppers plan their holiday shopping. The information aims to assist consumers in identifying opportune times to find holiday deals.

title: Final Thoughts From Charlie Munger on Apple, Warren Buffett, and the Big Costco Error
summary: This article compiles insights from Charlie Munger's final interviews, focusing on his investment philosophy, partnership with Warren Buffett, and specific investments. It covers his views on Apple, the "big Costco error" by Buffett, and Munger's perspectives on retailing, China, and company valuations. The article highlights how Munger influenced Buffett's investment strategy and his own unique approach to identifying valuable companies.

title: Which Was Charlie Munger’s Best Bet: Berkshire Hathaway or Costco?
summary: Charlie Munger, known for his work with Warren Buffett at Berkshire Hathaway, also had significant involvement with Costco and Daily Journal Corporation. While most of his wealth was tied to Berkshire, the article explores whether his investment in Costco might have yielded a better personal return. A comparison of hypothetical investment returns suggests Costco might have offered a higher compound annual growth rate for Munger than Berkshire Hathaway over specific periods.

title: Costco mourns longtime board member, reports sales jump
summary: Costco announced the passing of longtime board member and Berkshire Hathaway vice chairman Charles Munger at age 99. The company's CEO, Craig Jelinek, expressed deep condolences and acknowledged Munger's significant wisdom. In conjunction with this news, Costco also reported a 5.1 percent increase in net sales for November, reaching $20.14 billion.

title: Staples Counting on Discounts for the Remainder of 2023
summary: Despite a strong Black Friday, the author suggests a nuanced approach to the retail sector for Q4 2023, advising investors to focus on online retail ETFs and discount retailers/staples ETFs due to anticipated consumer weakness. The article highlights that e-commerce continues to gain market share and that discount retailers like Walmart and Costco are well-positioned to benefit as consumers seek savings on essential goods. It concludes that while online retail ETFs might experience some weakness, the broader consumer staples sector, particularly discount retailers, is likely to show strength.

title: Costco, Home Depot and Floor & Decor: Diverging Outcomes From a Similar Model
