The natural and organic grocer's success highlights its robust growth potential in a competitive market.

title: What would happen if massive battery plant proposed in Morro Bay caught fire?
summary: A safety report commissioned by Vistra Corp. states that a large fire at the proposed Morro Bay battery plant would not significantly endanger public health. The report, conducted by Ramboll, involved computer simulations and reviews, concluding that even if one block of batteries burned, the released toxins would not create significant health risks based on EPA standards. The project faces community opposition and will be subject to a ballot measure in November.

title: Tesla expands Semi testing program, partners with Costco, Sysco, and US Foods
summary: Tesla is expanding its Semi testing program, partnering with major companies like Costco, Sysco, and US Foods. These new collaborations aim to refine the electric Class 8 truck's engineering before mass production begins, adding to existing partnerships with PepsiCo, Martin Brower, and Walmart. Tesla is gearing up for mass production of the Semi, with initial customer deliveries planned for 2026.

title: Walmart Earnings: Low Prices and Strong Digital Presence Drive Market Share Gains
summary: Walmart delivered strong fiscal 2025 first-quarter results, driven by low prices and digital investments, which helped attract consumers and expand revenue by 6%. The company's adjusted earnings per share increased by 20% to $0.60, surpassing forecasts. Morningstar plans to raise its fair value estimate for Walmart stock, noting that the retailer is well-positioned to gain market share across various income groups despite current overvaluation.

title: PHYS ETF Alert: Michael Burry Is Betting Big on This Gold Fund
summary: Michael Burry's Scion Asset Management has made Sprott Physical Gold Trust (PHYS) its biggest bet, acquiring 440,000 units. This move highlights a growing trend among major investors to go long on gold, driven by potential Federal Reserve interest rate cuts, geopolitical uncertainties, and currency devaluation hedges. The PHYS ETF is unique due to its hybrid structure and 99.9% allocation to physical 400-ounce gold bars.

title: TJ Maxx's parent company plans to open 1,300 more stores - as CEO promises 'treasure hunt format' for shoppers
summary: TJX Companies, the parent company of TJ Maxx, Marshalls, and HomeGoods, plans to open over 1,300 new stores globally, despite some recent closures. CEO Ernie Herrman emphasized their "treasure hunt" business model, which leverages discounted merchandise from higher-end stores and appeals to a broad demographic, including Gen Z shoppers. This expansion reflects the company's confidence in its flexible and resilient off-price model to gain market share.

title: There’s a New Way to Shop at Costco Without a Membership
summary: Costco has partnered with Uber Eats to allow customers to shop for their products, including Kirkland items, and have them delivered without needing a Costco membership. This partnership is currently available at a limited number of locations in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Japan, with plans for expansion. While non-members pay full price on the Uber Eats app, members can apply their discounts, though prices may vary from in-store costs.

title: Kroger revamps private label pet line
summary: Kroger has revitalized its private label pet brand, Abound, by introducing new varieties of dog and cat food and treats, alongside updated packaging. This strategic move aims to capitalize on the growing pet supply market, with Kroger planning to launch more than 800 new store brand products in 2024 as it continues to expand its private label sales. The expansion aligns with recommendations for grocers to broaden their pet food assortments to meet diverse consumer needs, offering premium options at competitive prices.

title: Costco tops revenue estimates on rebound in demand for low-priced discretionary items
summary: Costco Wholesale exceeded third-quarter revenue expectations, driven by strong consumer demand for low-priced discretionary items and groceries amidst high living costs. The company's focus on fresh foods and increased purchases of toys, furnishings, and health products contributed to its robust performance, demonstrating resilience compared to other retailers. Costco's total revenue reached $58.52 billion, surpassing analyst estimates, with comparable sales and e-commerce growth also performing strongly.

title: EBay to drop American Express over fees, says customers have other options
summary: eBay announced its decision to stop accepting American Express globally starting August 17, citing "unacceptably high fees" for processing credit card transactions. The online marketplace stated that customers now have numerous alternative payment options available. American Express, in response, claims eBay's cost to accept AmEx cards is comparable to other networks and believes the decision is inconsistent with increasing competition.

title: Big-box retailer considers Liberty Lake
summary: A membership-based big-box retailer, strongly resembling Costco, is proposing a new 160,000-square-foot store and a 24-vehicle gas station in Liberty Lake, Washington. The proposed site spans 39.09 acres owned by a Centennial Properties Inc. affiliate, west of Kramer Parkway. While the retailer's name hasn't been confirmed, city officials and local business leaders suggest the project is moving forward and could significantly boost Liberty Lake's sales-tax generation.

title: Newmont CEO sees copper demand boom driving mining deals
summary: Newmont CEO Tom Palmer predicts a surge in mining deals driven by the escalating demand for copper, particularly from new sources like artificial intelligence, and the ongoing energy transition. Palmer also noted that Newmont is advancing plans to divest eight assets and reduce debt following its acquisition of Newcrest, while benefiting from strong gold prices due to global economic uncertainty. He highlighted that the gold sector is also ripe for consolidation as companies navigate capital access challenges and decarbonization efforts.

title: How Does Monday.com Make Money? Monday.com Business Model In A Nutshell
summary: Monday.com is a cloud-based work management platform founded in 2012 by Roy Mann, Eran Kampf, and Eran Zinman to help organizations scale efficiently. The company generates revenue by offering various subscription plans for its platform, catering to teams from small to enterprise-level based on the number of users and desired features. Its business model relies on a freemium approach with tiered paid plans that include features like Gantt charts, time-tracking, and advanced analytics, appealing to a wide range of industries and clients such as Costco and Uber.

title: This ETF strategy may help investors skirt market concentration risk
summary: Investors seeking to avoid market concentration risk might consider value-oriented investments, according to Phil McInnis of Avantis Investors. He suggests a diversified approach beyond typical index funds, favoring companies with low valuations and strong balance sheets through an ETF strategy that includes a profitability overlay. Avantis' U.S. Large Cap Value ETF (AVLV) aims for less concentration by making smaller bets on profitable, attractively priced companies across various sectors, demonstrating stronger performance than its benchmark.

title: What Buffalo could expect as Costco gets closer to opening here
summary: Buffalo Business First looked at other markets where Costco recently opened to anticipate what the impact might be for Buffalo as a new Costco store approaches opening. The project, which involves Costco Wholesale Corp. (NYSE: COST), received site plan approval in August 2023 for a location on Ridge Lea Road in Amherst, though Costco has yet to officially announce details. The article notes that Costco's policy is to not comment on future locations until 2-3 months prior to opening.

title: New Bank OZK Branches in the Works for West Little Rock
summary: Bank OZK is constructing two new branches in west Little Rock, including a Chenal Parkway location and an auto-banking branch on its headquarters campus. Both designs by Polk Stanley Wilcox Architects emphasize unique aesthetics and advanced banking technology. The Chenal Parkway branch, which broke ground in May, is designed with a sculpted roof that allows natural light into the lobby.

title: Costco class action claims retailer marks up online products
summary: A new class action lawsuit alleges that Costco misleadingly marks up products sold online without disclosing to consumers that these items may be cheaper in-store. Plaintiff Annie Song claims that Costco explicitly promises on its website to disclose such price differences but regularly fails to do so. Song is seeking to represent a class of consumers who paid more for online purchases without explicit disclosure of potential lower in-store prices.

title: New Solo Brands CEO Sets The Stage To Grow Its Flagship Stove And Chubbies Fashion Brand
summary: New Solo Brands CEO Christopher Metz is focused on turning around the company's performance after a disappointing 2023. He aims to leverage his multi-brand experience to professionalize the firm, supercharge flagship brands Solo Stove and Chubbies through innovation and expanded distribution, and improve financial performance. Metz has already brought in new leadership and marketing strategies to drive growth for the diverse brand portfolio.

title: Kirkland vs Titleist Lawsuit: Latest Updates on the Ongoing Legal Battle
summary: The legal dispute between Costco and Acushnet Holdings Corp, the maker of Titleist golf balls, has intensified. Acushnet has filed a countersuit against Costco, alleging that Kirkland Signature golf balls infringe on ten of Titleist’s patents and seek substantial damages. The countersuit also accuses Costco of false advertising regarding the quality claims of its Kirkland brand golf balls.

title: Walmart Continues to Hammer Target
summary: Target Corp. continues to struggle, seeing its revenue fall and net income remain flat, while its stock has stayed flat this year. In contrast, Walmart Inc. has significantly outperformed with a 29% stock gain and a U.S. revenue that is more than four times Target's. Walmart's vast store count, strong e-commerce presence, and leading grocery sales make it difficult for Target to gain market share, suggesting Target will fall further behind.

title: SIMPLY BETTER BRANDS CORP. ANNOUNCES NEW FLAVOR PACK FOR NATIONAL ROLLOUT OF TRUBAR™ IN COSTCO WHOLESALE
summary: Simply Better Brands Corp. announced a national rollout of its TRUBAR™ product in Costco Wholesale, building on previous successful promotions. The new flavor pack features a 16-count dual pack of "Oh oh cookie dough" and "Get in my belly, PB and jelly" and will initially be launched in four Costco regions, with more to follow. The company aims to expand the reach of its clean ingredient, plant-based nutrition brand to a wider audience through this partnership.

title: Costco Lawsuit Alleges Kirkland Baby Wipes Contain Dangerous Forever Chemicals
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Costco and Nice-Pak Products, alleging that their fragrance-free Kirkland Signature Baby Wipes contain unsafe levels of "forever chemicals" (PFAS). The lawsuit claims that the products are unfit for their intended use, especially given the sensitivity of babies' skin and the marketing of the wipes as "made with Naturally Derived Ingredients." This case seeks to represent all U.S. consumers who purchased these wipes within the applicable statute of limitations.

title: Consumer Reports finds unclear ingredients in seven brands of baby wipes
summary: A Consumer Reports investigation revealed that seven out of 15 popular baby wipe brands contain concerning or unclear ingredients, including potentially harmful chemicals and plastics. The report advises consumers to choose plant-based, fragrance-free, biodegradable wipes and warns against leaving wipes in hot environments or flushing them. Following the investigation, a lawsuit was filed against Kirkland (Costco) wipes, alleging high levels of PFAS.

title: Peace Coffee lands Costco Wholesale in Midwest states
summary: Minneapolis-based Peace Coffee, known for its sustainable, fair trade, and organic principles, has successfully expanded its retail presence by landing Costco Wholesale Corp. The brand's roasted coffee beans will now be available in Costco stores across the Midwest. This move signifies a significant growth opportunity for Peace Coffee.

title: FEATURE:Costco proving a one-stop shop for regional revitalization in Japan
summary: Costco's expansion in Japan is increasingly viewed as a key driver for regional revitalization, attracting cities and towns hoping to boost local economies through job creation and increased tax revenues. While successful in fostering economic growth and even population increases in some areas, this expansion also raises concerns among local merchants who struggle to compete with the American retail giant. Despite these challenges, Costco continues to expand, with its unique business model and product offerings seen as contributing to urban development and consumer entertainment.

title: Lawsuit claims Costco sold baby wipes containing ‘significant’ levels of PFAS
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is facing a class-action lawsuit alleging that its Kirkland Signature Baby Wipes, Fragrance Free, contain "significant" and "unsafe levels" of PFAS, harmful synthetic chemicals. The lawsuit, filed by Larisa Bullard and Mila Corrigan, claims the product is unfit for its intended use despite being labeled with "Naturally Derived Ingredients." Testing reportedly found 3.7 parts per billion of PFAS in the wipes, linking exposure to various health issues including liver damage and increased asthma.

title: Costco Raising Membership Fees
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is increasing its annual membership fees for the first time since 2017, effective September 1. Gold Star and Business memberships will rise by $5, while Executive Memberships will increase by $10, from $120 to $130, with an increased reward cap from $1,000 to $1,250. This decision accompanies strong financial results, including significant growth in net sales and membership fee income.

title: Costco memberships set to increase for first time since 2017
summary: Costco is set to raise its membership fees for the first time in seven years, with standard memberships increasing by $5 to $65 and Executive Memberships by $10 to $130 annually, effective September 1. This move is expected to impact 52 million memberships and follows similar increases by rivals like Sam's Club and Amazon. The fee hikes contribute significantly to Costco's profits, helping to offset expenses and keep prices down, and come as the company reported a 7.4% increase in net sales for the five weeks ending July 7.

title: THE FRIDAY 5: Kroger Makes Divestiture Moves; Costco Increases Membership Fees
summary: This article summarizes the top five food retail industry news stories. Key updates include Kroger's advancement with its Albertsons merger by divesting 579 stores to C&S Wholesale Grocers, a new labor agreement ratified at Wegmans, and membership fee changes by Costco and Sam's Club. Also highlighted are summer special promotions from Dollar General, Kroger, and 7-Eleven, and a new conservation partnership between Lidl and WWF.

title: Costco targets Forney in latest economic development win for city
summary: The Forney City Council has approved incentives for a new Costco warehouse, marking its 16th location in the DFW area. This development represents a significant economic win for Forney, a rapidly growing suburb east of Dallas, as Costco continues its expansion. The approval came just days before National Hot Dog Day, referencing Costco's famed $1.50 hot dog and drink combo.

title: Walmart, Costco Finally Sign On to Canadian Grocery Code of Conduct
summary: Walmart and Costco Wholesale Corp. have finally endorsed Canada's Grocery Code of Conduct, meaning all major retailers in the country have now signed on. This move is expected to bring more fairness, transparency, and predictability to Canada's grocery supply chain and benefit consumers. The code provides guidelines for retailer-supplier interactions, aiming to protect smaller grocers and standardize practices like product delisting and fee charging.

title: Beyond Completes Overstock.com Revival with Revamped Website, New Categories
summary: Beyond, Inc., owners of Overstock, Bed Bath & Beyond, and Zulily, has relaunched Overstock.com with a new website and expanded product categories. This "Grand Reopening" follows an executive overhaul and an accelerated plan to distinguish Overstock from Bed Bath & Beyond, with Overstock focusing on furniture, closeouts, and distressed merchandise, while also expanding into various other categories like apparel and home improvement. The company aims to become a leader in solving complex inventory problems for manufacturers and retailers while offering value to consumers.

title: Earnings call: Orion Group Holdings lowers 2024 guidance amid project delays
summary: Orion Group Holdings (ORN) reported Q2 revenue of $192 million and adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million, but lowered its full-year 2024 guidance due to project delays. Despite these setbacks, the company maintains a strong long-term outlook with a robust backlog of $876 million and significant new project wins, including contracts with Port Everglades, Port Tampa Bay, and Costco Wholesale. The revised guidance projects full-year revenue between $850 million to $900 million and adjusted EBITDA between $40 million to $45 million, with an expectation for margins to improve in the second half of the year.

title: Mondelēz International taps Nestlé, P&G veteran as tech chief
summary: Mondelēz International has appointed Filippo Catalano as its new chief information and digital officer. Catalano, who previously held senior technology roles at Nestlé, Reckitt, and Procter & Gamble, will report directly to CEO Dirk Van de Put. This appointment reflects a broader trend of companies enhancing their tech leadership, with Catalano tasked with driving digital transformation for the global snack company.

title: Costco may add to Dallas distribution center
summary: Costco appears to be planning an expansion of its Dallas distribution hub, with documents filed with the state indicating a 48,150-square-foot addition to its warehouse on Mountain Creek Parkway. This development highlights the retail giant's continued investment in its logistics infrastructure in the Dallas area.

title: Costco planning to expand Dallas presence
summary: Costco is expanding its presence in Dallas, Texas, with plans to add a 48,150-square-foot metal building to its distribution center and renovate its trailer parking. This expansion, estimated to cost $14.2 million, is scheduled to begin in November with delivery expected by May 2025. The retail giant already operates 12 locations in Dallas-Fort Worth and has four more in its pipeline across North Texas.

title: Kroger and Albertsons: A Case Study in Operational Resilience
summary: Despite the ongoing uncertainty surrounding their proposed $24.6 billion merger, Kroger and Albertsons are demonstrating operational resilience by focusing on their individual value creation strategies. Kroger, facing persistent legal and regulatory challenges, continues to prioritize customer solutions, lower prices, and digital expansion, while Albertsons is advancing its "Customers for Life" strategy to enhance customer engagement and loyalty. Both companies are investing in their respective models, emphasizing private brands, convenience, and digital capabilities, even as they navigate industry headwinds and merger-related delays.

title: Costco Reports Brisk Grocery Sales for July
summary: Costco reported strong net sales of $19.26 billion for July, marking a 7.1% increase from the previous year, with significant growth in grocery categories and e-commerce. The company is also implementing new measures to combat membership card sharing at warehouse entrances. These developments come as Costco prepares to raise its membership fees.

title: Costco to scan members’ cards at entry; July sales strong
summary: Costco is implementing a new policy requiring members to scan their physical or digital membership cards at store entrances to deter non-members from shopping. This change, which follows a July pilot program, coincides with a recent announcement of a $5 increase in annual membership fees, effective September 1. Additionally, the company reported strong July sales, with net sales up 7.1% year-over-year and e-commerce sales jumping 20.2%.

title: Costco settles PAGA class action for $2.95 Million
summary: Costco has agreed to a $2.95 million settlement in a PAGA class action lawsuit concerning wage and hour violations for non-exempt employees. Eligible employees who worked between April 12, 2021, and January 29, 2024, are automatically included in the settlement and will receive payments based on their days worked. The settlement aims to resolve claims regarding unpaid compensation related to meal/rest premiums, Hero Pay, and sick leave pay.

title: Harris Joins the FTC’s Food Fight Against Kroger-Albertsons Merger
summary: The article discusses Vice President Kamala Harris's stance on the Kroger-Albertsons merger, aligning with the FTC's efforts to block it due to concerns about rising grocery costs. The author argues that the FTC's objections are based on a narrow definition of the grocery market, ignoring significant players like Walmart, Amazon, and Costco, and that blocking the merger might ultimately harm consumers by preventing a stronger competitor against larger firms. The article suggests that increased food prices are more likely due to inflation than a lack of competition and criticizes the FTC's rationale regarding labor concerns and "food deserts."

title: Kroger, Parent Company of Mariano’s, Fights Federal Agency in a Battle That Could Upend Antitrust
summary: Kroger, parent company of Mariano's, is suing the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) over its approach to challenging the proposed $25 billion merger with Albertsons. The lawsuit alleges that the FTC's use of an in-house tribunal to assess the merger is unconstitutional, citing a recent Supreme Court ruling that limited regulatory agencies' powers. Experts believe a Kroger victory could drastically alter how the federal government combats monopolies, potentially leading to less antitrust scrutiny, more corporate concentration, and higher prices for consumers.

title: Mexico: Calavo Growers, Fresh Del Monte Produce, Mission Produce and West Pak Avocado purchased avocados from illegally deforested land, according to investigation
summary: An investigation by Climate Rights International (CRI) and Mexican NGO Guardián Forestal found that top Mexican avocado suppliers Calavo Growers, Fresh Del Monte Produce, Mission Produce, and West Pak Avocado purchased avocados in 2023 and 2024 from illegally deforested land. The investigation uncovered 60 instances of such purchases in key producing states like Michoacán and Jalisco. These suppliers then sell to major supermarket chains, despite public commitments from officials to remove illegally grown avocados from exports.

title: Target Results Show Shoppers Willing to Spend If Price Is Right
summary: Target Corp. (TGT) reported its first quarterly sales growth in over a year, driven by strategic price cuts on essential goods and popular deals. This approach successfully attracted inflation-burdened consumers, who prioritized value shopping. The retailer's comparable sales rose as shoppers responded to lower prices on items like milk, bread, bras, and pool noodles.

title: Align Technology Pilots U.S. Invisalign® Treatment Promotional Program on Costco.com
summary: Align Technology is piloting a promotional program on Costco.com allowing U.S. Costco members to purchase an Invisalign treatment e-card and Essentials Bundle+ for $99.99, entitling them to a $400 discount on Invisalign treatment. This initiative aims to increase access to doctor-directed Invisalign treatment for a wider population. The program includes an e-card with a redemption code and a bundle of Invisalign accessories, with members directed to my.Invisalign.com/Costco to find participating providers.

title: Align Technology Partners With Costco for Invisalign Discount
summary: Align Technology has partnered with Costco to pilot a promotional program offering a $400 discount on Invisalign treatment to US Costco members. Members can purchase an Invisalign treatment e-card on Costco.com for $99.99, which also includes an Invisalign Essentials Bundle+. This initiative aims to connect Costco members with Invisalign-trained dental and orthodontic practices.

title: Costco enters pilot with Invisalign parent
summary: Costco is launching a pilot program with Align Technology, the maker of Invisalign, to offer discounted dental aligner treatments to its members. Members can purchase an e-card on Costco.com for $99.99, which provides a $400 discount on Invisalign treatment with participating providers and includes an Invisalign Essentials Bundle+. This initiative aims to increase access to Invisalign treatment for Costco members.

title: Costco Shoppers Shocked to Find Calvin Klein and Lands’ End Jackets for $44 Cheaper
summary: Costco shoppers are discovering significant savings on name-brand jackets, including Calvin Klein trench coats and Lands' End 3-in-1 Systems Jackets, with some items being up to $44 cheaper than retail prices. TikTok users are highlighting these finds, showcasing the availability of stylish and functional outerwear at competitive prices. The warehouse store also offers its own Kirkland brand parkas and other raincoats for as low as $12, making it a go-to spot for affordable outerwear.

title: 'So embarrassing,' cries Costco shopper escorted out by staff over receipt mix-up – it was all down to self-checkout
summary: A Costco shopper shared their embarrassing experience of being escorted out of a store due to a receipt mix-up after using self-checkout. This incident highlights ongoing customer frustration with Costco's self-checkout policies and strict membership rules, which have recently been reinforced with new scanning procedures. Another customer also detailed their negative experience with self-checkout, comparing Costco's approach to Walmart's.

title: Kroger and Albertsons’ Dirty Tricks To Preserve Greedflation
summary: Kroger and Albertsons are attempting to merge into a price-gouging behemoth despite legal challenges and regulatory scrutiny, including an FTC lawsuit alleging anti-competitive practices. The companies have engaged in extensive lobbying, and Albertsons executives are accused of deleting potentially incriminating evidence. Kroger is also suing to challenge the constitutionality of the FTC's internal administrative court to sidestep regulatory oversight.

title: Walmart overhauls marketplace with resale, logistics support
summary: Walmart Inc. is significantly enhancing its third-party marketplace with new solutions including "Resold at Walmart" for used items, expanded multichannel fulfillment through Walmart Fulfillment Services (WFS), and a new premium beauty assortment. These initiatives aim to attract more sellers and improve the customer experience by offering a wider range of products and more efficient logistics support, particularly ahead of the holiday season. The company is also waiving peak season storage fees and expanding cash advances for qualifying sellers, demonstrating a strong commitment to growth in its e-commerce segment.

title: Decoding BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings Inc (BJ): A Strategic SWOT Insight
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club (NYSE:BJ) shows strong sales and membership growth, driven by its unique warehouse club model and omnichannel strategy. However, the company faces challenges with high debt and limited geographic presence, alongside external threats from economic volatility and market competition. Opportunities exist in expansion and digital innovation, which are crucial for BJ's sustained growth.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) DCF Valuation: Is The Stock Undervalued?
summary: This article presents a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation for Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) to determine if its stock is undervalued. Based on the DCF analysis, Costco's stock is found to be overvalued, with a calculated DCF value of $553.04 per share against a current market price of $888.05, resulting in a -60.58% margin of safety. The article details Costco's business profile, recent share price performance, and the inputs used for the DCF model.

title: Where to find the cheapest gas in New Orleans
summary: Ahead of Labor Day weekend, gasoline prices in Louisiana are significantly lower than the national average, with the average price of regular gasoline at $2.95. The article provides a detailed breakdown of gas stations offering the cheapest fuel across the New Orleans Metro, Jefferson Parish, Northshore, and Bayou Parishes, with prices as low as $2.55.

title: Mike Philbrick's Top Picks:iShares Gold Bullion ETF, TD Q U.S. Small-Mid-Cap Equity ETF, and iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF.
summary: Mike Philbrick, CEO of ReSolve Asset Management, shares his top investment picks. These include the iShares Gold Bullion ETF, the TD Q U.S. Small-Mid-Cap Equity ETF, and the iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF.

title: Recession or Not, These 3 Stocks Are Winners
summary: Amid economic uncertainties, this article highlights three stocks capable of performing well regardless of a recession: Waste Management (WM), Costco Wholesale (COST), and Prudential Financial (PRU). These companies are characterized by strong fundamentals, consistent demand for their services, and positive analyst outlooks, making them resilient investment options. They offer stability and potential upside even if market conditions deteriorate.

title: Costco is gaining market share as merchandising efforts are working, analysts say
summary: Analysts report that Costco is successfully gaining market share, driven by effective merchandising efforts. The company's recent monthly numbers in August showed a significant double-digit gain in nonfood sales. This performance positions Costco favorably for sustained growth throughout the remainder of the year.

title: Costco reportedly testing mobile inventory search
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is reportedly beta testing a mobile app feature that allows customers to search inventory for in-stock items at selected stores. This new tool, visible to some app users, enables customers to check product availability by entering names or descriptions of items. The testing reportedly began in June 2024, with customer posts on social media confirming the new feature.

title: 3 Overvalued Stocks to Sell and 3 Undervalued Stocks to Buy Instead
summary: Morningstar strategists discuss current market conditions, including inflation, consumer spending, and sector valuations. They identify three overvalued stocks (Costco, Eli Lilly, Southern) to sell and three undervalued stocks (Kraft Heinz, Medtronic, Evergy) to buy, providing detailed rationale for each recommendation. The article also covers recent earnings for Nvidia, Salesforce, Broadcom, Dick's Sporting Goods, Chewy, and Bath & Body Works.

title: ¿BBVA cuánto cobrará por realizar transferencias a partir de septiembre?
summary: BBVA México is implementing new fees for bank transfers starting in September, but these charges will only affect certain business accounts. The measure aims to optimize the profitability of the bank's corporate products, specifically impacting users of BBVA Banca Electrónica for legal entities and BBVA Net Cash. Individual customers will not experience these new charges and will retain their current conditions and fees.

title: FDA Approves GMO Salmon for U.S. Distribution
summary: The FDA has approved genetically modified salmon produced by AquaBounty Technologies for U.S. distribution, lifting an import alert. This approval allows AquaBounty to begin farming AquAdvantage Salmon in Indiana, despite previous strong resistance from major retailers. The company views this decision as a significant milestone for biotechnology and agricultural innovation in sustainable food production.

title: Kroger ‘committed to closing the merger’ with Albertsons
summary: Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen reiterated the company's commitment to the $24.6 billion merger with Albertsons, despite ongoing litigation and regulatory scrutiny from the Federal Trade Commission. He expressed confidence in the deal's benefits for customers, associates, and communities, while also stating Kroger is prepared to move forward even if regulators block the transaction. The article also covers Kroger's flattish Q2 performance and the strategic rationale behind the merger, aiming to compete with larger retailers.

title: Kroger zeroes in on customer experience to build loyalty and sales
summary: Kroger is focusing on enhancing its customer experience through in-store improvements and convenient digital delivery options, leading to increased sales and customer loyalty. The grocer achieved a 33% year-over-year improvement in "perfect orders" and is leveraging AI and associate investments to speed up order fulfillment. These CX investments are helping to grow its loyalty program membership and drive long-term sales, even as it faces regulatory scrutiny over its planned merger with Albertsons.

title: In insult to animals and customers, Target breaks its animal welfare promises
summary: Target has failed to uphold its decade-old promises to transition to cage-free eggs and eliminate gestation crates for pigs in its supply chain, despite other major companies fulfilling similar commitments. This inaction is seen as an insult to animals and customers, as public polling indicates strong support for improved animal welfare practices. Humane World has launched a public campaign urging Target to honor its commitments and address systemic animal cruelty.

title: Kroger and Albertsons prepare to make a final federal court argument for their merger
summary: Kroger and Albertsons are preparing for their final federal court argument regarding their proposed $24.6 billion merger. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is seeking a preliminary injunction to block the deal, arguing it would harm consumers through higher prices and reduced competition, while the companies contend the merger would enable them to lower prices and better compete with retail giants. Several states have also filed lawsuits against the merger, and a Colorado trial is set to begin in late September.

title: Portland judge considers fate of the Kroger-Albertsons supermarket mega-merger
summary: A federal judge in Portland heard closing arguments in the proposed $25 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons, which would create the largest supermarket company in U.S. history. The Federal Trade Commission, joined by eight states including Oregon, argues the merger would reduce competition, harm workers, and raise prices, while Kroger contends it would allow for reduced prices and better competition against large retailers. The judge is expected to make a decision soon in a case that has drawn national attention due to concerns about inflation and grocery costs.

title: Inside closing arguments from the FTC’s challenge to Kroger-Albertsons merger
summary: Closing arguments in the FTC's challenge to the Kroger-Albertsons merger concluded, with both sides presenting their cases to a federal judge. The FTC argued the merger would harm local competition and that the divestiture plan was insufficient, while Kroger and Albertsons contended the merger is necessary to compete with industry giants and would benefit consumers through lower prices and a stronger C&S Wholesale Grocers. The judge will issue a decision on a preliminary injunction at a later date.

title: AutoZone remains a dominant player but NAPA is tops in customer trust
summary: A new study by Market Force Information reveals key insights into the auto parts retail market. While AutoZone leads in market share with 32.3% of visits, NAPA Auto Parts excels in customer trust and overall customer experience. The study also highlights that despite the rise of online shopping, the majority of consumers still prefer in-store purchases for convenience.

title: Sam’s Club announces starting pay increase to compete with Costco
summary: Sam’s Club is raising its starting pay for hourly retail workers from $15 to $16, effective early November, to better compete for talent. This change affects nearly 100,000 employees and also includes larger raises for long-tenured workers. Despite the increase, Sam's Club's new starting wage remains below Costco's, which was raised to $19.50 in July.

title: Amherst Costco takes official step forward - Buffalo Business First
summary: A new Costco retail warehouse in Amherst, New York, has taken an official step forward with a building permit application filed for the project. The construction cost for the Costco, located at 4230 Ridge Lea Road, is estimated to be nearly $22.49 million. This development signals progress for the long-awaited Costco location in the Buffalo area.

title: Sunrun Slips After Announcing End of Partnership With Costco
summary: Sunrun Inc. shares declined after the residential solar provider announced the termination of its sales partnership with Costco Wholesale Corp. The breakup occurred because the companies could not agree on terms, with Costco reportedly disfavoring Sunrun's subscription model due to its lower upfront revenue under standard accounting.

title: Sunrun reiterates stock target, hold rating despite Costco partnership end
summary: Sunrun (NASDAQ: RUN) has ended its sales partnership with Costco due to differing business priorities, but Truist Securities maintained its Hold rating and an $18.00 price target, expecting no substantial financial impact. The residential solar provider is redirecting sales efforts to other channels, including an expanded relationship with Lowe's, and has demonstrated strong stock performance and recent securitization deals. Despite an overall revenue decline, Sunrun expects net income growth this year and has surpassed 1 million customers.

title: Kroger SWOT Analysis (2025)
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of Kroger for 2025, examining its internal strengths and weaknesses, as well as external opportunities and threats. It highlights Kroger's extensive product range, strong brand, and financial performance as strengths, while noting weaknesses like limited international presence and vulnerability to cybersecurity threats. The analysis also identifies opportunities in e-commerce and private label expansion, alongside threats from intense competition and shifting consumer preferences.

title: Costco plans new store in Raleigh area — here's where
summary: Costco is planning to open a new store in Wake Forest, North Carolina, which will be its fifth location in the Raleigh and Durham region. This expansion targets a rapidly growing corridor in the Triangle area. The article highlights Costco's continued growth in the region, indicating a strategic focus on booming areas.

title: Costco made these subtle changes, adding enough ‘friction’ to prompt a downgrade
summary: A Truist analyst downgraded Costco's stock due to concerns over rich valuations despite the company's strong business performance and market share gains. The stock pulled back from a record high after the analyst recommended investors stop buying, highlighting increased selloff risk.

title: Market Analysis: Costco Wholesale And Competitors In Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail Industry
summary: This article provides a comprehensive industry comparison of Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ: COST) against its key competitors in the Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail industry. It analyzes important financial metrics, market position, and growth prospects to offer insights into Costco's performance, highlighting its valuation, profitability, and debt-to-equity ratio relative to peers.

title: Costco Wraps Fiscal Year With Steady Q4
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. concluded its fiscal year with a stable fourth quarter, reporting a 6.3% rise in U.S. adjusted sales comps and total revenue of $79.69 billion. E-commerce sales were a bright spot, leaping 19.4% in Q4, and membership figures remained strong even after a recent fee hike. The company also saw significant growth in store visits and continued demand for groceries and even gold bars, positioning it well for fiscal 2025 with 30 new warehouses opened.

title: Does Costco Own Kirkland’s Home Decor Stores?
summary: This article clarifies the common confusion between Costco's private label Kirkland Signature and the home decor retailer Kirkland's, Inc. It explains that Kirkland Signature is Costco's own brand, named after its headquarters, while Kirkland's, Inc. is a separate, independent company founded in 1966. Despite the similar names, the two entities are not related.

title: THE FRIDAY 5: New Leader at Stop & Shop; Kroger Prepares for 3rd Court Battle
summary: This article covers the top five food retail industry news items, including Roger Wheeler's new leadership role at Stop & Shop, Kroger's ongoing court battles regarding its merger with Albertsons, a potential port strike impacting the U.S. food supply chain, Whole Foods' research into Gen Z consumer preferences, and Weis Markets' expansion in Pennsylvania through an acquisition.

title: Costco's sales growth slows in Q4, but earnings beat estimates
summary: Costco reported solid financial results for its fourth quarter and fiscal year ending September 1, with earnings beating expectations despite weaker-than-expected revenue growth. Net sales for the full fiscal year reached $249.6 billion, a 5% rise, and net income increased significantly. The company highlights global expansion, e-commerce growth, and technological upgrades as key drivers for long-term success.

title: Costco’s sales are strong, but valuation ‘leaves no room for error,’ says analyst
summary: An analyst from Truist Securities noted that Costco's sales and margins are strong following its fourth-quarter results. However, the analyst, Scot Ciccarelli, cautioned that the company's current valuation has become "extremely stretched," leaving little room for error despite its positive performance.

title: CVS Mission and Vision Statement
summary: This article analyzes CVS Health's mission and vision statements, which focus on delivering superior, connected, and affordable human-centered healthcare experiences. It details how the company aims to improve customer health and well-being through innovative solutions, community engagement, and a patient-centric approach. The piece also explores CVS's core values, emphasizing putting people first, rising to challenges, fostering collaboration, simplifying processes, inspiring trust, and championing safety and quality.

title: Costco at Crossgates groundbreaking likely in 2025 - Albany Business Review
summary: Construction for the Costco at Crossgates is expected to commence in 2025, following delays caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and multiple unsuccessful lawsuits. This Costco would be the first in the Albany region, adding to the retailer's 891 stores worldwide.

title: Will Costco Stock Hit $1,000 in 2024?
summary: Shares of Costco Wholesale Corporation (COST) are up significantly, with potential to reach $1,000 in 2024 due to strong revenue growth, a robust membership base, and expanding e-commerce capabilities. Despite missing Q4 revenue expectations, Costco's comparable sales exceeded forecasts, driven by increased shopper traffic, impressive EPS, a growing paid membership, and strategic warehouse expansion. Analysts rate Costco a "Moderate Buy" with an average price target of $914.47, suggesting that even with a premium valuation, its strong growth prospects make a $1,000 target realistic.

title: Colorado antitrust trial in Kroger-Albertsons merger has King Soopers' parent dangling 10% price drop
summary: A Colorado antitrust trial against the Kroger-Albertsons merger has begun, with the state arguing the merger will increase grocery prices and reduce competition, especially in rural areas. Kroger's lawyers countered that the merger would allow them to offer prices 10-12% lower than Albertsons due to increased scale, better competing with retail giants like Walmart and Amazon. The state also alleged collusion between Kroger and Albertsons during a 2022 King Soopers worker strike.

title: Buy Costco American Express Transunion Stocks Motley Fo
summary: Shelby McFaddin, an investment analyst at Motley Fool Asset Management, suggests buying stocks like TransUnion, American Express, and Costco. She believes TransUnion will benefit from cooling inflation and renewed ad spending, while American Express is well-positioned to expand its cardholder base in a lower-rate environment due to its strong premium customer base. Costco is highlighted for its excellent management and ability to provide value to consumers, even with a rich valuation.

title: Are the Costco platinum bars worth buying? Here’s what finance pros say.
summary: Costco is now selling one-ounce platinum bars for $1,089.99 each, following its successful venture into selling gold bars. This price is slightly above the current market value of platinum, prompting financial experts to weigh in on whether these bars are a worthwhile investment. While gold sales were a huge success for Costco in 2023, the article explores if platinum will generate similar interest from investors.

title: Executive Vice President Claudine Adamo Sells Shares of Costco W
summary: Claudine Adamo, Executive Vice President of Costco Wholesale Corp (COST), sold 3,200 shares of the company on September 30, 2024. This transaction adds to a trend of 26 insider sells with no insider buys at Costco over the past year. The article notes that Costco's stock is currently considered "Significantly Overvalued" according to the GF Value, with a price-to-earnings ratio significantly higher than the industry median.

title: EXCLUSIVE Q&A: Lovesac extends sustainability to store growth, remodel plans
summary: Lovesac is integrating its "Designed for Life" sustainability standard into its building and remodeling plans, in addition to its product development. This strategy includes utilizing sustainable materials, installing LED lighting across all showrooms, and piloting energy management systems to enhance efficiency. The company plans to continue its store expansion, including shop-within-shops and pop-up locations, while focusing on sustainable design for long-term durability.

title: VDC: PEG Near 3 Is Just Too High Despite Bullish Technicals (NYSEARCA:VDC)
summary: The Vanguard Consumer Staples Index Fund ETF Shares (VDC) is currently overvalued with a P/E ratio above 21x and a PEG ratio of 2.95, resulting in a "hold" rating despite its attractive features like low fees, high liquidity, and a 1.3% higher yield than the S&P 500. While the ETF benefits from solid long-term technicals and favorable Q4 seasonals, current RSI weakness indicates a potential pause, suggesting a buying opportunity might arise if it approaches the $210 support level. The concentrated portfolio in large-cap value stocks such as Costco and Walmart necessitates close monitoring of these key holdings.

title: Costco’s Gold Bars Fly Off Shelves as Bullion Prices Smash Records
summary: Costco is experiencing high demand for its gold bullion bars, with products quickly selling out across the US. This phenomenon is attributed to gold's surging prices, Costco's competitive pricing compared to traditional dealers, and its appeal as a safe-haven asset and inflation hedge. The warehouse retailer is making gold accessible to a broader consumer base.

title: Costco reveals sales jump in first month after raising fees, boosted by one crucial week
summary: Costco reported a 9% rise in September sales to $24.62 billion after raising its membership fees. The sales boost was significantly contributed by the last week of September, which saw abnormal consumer activity due to Hurricane Helene and port strikes. This indicates that shoppers were unfazed by the recent membership-fee hike.

title: 4 Risky Stocks to Sell and 4 Picks to Buy Instead
summary: This article discusses the current market outlook, highlighting morningstar's assessment of overvalued sectors and stocks, particularly in consumer defensive and utilities. It offers specific stock recommendations to sell (Walmart, Costco, Vistra, Public Service Enterprise Group) and buy (Dollar General, Constellation Brands, Evergy, WEC Energy) based on valuation and long-term prospects. The analysis also touches on economic indicators, upcoming earnings reports for regional banks and tech companies, and the potential impact of AI on utilities.

title: In Colorado, Safeway would be owned by 2 companies post merger. Neither would be Albertsons.
summary: If the Kroger-Albertsons merger proceeds, Safeway stores in Colorado would be split between two owners: Kroger and C&S Wholesale Grocer. The article details the ongoing antitrust case in Colorado seeking to block the merger, highlighting concerns about competition, worker collusion allegations, and the suitability of C&S Wholesale Grocer as a retail operator. Albertsons CEO Vivek Sankaran testified that merging is essential for profitability and scale against larger retailers like Walmart and Costco.

title: How much money you'd have now if you invested $1,000 in Netflix 10 years ago
summary: This article analyzes the returns on a $1,000 investment in Netflix over various periods, including one, five, and ten years ago, as well as since its IPO. It highlights Netflix's recent stock performance due to password sharing crackdowns and new initiatives, and also discusses the company's decision to stop providing quarterly subscriber numbers. The article also recommends passive investing strategies like low-cost index funds as an alternative to hand-selecting individual stocks.

title: Why this money manager sees FirstService, Novo Nordisk and Microsoft as good long-term holdings
summary: Money manager Paul Harris of Harris Douglas Asset Management Inc. focuses on long-term investments in high-quality businesses, holding onto a core group of about two dozen stocks. He emphasizes that less than 4% of stocks drive most market gains and seeks companies with strong balance sheets and high returns on invested capital. His firm's top holdings include FirstService Corp., Novo Nordisk A/S, and Microsoft Corp., which he continues to buy for new clients due to their strong fundamentals and growth prospects in property management, diabetes/weight-loss drugs, and AI respectively.

title: Bend’s new Costco bustles with excitement Saturday during long-anticipated opening day
summary: Bend's highly anticipated new Costco store officially opened its doors on Saturday, October 19, 2024, replacing an older, smaller location. The new 185,000-square-foot warehouse, significantly larger than its predecessor, features ample parking and more spacious aisles, addressing previous customer concerns. Shoppers expressed immense excitement for the grand opening, enjoying increased product offerings and an expanded staff of 508 employees.

title: SNYR IPO News - Consumer products firm Synergy CHC prices Nasdaq uplisting at $9, the low end of the range
summary: Synergy CHC, a consumer products firm specializing in health care, beauty, and lifestyle products, priced its Nasdaq uplisting at $9 per share, the lower end of its expected range. The company raised $10 million by offering 1.2 million shares, 0.2 million more than initially anticipated. Synergy CHC, which owns brands like FOCUSfactor and Flat Tummy, plans to list under the symbol SNYR, with Roth Capital acting as the sole bookrunner.

title: Pro-Lifers to Walmart, Kroger, and Costco: Stop Putting Profit Over People. Instead, Refuse to Sell Chemical Abortion Pills
summary: A coalition of Christian and conservative investors, organized by Alliance Defending Freedom and led by Inspire Investing, has urged retailers like Walmart, Costco, and Kroger to refuse the sale of chemical abortion pills. They argue that selling these pills prioritizes profit over women's health, citing risks and potential legal issues associated with mifepristone. The article highlights concerns about the safety of chemical abortion, referencing a tragic death and FDA statistics on adverse outcomes, while criticizing the Biden administration's removal of safeguards.

title: Grainger Tops National Employee Opportunity Ranking
summary: W.W. Grainger Inc., a major industrial distributor, has been ranked as the top provider of employee opportunities among large U.S. companies in the 2024 American Opportunity Index. The company's performance is attributed to its core principles, recognition of its workforce as a competitive advantage, and various development programs. Grainger Chairman and CEO D.G. Macpherson emphasized the company's commitment to providing meaningful career opportunities for every team member.

title: XPO grows local shipments by 10% in Q3
summary: XPO increased its local shipment count by over 10% year-over-year in Q3, despite an overall decrease in shipments. This growth was attributed to improving service and reopening acquired Yellow Corp. service centers, adding 8,000 new local customers. The focus on higher-yield local shipments and premium services, combined with effective yield management and cost control, helped XPO improve margins and 1.9% YoY revenue growth in a challenging freight market.

title: Costco submits new plan for El Dorado Hills — no apartments or other retail, but a gas station
summary: Costco has submitted an updated proposal for a retail development in El Dorado Hills, which omits apartments and other retail spaces but includes a gas station. This new plan for the Silva Valley Parkway location represents significant changes from previous proposals. El Dorado County is currently reviewing the revised submission.

title: Kroger-Albertsons merger in court: 6 key takeaways
summary: This article discusses the key takeaways from the court battles surrounding the proposed Kroger-Albertsons merger, focusing on arguments made by the FTC, Washington state, Colorado, and the supermarket chains. Contentions centered on competition, pricing, and the proposed divestiture deal to C&S Wholesale Grocers. The article highlights the differing views on market definition, Albertsons' financial viability, the suitability of C&S as a competitor, and Kroger's pledge to lower prices post-merger.

title: Clorox Partnership Supports Suppliers With Sustainability Tracking
summary: The Clorox Company has partnered with Manufacture 2030 (M2030) to enhance sustainability tracking for its suppliers, enabling them to measure, manage, and reduce carbon emissions. This initiative allows Clorox to consolidate supplier sustainability data, export it for the Carbon Disclosure Project, and work towards its net-zero emissions goal by 2050. The article also highlights how other CPGs like Kenvue and Stanley are leveraging data and AI for their sustainability efforts.

title: Is Target (NYSE:TGT) Using Too Much Debt?
summary: This article analyzes Target's debt levels, concluding that while the company carries significant liabilities, its strong market capitalization and ability to cover interest expenses make its debt manageable. Target's net debt to EBITDA ratio is 1.3 times, and its EBIT covers its interest expense 14.7 times. Despite a weaker cash conversion of 43% of EBIT, the company's financial health is considered stable, with debt potentially boosting shareholder returns.

title: What the stock market is saying about Albertsons and Kroger
summary: The stock market is sending divergent signals about the proposed merger between Kroger and Albertsons, with Kroger's stock up over 30% this year while Albertsons' stock has declined more than 13%. Analysts suggest Albertsons needs the merger more than Kroger, and its stock performance reflects investor doubts about the deal's approval and the company's ability to compete independently. Kroger's stock strength is partly attributed to share buybacks and steady (though not stellar) results, positioning it to perform reasonably well even if the merger falls through.

title: Krispy Kreme restructuring, lowers earnings guidance
summary: Krispy Kreme is undergoing a management restructuring and has lowered its earnings guidance for 2024, despite accelerating its national rollout of doughnuts at McDonald’s. The restructuring follows the sale of Insomnia Cookies and aims to align talent and capital with business priorities, focusing on US expansion and a capital-light franchise model internationally. The company reported a net income in the third quarter primarily due to the Insomnia Cookies sale, but adjusted for the sale, sales were up 3.5%, though profitability was impacted by underperformance in the UK and increased logistics costs.

title: PHARMACIES, PIXELS, AND PRIVACY: Costco’s Prescription for Legal Trouble
summary: A federal court has largely allowed a lawsuit against Costco to proceed, challenging its use of Meta's tracking pixel on its pharmacy website. The lawsuit alleges that Costco illegally collected and shared sensitive prescription-related data, potentially violating federal and California privacy laws. The court's decision emphasizes that prescription searches are considered protected content, raising significant liability concerns for healthcare providers using similar tracking tools.

title: The 7 Big Grocery Store & Supermarket Stocks Ranked By Expected Returns
summary: This article ranks the top 7 grocery store stocks by their 5-year expected total returns, providing detailed analysis for each. It highlights key financial performance updates, dividend growth status, and the competitive landscape for these companies, including the impact of online shopping and Amazon's entry into the grocery sector. The analysis focuses on companies' abilities to adapt to changing consumer demands and maintain growth.

title: Costco Membership Fees Are What Makes It Profitable
summary: Costco's membership fees, while only 2% of annual revenue, are crucial to its profitability because they contribute 66% of the retailer's bottom line due to their presumed zero cost. The company recently raised its membership fees for the first time in seven years, impacting 52 million members. This move significantly boosts Costco's net income, which rose 17% to $7.37 billion in the last fiscal year.

title: Publix, Walmart and CVS: What stores are closed in Florida for Thanksgiving 2024?
summary: This article lists major retailers and grocery stores in Florida that will be closed or open with modified hours for Thanksgiving Day 2024. Publix, Sam's Club, Target, Walmart, Aldi, Winn-Dixie, and Trader Joe’s will be closed, while CVS and Whole Foods will have modified hours, and Walgreens will be closed unless they are 24-hour locations. The closures allow employees to spend time with loved ones during the holiday.

title: Should You Buy the Dip on Costco Wholesale Stock?
summary: This article examines whether Costco Wholesale stock is a good buy after a recent dip, noting its strong business model and resilience, but highlights its high valuation with a price-to-earnings multiple of 50. Despite its consistent growth and attractive membership-based model, the author advises against rushing to buy due to the stock being overly expensive, suggesting it should be on a watchlist instead. The Motley Fool Stock Advisor team also did not include Costco in their top 10 stock recommendations.

title: Delta Is Bringing Shake Shack Burgers To Its In-Flight Menu
summary: Delta Airlines is enhancing its in-flight menu by partnering with Shake Shack to offer cheeseburgers to first-class passengers on select flights from Boston starting December 1st. These meals, which include chips, a Caesar salad, and a brownie, will initially be available on routes over 900 miles, with plans for a broader rollout to more U.S. markets in 2025. This collaboration aligns with Delta's focus on service excellence and community engagement.

title: Target Earnings: Stock Craters Amid Weak Demand for Discretionary Items, Further Margin Pressure
summary: Target's stock cratered after its third-quarter results showed weak demand for discretionary items and further margin pressure, leading Morningstar to plan a reduction in its fair value estimate. The retailer saw only 1% top-line growth and cut its full-year EPS guidance. Despite a planned fair value estimate cut, Morningstar's longer-term outlook for comparable sales growth and operating margin remains intact.

title: Target Shares Tumble After Retailer Cuts Profit Outlook
summary: Target (TGT) cut its full-year profit outlook after a disappointing quarter, causing shares to fall over 20%. The retailer cited reduced consumer spending on nonessential items and unexpected costs from an inventory buildup ahead of a potential US port strike. Investors are reportedly losing patience with Target's turnaround plan as rival Walmart continues to gain market share.

title: BJ’s stock rises on first membership-fee increase in 7 years
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club announced its first membership fee increase in seven years, leading to a rise in its stock. Effective January 1, 2025, the BJ Club membership will increase by $5 to $60, and the Club+ membership will increase by $10 to $120. This follows a similar fee hike by competitor Costco earlier this year.

title: Kroger CMO Stuart Aitken to step down
summary: Kroger announced that Stuart Aitken, chief merchandising and marketing officer, will step down at the end of the year to pursue other opportunities. Mary Ellen Adcock, senior vice president of operations, will succeed him, taking over on January 1. Aitken played a significant role in Kroger's fresh-focused, omnichannel strategy and expansion of alternative revenue streams, during a sensitive period for the grocer awaiting merger approval with Albertsons.

title: Gotta Love Lindale Rumors - A Kentucky Born Texas Steakhouse Could Be Coming
summary: Lindale, Texas is abuzz with rumors of a Texas Roadhouse restaurant possibly opening in the area, specifically along the I-20 and Highway 69 corridor. This follows a trend of big-name business speculation in Lindale, which has historically included whispers of Disney, Buc-ee's, Target, Costco, and H-E-B. While the exact location and certainty of Texas Roadhouse's arrival remain debated among residents, the prospect is generating excitement in the community.

title: Circana names Kroger exec Stuart Aitken president and CEO
summary: Circana, a retail data analytics company, has appointed Stuart Aitken, currently Kroger’s chief merchandising and marketing officer, as its new president and CEO, effective January 1, 2025. Aitken brings extensive experience from leading data-focused organizations like Dunnhumby and 84.51°, and his selection highlights Circana's focus on customer-centric merchandising and digital revenue growth. His departure from Kroger, where he was instrumental in driving high-margin digital revenue streams, marks the second C-suite executive to leave the grocer this year for a high-level position.

title: 10 Major Arizona Industries to Consider if You’re Working in or Moving to the Grand Canyon State
summary: Arizona's economy is diverse, offering job opportunities across various sectors for those looking to work in or move to the state. Key industries include third-party administration and insurance, automotive retail, healthcare, commercial banking, public education, and several retail and insurance segments. The article highlights major companies within each sector and suggests cities for potential residents to consider.

title: Costco Gold Membership is up for grabs at a shockingly low price — but only for a short time
summary: A limited-time deal on Stack Social offers Costco's Gold Star Membership for an effective price of $20, significantly down from its usual $65 annual fee. This discount is achieved by including a $45 Costco Shop Card with the membership. The offer is valid for new members or those whose memberships have expired for over 18 months, and it includes a free Household Card.

title: DICK’S Sporting Goods: The Under-the-Radar Buy-and-Hold Winner
summary: DICK’S Sporting Goods (DKS) is presented as a strong buy-and-hold candidate for dividend-growth portfolios due to its sustained financial health, growth, and capital returns. The company reported a solid beat-and-raise quarter, indicating resilience against macroeconomic headwinds and a positive outlook for future growth and analyst upgrades. DKS maintains solid margins, generates ample cash flow, and offers a healthy dividend, making it an attractive investment.

title: Forget Costco Stock: Buy These 3 ETFs Instead
summary: This article suggests three ETFs as alternative investments to Costco stock, despite Costco's strong performance. It highlights Fidelity MSCI Consumer Staples Index ETF (FSTA), VanEck Retail ETF (RTH), and iShares Global Consumer Staples ETF (KXI) for their exposure to Costco and broader consumer staples or retail sectors. The article details the holdings, expense ratios, and ratings for each ETF, providing a diversified investment approach.

title: Is Another Big Special Dividend Coming Up for Costco Wholesale Investors in December?
summary: Costco Wholesale has historically issued special dividends in strong years, particularly in December. While the company has a low payout ratio and could increase its regular dividend, it favors special dividends for flexibility. However, given more tepid growth and a special dividend paid last year, the author does not anticipate another one in December, despite the stock's strong performance.

title: When will Costco open its Buffalo-area store?
summary: The opening date for Costco's first Buffalo-area store remains uncertain, despite news breaking in spring 2022 about the project. Costco reportedly wants the site fully built out before beginning construction on its store, which is planned as part of the Amherst Commerce Center development. The retailer has yet to officially confirm its arrival in the area.

title: Fast-food restaurant planned at proposed St. Augustine Walmart Supercenter site
summary: A fast-food restaurant with a dual drive-thru, consulted by a frequent Chick-fil-A partner, is planned for an outparcel at the future St. Augustine Walmart Supercenter. The restaurant will be 5,558 square feet with seating for 106 inside and 16 outside, and features a double drive-thru capable of handling 57 cars. The larger Walmart project, including the restaurant and a gas station, is still in the pre-application phase.

title: After Earnings, Is Target Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar assessed Target's stock after its Q3 earnings miss and revised forecast. Despite a share plunge, Morningstar believes Target's stock is currently fairly valued at $135 per share, aligning with its 3-star rating, and notes the company lacks an economic moat due to intense retail competition. The article also discusses Target's strong financial position but highlights significant risks from digital retail competition, particularly from Walmart and Amazon.

title: VictoryShares Launches GFLW, a Growth-Oriented FCF ETF
summary: VictoryShares has launched its new Free Cash Flow Growth ETF (GFLW), focusing on high-quality, profitable, large-cap growth companies. This ETF expands VictoryShares' existing FCF suite by targeting companies with strong free cash flow profitability and significant growth prospects. GFLW aims to provide investors with exposure to companies capable of compounding FCF generation through a unique methodology that screens for profitability and growth potential.

summary: This article provides current and historical stock price data for the First Trust Global Tactical Commodity Strategy Fund (FTGC).
