The page also features recent articles related to shares and client reviews of the Capital.com platform.

title: Costco’s results will show us how important bargains still are for shoppers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is set to release its quarterly earnings, which are anticipated to highlight the continued importance of value for consumers. The results will also shed light on the performance disparity between warehouse retailers like Costco, Walmart, and Amazon compared to other retailers. This earnings report is expected to provide key insights into current retail trends.

title: Costco’s Popular Kirkland Baby Diapers Are Shifting Suppliers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is changing the manufacturer for its Kirkland Signature brand diapers from Kimberly-Clark Corp. to First Quality. This change, effective in January, comes as Kimberly-Clark scales back its private label businesses to improve profitability.

title: Costco’s Extremely In-Demand Item Will Drop In Quality, Insiders Say
summary: Costco's popular Kirkland Signature Diapers are reportedly switching manufacturers from Kimberly-Clark Corp. (Huggies) to First Quality (Cuties) starting in January due to Kimberly-Clark's desire to focus on premium brands. This change has led to fears among shoppers that the quality of the beloved and affordable Kirkland diapers may decline, despite currently being lauded for their similarity to Huggies. Customers and experts suggest that any change in product quality following the supplier switch will be noticeable to consumers.

title: Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company ETF (FNDX) Stock Price Quote Today & Current Price Chart
summary: This article provides the current stock price quote and chart for the Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company ETF (FNDX), highlighting its current trading data, key statistics, and CFD trading conditions. It details aspects like spread, overnight funding adjustments, margin requirements, and commission. The page also features a section with related market articles and customer reviews for the trading platform.

title: Albertsons sues Kroger after judge rules against grocery merger
summary: Albertsons has formally terminated its proposed $25 billion merger with Kroger and is suing its competitor, alleging Kroger violated their contract regarding the deal's approval process. This legal action follows a judge blocking the planned tie-up and highlights a dispute over responsibility for legal fees and a potential $600 million termination fee. Kroger has called Albertsons' allegations "baseless and without merit."

title: Albertsons gives up on Kroger merger, sues grocery chain
summary: Albertsons is suing Kroger and abandoning their $24.6 billion merger after judges halted the deal, citing Kroger's alleged failure to secure regulatory approval. Albertsons claims Kroger did not exert "best efforts" to overcome antitrust objections, which Kroger denies, accusing Albertsons of breaching the merger agreement. The lawsuit follows preliminary and permanent injunctions issued in federal courts in Oregon and Washington.

title: GROCERY MEGA-MERGER: Day after court rulings, Albertsons/Safeway bags the plan
summary: Albertsons has officially terminated its merger agreement with Kroger following injunctions issued by courts in Oregon and Washington state on December 10, 2024. Albertsons announced its decision while also filing a lawsuit against Kroger, accusing Kroger of willfully breaching the merger agreement. Kroger, in turn, called the lawsuit "baseless and without merit."

title: What’s ahead for Kroger & Albertsons after their failed merger
summary: Following the failed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons due to regulatory blocking, both companies are now seeking individual strategies to gain market share. Key areas of focus include investing in e-commerce and advertising platforms, expanding private label brands, and potentially pursuing smaller, non-overlapping mergers or acquisitions. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general hailed the merger's failure as a victory for consumers, preventing higher grocery prices.

title: Genetically Engineered Salmon Production Ends as AquaBounty Shutters Last Facility
summary: AquaBounty Technologies (NASDAQ: AQB) has announced the cessation of all genetically engineered AquAdvantage® salmon production, the culling of remaining fish, and the closure of its last North American facility in Prince Edward Island, Canada. This decision follows decades of controversy, market rejection, and legal challenges, with the company citing insufficient liquidity to maintain operations. Environmental groups, Indigenous communities, and allies celebrate this as a victory against GE food animals and emphasize the importance of sustainable wild salmon and ecosystem protection.

title: Kroger to move on from failed Albertsons merger 'from a position of strength'
summary: Kroger has terminated its $24.6 billion agreement to acquire Albertsons Cos. after regulatory injunctions, stating it is no longer in its best interests to pursue the merger. Following the termination, Kroger plans to resume share repurchases with a new $7.5 billion buyback program, leveraging its strong balance sheet to invest in business growth and return capital to shareholders. The company will continue with its "Leading with Fresh and Accelerating with Digital" strategy, focusing on investments in lower prices, higher associate wages, and store network expansion.

title: Kimberly-Clark ends partnership with Costco for diaper production
summary: Kimberly-Clark has announced it will stop producing Huggies diapers for Costco, shifting its business strategy to prioritize higher-margin premium products under its own brand. This move is expected to result in a 2% drop in Kimberly-Clark’s profits next year, while Costco will begin selling diapers made by First Quality under its Kirkland Signature brand. The company aims to focus investments on capacity and technology to strengthen its own brands.

title: Costco Goes Greener in Latest Fiscal Year
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has released its annual update on sustainability commitments, detailing progress in operations, people and communities, and merchandising. The company is actively working on its Climate Action Plan, expanding its workforce dashboard, and increasing sustainable merchandise offerings by engaging directly with suppliers and partnering with organizations like the Seafood Task Force. These efforts align with an evolving regulatory landscape and Costco's commitment to a more sustainable future for its stakeholders.

title: Is Moderna Stock Underperforming the Dow?
summary: Moderna (MRNA) stock has significantly underperformed the Dow Jones Industrials Average, plummeting 75.5% from its 52-week high and 57.9% year-to-date. This underperformance is attributed to declining COVID-19 vaccine sales and uncertainty surrounding future revenue growth, despite the company's large market cap and mRNA technology advantage. Wall Street analysts are cautious, giving MRNA a "Hold" rating with an 88.2% potential upside from current levels.

title: Luxury furniture designer to open in shuttered NW 23rd space
summary: King Living, a luxury furniture designer, is set to open its third U.S. showroom in the former Williams Sonoma storefront in Northwest Portland next summer. This expansion marks a new development for the area, utilizing a previously shuttered retail space. The article was written by Sara Edwards for the Portland Business Journal.

title: 5 lessons for grocers from the Kroger-Albertsons saga
summary: The collapse of the Kroger-Albertsons merger offers five critical lessons for the grocery industry, ranging from effective merger messaging to the risks of mega-mergers and the importance of strategic divestiture partners. Analysts suggest that Albertsons must now redefine its competitive strategy, while Kroger may pursue smaller acquisitions. The saga underscores the ongoing vulnerability of traditional supermarkets against giants like Walmart and Costco, potentially leading to more M&A activity driven by the need for scale.

title: Join the club: The economics of membership retail
summary: The article discusses the growing trend of membership retail, highlighting how warehouse clubs like BJ's and Costco have recently increased their membership fees and continue to see high renewal rates. It also explores the expansion of subscription models beyond traditional clubs, noting how giants like Amazon and Target are leveraging subscriptions for delivery and perks, and how niche lifestyle brands like Fabletics and Liquid I.V. are entering this space to cater to younger consumers' hobbies and interests. The piece emphasizes the benefits for both consumers, who receive convenience and extras, and companies, which gain recurring revenue and engaged customers.

title: Liberty Hill moves closer to reeling in its 'whale': Costco
summary: Costco is reportedly moving closer to opening its seventh Austin-area location in Liberty Hill, Texas. The retail giant appears to have a site under contract, although the construction timeline remains unclear. This expansion signifies continued growth for Costco in the Austin metropolitan area.

title: Christmas Eve 2024: Store hours for Costco, Walmart, Walgreens, Target and more
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of Christmas Eve 2024 store hours for numerous major retailers including Walmart, Target, Costco, and Walgreens. Many stores will close early on Christmas Eve, with some, like Big Lots and Party City, facing store closures and liquidation sales, highlighting the compressed shopping season. Shoppers are advised to check local store websites or apps for the most accurate hours.

title: What Stores Are Open and Closed on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to the operating hours of various stores, financial institutions, pharmacies, and postal services on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day 2024. Many businesses will be closed or have reduced hours, particularly on Christmas Day, to allow employees to celebrate the holiday. Shoppers are advised to check local store hours, especially for independently owned businesses.

title: The Walmart Effect
summary: New research suggests that Walmart has a broadly negative economic impact on the communities it operates in, challenging the long-held belief that its low prices significantly benefit consumers. Two papers indicate that the costs of lower earnings and higher unemployment outweigh the savings for shoppers, ultimately making communities poorer. The findings also question the consumer-welfare standard used in antitrust regulation, suggesting it overlooks broader economic impacts beyond price.

title: 3 Stocks With Rising Prices That Are Likely to Split in 2025
summary: The article identifies Broadcom (AVGO), Casey's General Stores (CASY), and Costco (COST) as companies whose stock prices are high enough to warrant a stock split in 2025. Stock splits make shares more affordable, increase market liquidity, and signal company confidence, often leading to outperformance. The author details the financial health and growth drivers for each company, reinforcing the likelihood of future splits.

title: Costco Drops Amid Yield Concerns: Why $900 Could Be the Next Big Opportunity
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) experienced a 3% drop due to rising 10-year Treasury yields, signaling investor concerns about inflation and consumer spending. Despite a strong 43% gain in 2024, the selloff highlights macroeconomic headwinds. Analysts are watching the stock's 50-day moving average, with a potential short-term target of $900, which could be a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

title: Costco defends DEI program as other major retailers drop controversial diversity push
summary: Costco's board of directors is urging shareholders to vote against a proposal to eliminate its Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) program, defending its practices as beneficial for employees, members, and suppliers. This comes as other major retailers have scaled back similar initiatives following a Supreme Court ruling and warnings from state attorneys general. The National Center for Public Policy Research is challenging Costco's DEI program, alleging it involves discriminatory practices and rebrands rather than eliminates problematic policies.

title: Costco to shut down 500 stores for 24 hours with Aldi and Sam's Club also closed
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp will close all 500+ of its U.S. stores on New Year's Day, January 1, 2025, following a Christmas Day closure. Other major retailers like Aldi and Sam's Club will also be closed, while Walmart, Target, and Kroger will maintain normal operating hours. All affected retailers will resume regular operations on January 2.

title: 3 Reasons Costco Stock Will Have More Room to Run in 2025
summary: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) stock, despite a recent dip, is poised for further growth in 2025 due to strong customer retention, ambitious expansion plans including e-commerce, and a robust cash balance. The company's recent membership fee increase has not impacted its high retention rate, and ongoing store openings and digital growth, alongside a significant cash position and potential future stock split, suggest continued upside.

title: How Vending Kiosks Curb Store Shrink and Optimize Labor
summary: Cantaloupe, Inc. has expanded its Smart Store vending machine line (600 and 700 models) for grocery stores, aiming to reduce shrink, optimize labor, and offer convenient shopping for shelf-stable and fresh items. These machines use weighted shelves and cameras for inventory monitoring and allow various payment methods. According to Cantaloupe's chief revenue officer, Jeff Dumbrell, the kiosks can nearly eliminate theft and improve customer experience by speeding up transactions, even for high-cost items typically prone to theft.

title: 3 new Costco stores are coming to this booming area of North Texas
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. plans to open three new stores in Collin County, North Texas, in 2025, specifically in Celina, Prosper, and Allen. These new locations are driven by the area's robust population growth and existing Costco stores operating at full capacity. The expansion underscores major retailers' significant investment in this rapidly growing part of the Metroplex.

title: Retailers Try on More Tech
summary: Retailers are entering a new phase of growth driven by AI and automation, according to Morgan Stanley. Key technologies like retail media, AI, and automation are expected to boost profitability and growth, particularly for larger retailers who can invest more in these advancements. This technological adoption will lead to margin expansion and consolidation within the retail sector.

title: Why the S&P 500 ESG Index Continues to Outperform the S&P 500
summary: The S&P 500 ESG Index has consistently outperformed the S&P 500, especially since Q4 2021, driven primarily by stock selection through the exclusion of lower ESG-scoring companies. This outperformance is attributed to factors like strong climate strategy, risk management, and governance. The article also details the index's construction, recent rebalance additions and exclusions, and anticipates future ESG catalytic regulations.

title: Costco is cracking down on membership moochers
summary: Costco is implementing stricter measures to prevent non-members from using membership cards, particularly at self-checkout registers. Employees are now requiring members to show their photo ID in addition to their membership card. This move aims to ensure that customers pay for their own memberships, aligning with Costco's business model.

title: Spooked shoppers load up on toilet paper during port strike
summary: Shoppers in the U.S. are stocking up on toilet paper and other necessities due to fears of supply chain disruptions from a port strike and increased demand in areas affected by Hurricane Helene. Retailers like Costco, Kroger, and Walmart are seeing spikes in demand, with some implementing purchase limits, though major manufacturers believe their supply chains are prepared for the strike. This behavior echoes the early days of the pandemic when similar stocking up occurred.

title: Costco Wholesale (COST) ROIC % : 20.73% (As of Aug. 2025)
summary: This article details Costco Wholesale's Return on Invested Capital (ROIC %) as 20.73% as of August 2025, highlighting its historical data and competitive comparison within the Discount Stores subindustry. title: Costco's CEO on how the big U.S. port strike could impact holiday shopping
summary: Costco (COST) Wholesale Corp. is addressing potential supply chain disruptions due to a looming U.S. port strike, especially for nonfood imports ahead of the holiday season. CEO Ron Vachris stated that the company has implemented contingency plans, including pre-shipping goods and exploring alternative ports, to mitigate the impact. While acknowledging the potential for disruption, Costco's reliance on a mix of imported and domestic nonfood items helps manage the risk.

title: Costco raises membership fee for first time since 2017
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is increasing its annual membership fees for the first time since 2017. The standard membership fee will rise by $5 to $65, and the premium "Executive Membership" fee will increase by $10 to $130, effective September 1. This move, long anticipated by Wall Street, will impact approximately 52 million memberships.

title: Here's what to know about Costco coming to the Treasure Coast
summary: Costco is under construction in Stuart, Florida, with plans to open by spring 2025, offering a big-box store, gas station, restaurants, and apartments. This new development on Kanner Highway also includes a separate distribution center relocation to Port St. Lucie. The project is a significant addition to the Treasure Coast, with developers building and funding a new public road to connect Kanner Highway and Willoughby Boulevard.

title: Costco in Port St. Lucie? Here are five things to know about the distribution depot
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. plans to build a new distribution depot in Port St. Lucie, relocating its facility from West Palm Beach to a nearly 200-acre site in Southern Grove. The project, including tax breaks approved by the City Council, is expected to create 265 jobs and have a significant economic impact. While only a distribution center has been confirmed, city officials hint at efforts to bring a retail store to Port St. Lucie as well.

title: Costco plans to move distribution center to Port St. Lucie from West Palm Beach
summary: Costco is relocating its distribution center from West Palm Beach to Port St. Lucie, with approval granted for tax breaks and land deals for "Project Everest." The new facility is expected to create 265 full-time jobs and could lead to a future Costco retail store in the area. The distribution center project is anticipated to have a significant economic impact on the region.

title: COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP /NEW SEC 10-K Report
summary: Costco Wholesale Corporation has released its Form 10-K report for fiscal year 2024, detailing significant financial growth including a 5% increase in net sales to $249,625 million and a 17% increase in net income to $7,367 million. The report highlights strategic initiatives such as warehouse expansion, e-commerce growth, and private-label penetration, alongside future plans for opening new warehouses. Costco also addresses challenges and risks, including market competition, economic factors, supply chain disruptions, and regulatory changes, outlining management strategies to mitigate these issues.

title: How these three women choose what you’ll buy at Walmart
summary: This article highlights the critical role of three women at Walmart Inc. who are responsible for selecting the vast majority of goods sold, totaling $650 billion annually. Latriece Watkins, Megan Crozier, and Andrea Albright are chief merchants and sourcing executives for Walmart U.S., Sam's Club, and global sourcing, respectively. They explain how they identify trends, work with buyers and suppliers, and make strategic decisions to ensure the right products are on shelves for customers, especially during competitive times like the holiday season.

title: Innovators in alcohol-free: TÖST
summary: TÖST is a non-alcoholic beverage founded in 2017 by Brooks Addington, offering an elevated drink experience with a blend of white tea and botanicals. The brand has gained significant traction, including a minority investment from Constellation Brands, and is expanding its reach with new canned formats and flavors in 2025. TÖST aims to provide a sophisticated alternative for consumers seeking alcohol-free options in a growing moderation movement.

title: EXEC: Hydro Flask Adds Velocity with Expanding Amazon, Target and Costco Programs
summary: Helen of Troy Limited, parent company of Hydro Flask, Osprey, and OXO brands, reported positive momentum in its Home & Outdoor segment for Q3 fiscal year 2025, partially offsetting declines in Beauty & Wellness. Hydro Flask saw significant distribution gains at Target and Costco, alongside strong e-commerce performance, including being Amazon's #1 Best Seller during Prime Day. The company also detailed its Project Pegasus restructuring plan, aimed at improving operating margins, and provided an updated fiscal 2025 outlook including the acquisition of Olive & June.

title: News | Albertsons steps up streamlining of stores, including closings
summary: Albertsons is moving forward with streamlining its store portfolio, which will include both opening and closing locations, after its proposed merger with Kroger was blocked. The company aims to cut $1.5 billion in costs over the next three years and will focus on optimizing its real estate footprint. While there may be more closures than previously seen due to "general hygiene of the real estate portfolio," Albertsons also plans for new store openings and will consider strategic transactions to create long-term shareholder value.

title: What to know about Costco memberships, food court, rewards, location, returns, refunds
summary: This article provides key information on Costco ahead of its Treasure Coast opening, covering membership benefits, the popular food court, and the store's generous return policy. It details the differences between Gold Star and Executive memberships, lists popular food court items and prices, and clarifies exceptions to their refund policy for electronics and certain high-value items.

title: ACVF - Conservative Values ETF - Divests from Costco and Allstate expanding its fight against corporate 'Woke-ism” and DEI
summary: The American Conservative Values ETF (ACVF) has divested its holdings in Costco and Allstate, citing the companies' commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives. Simultaneously, ACVF has removed its boycott of Walmart and added the retailer to its portfolio, praising Walmart's move away from DEI efforts. This action is part of ACVF's broader strategy to combat corporate "woke-ism" and reward companies that align with conservative values.

title: Here’s what’s being built along Riverside Boulevard near Costco in Loves Park
summary: A new Valvoline Instant Oil Change is currently under construction in Loves Park, near the Costco and Burger King interchange at Interstate 90 and Riverside Boulevard. The 2,028-square-foot facility will feature three oil change bays at 4020 Stadium Drive, though a grand opening date has not yet been set. This addition continues the development in Loves Park's growth corridor, following the recent opening of a new four-story extended-stay hotel.

title: BJ's Wholesale Reaches 250 Clubs With Latest Opening in Kentucky
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. announced the opening of its 250th club in Louisville, KY, marking its first location in Kentucky and expanding its presence to the 21st state. The company continues to drive growth through strategic initiatives like expanding its own-brand portfolio and enhancing omnichannel capabilities, which has resulted in increased membership and strong sales performance. Despite the stock trading at a premium, its strong performance and strategic focus position it for long-term success.

title: Once Upon a Farm debuts protein bars
summary: Once Upon a Farm has launched new Refrigerated Protein Bars, now available nationwide. These organic and Non-GMO Project Verified bars are designed for active kids, offering 8 grams of protein from milk and whey concentrate, real fruit and vegetables, and whole-grain oats with no added sugar. The company, co-founded by Jennifer Garner, aims to provide nutritious and delicious snack options in flavors like Oatmeal Chocolate and Cinnamon Roll.

title: New Sprouts Farmers Market location draws crowds to Delaware town
summary: A new Sprouts Farmers Market has opened in Middletown, Delaware, attracting crowds to the town. Host Ashley Harder reported on the new grocery store, highlighting its contribution to enabling a consciously healthy lifestyle for residents.

title: Costco to make major change to food courts this summer
summary: Costco announced a significant change for its food courts, switching from Pepsi to Coca-Cola products starting in the summer. This decision was revealed by CEO Ron Vachris during an investor meeting, though no specific reason for the change was given. The popular $1.50 hot dog and soda combo price will remain unchanged despite this beverage swap.

title: Costco confirms major food court changes
summary: Costco is making a significant change to its food courts by switching back to Coca-Cola products after more than a decade of serving Pepsi. This decision was announced by CEO Ron Vachris during the company's annual shareholders meeting. Importantly, the price of the famous $1.50 hotdog combo will remain unchanged.

title: The clock is ticking for Costco and Teamsters to unite on a new contract
summary: Costco and the Teamsters Union are nearing a deadline for a new contract affecting approximately 18,000 workers nationwide. Teamsters have authorized a strike if an agreement isn't reached, citing Costco's failure to bargain constructively. Costco's CEO claims good relations with the union and highlights the company's "superior" employee benefits and wages.

title: QQQ vs ONEQ: Is There Any Real Difference Between These ETFs?
summary: This article compares two ETFs, Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Fidelity Nasdaq Composite Index ETF (ONEQ), for investors looking to bet on big tech and AI. While both offer exposure to tech-heavy indices, QQQ tracks the Nasdaq 100 (100 largest non-financial firms) and ONEQ follows the Nasdaq Composite (over 1,000 stocks). The author notes QQQ's higher returns over 10 years but suggests ONEQ might be a better pick for broader exposure and potential future performance driven by mid-cap and financial sector holdings.

title: Complaint Filed Against Grocery Outlet
summary: A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. in Northern California, alleging investor losses due to misleading disclosures related to a tech upgrade. The complaint, filed as Liberato v. Grocery Outlet Holding Corp., focuses on the period from November 2023 to May 2024, during which investors reportedly sustained losses. The company attributed worse-than-expected results in May 2024 to tech challenges.

title: Celebrating Black History Month: Best practices for social media and beyond
summary: This article explores how brands can authentically celebrate Black History Month and integrate Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) initiatives year-round, especially as companies reduce their DEIA efforts. title: Consumers Rank Speed as Top Reason for Self-Checkout
summary: A report by NCR Voyix, "2025 Commerce Experience Report," reveals that speed is the primary reason shoppers opt for self-checkout, with 77% preferring it for faster transactions and shorter lines. summary: First Solar has committed to excluding deep-sea mined minerals from its supply chain, marking a significant win for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) shareholder activists. This decision, prompted by a shareholder resolution from As You Sow, signals continued corporate attention to environmental concerns despite potential political headwinds. The agreement highlights an ongoing receptiveness among some companies to ESG principles, even as overall resolution filings might slightly decrease.

title: Costco Just Brought Back This Customer-Favorite Garden Gem for Spring
summary: Costco has brought back its customer-favorite self-watering raised cedar planter for $149.99, the same price as the previous year. It also prevents dogs from disturbing plants and allows for good drainage.

title: BJ's Wholesale Harnessing Digitization & Membership for Growth
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club is set to sustain its growth momentum by focusing on digital innovation and expanding its membership base. The company has invested in its digital infrastructure to enhance customer experience, offering services like same-day delivery and curbside pickup, which has led to increased engagement and higher average purchase values from digitally-enabled members. BJ's strong membership model, supported by successful acquisition efforts, increased renewal rates, and a recent membership fee hike, is expected to continue driving revenue growth.

title: This huge chain closed all its stores; smaller-format locations are coming back in 2025
summary: Bed Bath & Beyond, which filed for bankruptcy in 2023, is making a retail comeback with smaller-format stores. This return is due to a multi-million-dollar investment from Kirkland’s Inc., which will operate the new stores as part of a strategic partnership with Beyond, the parent company of Bed Bath & Beyond. The first new store is expected to open later in 2025, focusing on a more efficient, neighborhood-focused format.

title: Canned Tuna From Walmart, Costco Recalled Over Botulism Risk
summary: Tri-Union Seafoods has issued a voluntary recall of canned tuna products sold at major retailers like Walmart, Costco, Trader Joe's, and Harris Teeter. The recall is due to a defect in the can's pull tab, which could lead to leakage or contamination with Clostridium botulinum, a potentially fatal bacteria. The company advises customers to discard affected products immediately.

title: CVS Q4 tops Street; revenue up 4.2%
summary: CVS Health Corp. reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and revenue, despite a drop in net income and adjusted earnings per share due to cost pressures in its insurance business. Total revenue increased by 4.2% to $97.71 billion, exceeding analyst estimates. The company anticipates full-year adjusted earnings in the range of $5.75 to $6 per share for the upcoming fiscal year.

title: Kroger names new CFO
summary: Kroger has appointed David Kennerley, formerly Senior Vice President and CFO for PepsiCo Europe, as its new chief financial officer, effective April 3. He will succeed interim CFO Todd Foley, who plans to retire at the end of the fiscal first quarter. Kennerley's appointment is a significant C-suite change for Kroger, occurring as the company navigates its business strategy after its unsuccessful merger attempt with Albertsons.

title: Costco Was Just Dethroned As the Top Warehouse Club for Customer Service
summary: Sam's Club has surpassed Costco to become the top warehouse club for customer service, according to the latest American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI) report. Sam's Club's rise is attributed partly to its adoption of new technology like Scan & Go and a focus on curbside pickup. Costco, while maintaining its ACSI score, dropped to second place as Sam's Club's score significantly increased.

title: 3 Consumer Staples ETFs for Stability in a Volatile Market
summary: In a market experiencing volatility due to inflation and tariff uncertainties, consumer staples ETFs can offer stability and defensive investment options. summary: As gold prices reach record highs, the article explores two high-volatility option trading opportunities: a Newmont (NEM) mining strangle and a Costco (COST) skewed iron condor. The author, Michael "Dr. Data" Rechenthin, provides specific trade ideas for NEM and COST based on implied volatility and market conditions.

title: Retail Insights® 2025 Retail Universe for U.S. Premium Natural, Organic Foods, Supplements & Personal Care
summary: In 2024, the U.S. natural organic products market saw significant growth, adding $7.137 billion in sales to reach $110.75 billion, outpacing conventional grocery channels. Supernaturals like Whole Foods and Sprouts maintained their lead, while compact grocers and club stores experienced the highest percentage growth in natural organic sales. The report details the performance of eight retail channels, highlighting the increasing market share and productivity of natural organic products.

title: 'Makes sense why my daughter has been getting rashes': Costco shopper issues warning to parents who rely on Kirkland diapers
summary: Costco's decision to switch manufacturers for its Kirkland Signature diapers, from Kimberly-Clark Corp. to First Quality, has sparked concern and backlash among parents. Many shoppers, including one mother in a viral TikTok video, report that the new diapers are causing rashes and discomfort in their children, leading them to abandon the Kirkland brand despite its affordability. This change is reportedly part of Costco's strategy to prioritize name brands over its less profitable private label products.

title: Costco chairman reveals surprising luxury items that are selling out
summary: Costco's chairman, Hamilton "Tony" James, highlighted that the retailer successfully sells a surprising range of luxury items, from Porsches to Rolex watches, Dom Perignon, and gold bars. He noted that despite a generally average-income customer base, the presence of affluent members with double the average income allows Costco to move high-end products rapidly due to their appreciation for good deals. James also mentioned the recent quick sale of gold bars, questioning whether affluent individuals or those wary of the economy are driving these purchases.

title: QVCGA - QVC Group Inc Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides comprehensive stock information for QVC Group Inc (QVCGA), including its current price, financial metrics, and recent news. It details analyst ratings, insider transactions, and a timeline of corporate announcements, highlighting financial results, strategic moves like a reverse stock split, and management changes. The company operates through QxH, QVC International, and CBI segments, focusing on video and online commerce.

title: 98% of John Deere & Apple Shareholders Reject Anti-Diversity Proposals
summary: Shareholders of Deere & Co (NYSE:DE) and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) overwhelmingly rejected shareholder proposals aimed at undermining diversity and inclusion programs, with votes against reaching over 98% at both companies. This follows a similar rejection at Costco, indicating a strong shareholder belief that diversity and inclusion are material to profitable growth and financial outperformance. Andrew Behar, CEO of As You Sow, stated that these votes signal a rejection of attempts to inject political culture wars into standard business practices, reinforcing the business rationale for diverse workforces.

title: Costco announces 9 new stores opening in 2025, starting with 6 in March
summary: Costco plans to open nine new warehouse stores globally in 2025, with six locations in the U.S. slated to open by March. These new U.S. stores will be located in California, Texas, Michigan, and Massachusetts, and additional international expansion is planned for Japan and Australia. Costco CEO Ron Vachris also reported strong January sales, with net sales increasing by 9.2% from the previous year.

title: Apple and John Deere reject anti-DEI proposals amid corporate walkbacks
summary: Apple and John Deere shareholders have voted against anti-DEI proposals, contrasting with other companies that are dismantling or softening their diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts amidst a changing political and legal landscape. A recent executive order and Department of Justice memo signal federal opposition to DEI programs, prompting many brands like Bank of America, Google, and Disney to walk back their initiatives. However, some companies like e.l.f. and Patagonia are reaffirming their DEI commitments, while those that have scaled back, like Target, have faced public criticism and boycotts.

title: After Earnings, Is Walmart Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $58 per share for Walmart (WMT) and rates it as significantly overvalued following its fiscal first-quarter earnings report. Despite strong performance in key metrics like comparable sales and high-margin profit streams, underwhelming fiscal 2026 guidance led to a stock sell-off. Morningstar believes Walmart possesses a wide economic moat due to its brand, cost advantage, and extensive physical footprint, but faces risks from e-commerce competition.

title: Blink Charging Remains Bullish on the EV Supply Equipment Sector
summary: Despite potential changes in government policy regarding electric vehicles, Blink Charging expressed optimism about the continued growth of the EV supply equipment sector. The company's officials noted that state and local efforts, combined with increasing private investment and consumer demand for affordable EV models, are expected to sustain momentum. They also highlighted the increasing use of polycarbonate in charging station enclosures due to its performance benefits over traditional metal.

title: Pardon the Disruption: Where does Kroger go from here?
summary: Rodney McMullen's unexpected resignation as Kroger CEO leaves the supermarket giant facing significant challenges, including stiff competition from discounters, an uncertain omnichannel strategy, and the failed Albertsons merger. The new CEO will need to innovate and revitalize Kroger's core grocery business, digital presence, and explore further acquisitions to maintain relevance in a rapidly evolving market. Despite its strengths in private label and alternative profit streams, Kroger must adapt to customer demands and differentiate itself beyond traditional supermarket advantages.

title: Walmart Launched a Video Game. Are Shoppers Sold on It?
summary: Walmart has launched "Walmart Unlimited," a gamified miniseries developed with Unity and Spatial, marking its expansion into gamified shopping after a successful Roblox e-commerce channel. The series features three young characters on quests, integrating real Walmart supplier products into each episode. This initiative builds on Walmart's existing collaborations with Unity, aiming to empower developers to integrate Walmart's commerce APIs into games and apps, allowing users to purchase physical products without leaving the virtual environment.

title: The company that commissioned Wall Street's 'Fearless Girl' statue radically adjusts diversity policies for its index funds
summary: State Street, known for commissioning the "Fearless Girl" statue, has reversed its diversity policies for companies in its index funds. Previously requiring 30% female board representation, the company now encourages boards to determine their own composition with diverse experiences and perspectives. This move, which also drops requirements for DEI goals and disclosure of gender/racial board makeup, aligns with a broader trend of companies walking back DEI programs.

title: Albertsons CEO to step down after Kroger merger fails. What he says about grocer’s future
summary: Albertsons CEO Vivek Sankaran is set to retire on May 1st after the failed merger attempt with Kroger. He will be succeeded by Susan Morris, current executive vice president and chief operations officer.
